source.extraction: python-docx body-order extraction; section-aligned bilingual content

title.zh: 第一章：什么是六西格玛？

en.text: Six Sigma, or 6σ, is both a methodology for process improvement and a statistical concept that seeks to define the variation inherent in any process. The overarching premise of Six Sigma is that variation in a process leads to opportunities for error; opportunities for error then lead to risks for product defects. Product defects—whether in a tangible process or a service—lead to poor customer satisfaction. By working to reduce variation and opportunities for error, the Six Sigma method ultimately reduces process costs and increases customer satisfaction.

zh.text: 六西格玛（Six Sigma，或 6σ）既是一套流程改进方法，也是一种用于描述流程固有变异的统计概念。六西格玛的基本前提是：流程中的变异会带来出错机会；出错机会会进一步带来产品或服务缺陷的风险；缺陷最终会损害客户满意度。通过减少变异和出错机会，六西格玛方法最终能够降低流程成本并提升客户满意度。

rows: 术语说明 Six Sigma / 6σ：既指一套流程改进方法，也指一种统计质量目标；核心是用数据减少变异、缺陷和返工。
zh.text: 术语说明 Six Sigma / 6σ：既指一套流程改进方法，也指一种统计质量目标；核心是用数据减少变异、缺陷和返工。

title.zh: 数据驱动的流程与决策

en.text: In applying Six Sigma, organizations, teams, and project managers seek to implement strategies that are based on measurement and metrics. Historically, many business leaders made decisions based on intuition or experience. Despite some common beliefs in various industries, Six Sigma doesn’t remove the need for experienced leadership, and it doesn’t negate the importance of intuition in any process. Instead, Six Sigma works alongside other skills, experience, and knowledge to provide a mathematical and statistical foundation for decision making. Experience might say a process isn’t working; statistics prove that to be true. Intuition might guide a project manager to believe a certain change could improve output; Six Sigma tools help organizations validate those assumptions.

zh.text: 在应用六西格玛时，组织、团队和项目经理会努力采用基于测量和指标的策略。过去，许多企业领导者依靠直觉或经验做决策。六西格玛并不是要否定经验型领导，也不是要排斥流程中的直觉判断；相反，它让技能、经验和知识获得数学与统计基础。经验可能告诉我们某个流程运转不佳，统计数据则能证明这一点；直觉可能让项目经理认为某项改变能提升产出，六西格玛工具则帮助组织验证这些假设。

title.zh: 没有六西格玛时的决策

en.text: Without proper measurement and analysis, decision making processes in an organization might proceed as follows:
Someone with clout in the organization has a good idea or takes interest in someone else’s idea.
Based on past experience or knowledge, decision makers within an organization believe the idea will be successful.
The idea is implemented; sometimes it is implemented in beta mode so expenses and risks are minimized.
The success of the idea is weighed after implementation; problems are addressed after they impact products or processes in some way in the present or the future.

Beta testing is sometimes used in a Six Sigma approach, but the idea or change in question goes through rigorous analysis and data testing first. The disadvantage of launching ideas into beta—or to an entire population--without going through a Six Sigma methodology is that organizations can experience unintended consequences from changes, spend money on ideas that don’t end up working out as planned, and impact customer perceptions through trial-and-error periods rife with opportunities for error. In many cases, organizations that don’t rely on data make improvements without first understanding the true gain or loss associated with the change. Some improvements may appear to work on the surface without actually impacting customer satisfaction or profit in a positive way.

zh.text: 如果缺少适当的测量和分析，组织内的决策过程可能会变成下面这样：

zh.alt: 缺少测量与分析时的决策流程图

zh.text: 组织中有影响力的人提出一个好点子，或对别人的点子产生兴趣。
决策者基于过往经验或知识，相信这个点子会成功。
点子被付诸实施；有时会以 Beta 测试形式上线，以尽量降低费用和风险。
实施后才评估成败；问题通常要等到已经影响当前或未来的产品、服务或流程后才被处理。

rows: 术语说明 Beta testing（Beta 测试）：在相对受控的环境中，让选定人群或流程先试用新想法、系统或产品；发现并修正潜在问题后，再推广到更大范围。
zh.text: 术语说明 Beta testing（Beta 测试）：在相对受控的环境中，让选定人群或流程先试用新想法、系统或产品；发现并修正潜在问题后，再推广到更大范围。
Beta 测试有时也会被纳入六西格玛方法，但相关想法或变更必须先经过严谨的分析和数据检验。如果不经过六西格玛方法，就直接把想法推入 Beta 测试甚至全面推广，组织可能会遭遇意料之外的后果：把资金花在最终无法按计划奏效的方案上，或在充满出错机会的试错期中损害客户感知。许多不依赖数据的组织会在尚未理解真实收益或损失之前就开始改进。有些改进表面看似有效，却未必真正提升客户满意度或利润。

title.zh: 使用六西格玛时的决策

en.text: The Six Sigma method lets organizations identify problems, validate assumptions, brainstorm solutions, and plan for implementation to avoid unintended consequences. By applying tools such as statistical analysis and process mapping to problems and solutions, teams can visualize and predict outcomes with a high-level of accuracy, letting leadership make decisions with less financial risk.

Six Sigma methods don’t offer a crystal ball for organizations, though. Even with expert use of the tools described in this book, problems can arise for teams as they implement and maintain solutions. That’s why Six Sigma also provides for control methods: once teams implement changes, they can control processes for a fraction of the cost of traditional quality methods by continuing the use of Six Sigma tools and statistics.

zh.text: 六西格玛方法使组织能够识别问题、验证假设、头脑风暴解决方案，并规划实施路径，从而避免意外后果。通过将统计分析、流程图等工具应用于问题与方案，团队可以更准确地可视化并预测结果，让管理层在较低财务风险下做出决策。
当然，六西格玛并不能给组织一颗“水晶球”。即使熟练使用本书介绍的工具，团队在实施和维持解决方案时仍可能遇到问题。因此，六西格玛还强调控制方法：一旦团队实施了变更，就要持续使用六西格玛工具和统计方法，以远低于传统质量方法的成本控制流程。

en.text: Six Sigma as a methodology for process improvement involves a vast library of tools and knowledge, which will be covered throughout this book. In this section, we’ll begin to define the statistical concept represented by 6σ.

At the most basic definition, 6σ is a statistical representation for what many experts call a “perfect” process. Technically, in a Six Sigma process, there are only 3.4 defects per million opportunities. In percentages, that means 99.99966 percent of the products from a Six Sigma process are without defect. At just one sigma level below—5σ, or 99.97 percent accuracy--processes experience 233 errors per million opportunities. In simpler terms, there are going to be many more unsatisfied customers.

zh.text: 作为流程改进方法，六西格玛包含大量工具和知识，本书后续会逐步展开。本节先从统计概念角度说明 6σ 的含义。
从最基本的定义看，6σ 是许多专家所说“近乎完美”流程的统计表示。严格来说，一个六西格玛流程每百万次机会中只有 3.4 个缺陷。换成百分比，即六西格玛流程产出的产品中有 99.99966% 没有缺陷。若低一个西格玛水平，即五西格玛，准确率约为 99.97%，流程每百万次机会会出现 233 个错误。简单说，这意味着会有多得多的不满意客户。

rows: 术语说明 Defect 与 Opportunity：Defect 是未满足客户或规格要求的缺陷；Opportunity 是一次可能发生缺陷的机会。六西格玛常用“每百万机会缺陷数”衡量质量。
zh.text: 术语说明 Defect 与 Opportunity：Defect 是未满足客户或规格要求的缺陷；Opportunity 是一次可能发生缺陷的机会。六西格玛常用“每百万机会缺陷数”衡量质量。

en.text: According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, air traffic controllers in the United States handle 28,537 commercial flights daily.1 In a year, that is approximately 10.416 million flights. Based on a Five Sigma air traffic control process, errors of some type occur in the process for handling approximately 2,426 flights every year. With a Six Sigma process, that risk drops to 35.41 errors.

The CDC reports that approximately 51.4 million surgeries are performed in the United States in a given year.2 Based on a 99.97 accuracy rate, doctors would make errors in 11,976 surgeries each year, or 230 surgeries a week. At Six Sigma, that drops to approximately 174 errors a year for the entire country, or
just over 3 errors each week. At Five Sigma, patients are 68 times more likely to experience an error at the hands of medical providers.

While most people accept a 99.9 percent accuracy rate in even the most critical services on a daily basis, the above examples highlight how wide the gap between Six Sigma and Five Sigma really is. For organizations, it’s not just about the error rate—it’s also about the costs associated with each error.

Consider an example based on Amazon shipments. On Cyber Monday in 2013, Amazon processed a whopping 36.8 million orders.3 Let’s assume that each order error costs the company an average of $35 (a very conservative number, considering that costs might include return shipping, labor to answer customer phone calls or emails, and labor and shipping to right a wrong order).
Cost of Amazon Order Errors, 5σ Total Orders Errors Average Cost per Error Total Cost of Errors 36.8 million 8,574.4 $35 $300,104.00
Cost of Amazon Order Errors, 6σ Total Orders Errors Average Cost per Error Total Cost of Errors 36.8 million 125.12 $35 $4,379.20
For this example, the cost difference in sigma levels is still over $295,000 for the Cyber Monday business.

For most organizations, Six Sigma processes are a constant target. Achieving and maintaining Six Sigma “perfection” is difficult and requires continuous process improvement. But even advancing from lower levels of sigma to a Four or Five Sigma process has a drastic impact on costs and customer satisfaction. Let’s look at the Amazon Cyber Monday example at other levels of sigma.

Sigma Level Defects per Million Opportunities Estimated Cyber Monday Defects Total Cost (at $35 estimate per error) One Sigma 690,000 25,392,000 $888,720,000 Two Sigma 308,000 11,334,400 $396,704,000 Three Sigma 66,800 2,458,240 $86,038,400 Four Sigma 6,200 228,160 $7,985,600 Five Sigma 233 8,574.4 $300,104 Six Sigma 3.4 125.12 $4,379
At very low levels of sigma, any process is unlikely to be profitable. The higher the sigma level, the better the bottom line is likely to be.

zh.text: 根据美国国家海洋和大气管理局的数据，美国空中交通管制员每天处理 28,537 架次商业航班，一年约 1,041.6 万架次。若空管流程处在五西格玛水平，处理流程中每年约有 2,426 架次航班会出现某类错误；如果达到六西格玛水平，这一风险会降至约 35.41 次。
美国疾病控制与预防中心报告显示，美国一年约进行 5,140 万台手术。若准确率为 99.97%，医生每年会在 11,976 台手术中出错，即每周约 230 台；达到六西格玛水平后，全国全年错误数会降至约 174 次，也就是每周略高于 3 次。在五西格玛水平下，患者遭遇医疗服务提供者错误的可能性是六西格玛水平的 68 倍。
多数人在日常关键服务中能够接受 99.9% 的准确率，但这些例子说明，六西格玛和五西格玛之间的差距非常大。对组织而言，这不仅是错误率问题，还关系到每一次错误背后的成本。
以亚马逊发货为例。2013 年网络星期一，亚马逊处理了高达 3,680 万份订单。假设每个订单错误给公司造成 35 美元的平均成本（这是非常保守的估计，因为成本可能包括退货运费、客服接听电话或邮件的人力，以及纠正错误订单所需的人力和运输费用）。
亚马逊订单错误成本，5σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，5σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，5σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，5σ 订单总数 错误数 每个错误平均成本 错误总成本 36.8 million 8574.4 $35 $300,104.00
亚马逊订单错误成本，6σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，6σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，6σ 亚马逊订单错误成本，6σ 订单总数 错误数 每个错误平均成本 错误总成本 36.8 million 125.12 $35 $4,379.20
在这个例子中，仅网络星期一业务，不同西格玛水平造成的成本差异就超过 295,000 美元。
对多数组织来说，六西格玛流程是一个持续追求的目标。达到并维持六西格玛“完美”很困难，需要持续流程改进。但即使只是把较低西格玛水平提升到四西格玛或五西格玛，也会显著影响成本和客户满意度。下表继续沿用亚马逊网络星期一示例，比较不同西格玛水平下的结果。

rows: 术语说明 DPMO：Defects Per Million Opportunities，指每百万次机会中的缺陷数；数值越低，流程质量越高。

en.text: Organizations and teams can calculate the sigma level of a product or process using the equation below:

Consider a process in a marketing department that distributes letters to customers or prospects. For the purposes of the example, imagine that the process inserts 30,000 letters in preaddressed envelopes each day. In a given business week, the process outputs 150,000 letters.

The marketing department begins receiving complaints that people are receiving letters in envelopes that are addressed to them, but the letters inside are addressed to or relevant to someone else. The marketing department randomly selects 1,000 letters from the next week’s batch and finds that 5 of them have errors. Applying that to the total amount, they estimate that as many as 750 letters could have errors. (Sampling and extrapolation are covered in depth in the advanced chapters on statistics.)
The letter process has 150,000 opportunities for error each week and an estimated 750 defects.
Look up a yield of 99.5 in the abridged Sigma table below and you’ll see the process described above is currently between 4 and 4.1 sigma.

title.en: Sigma Level Is Not a Final Indicator
title.zh: 西格玛水平不是最终指标

en.text: Sigma levels provide organization with a high-level look at how a process is performing, but comparing sigma levels between multiple processes doesn’t always point to the particular process an organization
should improve first. Leadership should also consider costs, resources, and the estimated impact of improvements.
For example, consider these processes that might be found in a food processing plant:

rows: Attaching a decorative element to food item
Decorative touch is centered on food product and stable so it won't fall off in transit
Product reaches the right customer in a timely manner
en.text: Process Performance Metric(s) Current Sigma Level Attaching a decorative element to food item Decorative touch is centered on food product and stable so it won't fall off in transit 2.2 Packing product Product is sealed for freshness 3.1 Shipping of product Product reaches the right customer in a timely manner 4.3

A glance at sigma levels indicates that the process that attaches the decorative element is in most need of improvement. While that process has the highest rate of defects, leadership within the plant would have to ask themselves: How much does that matter to the customer, and what is the hit to the bottom line?

It’s likely that most customers will notice most that the product is sealed for freshness and reaches the right location. Since bad product has to be thrown away, the most expensive errors might be associated with improper sealing during packing. The plant is likely to use resources to improve the packing process before addressing the decorative element issue.

After the packing process is improved, the plant might then consider whether to improve the decorating process or the shipping process. As part of that consideration, the company might conduct customer surveys to reveal that some customers have stopped buying the product because of the decorative element issue. An analyst estimates that the loss of sales related to that issue are costing the company $1,000 a week. Shipping issues are costing the company $500 a week.

Should the company address the costlier issue first? What if you were told that the shipping process could be improved with staff training sessions, while the decorative element issue required an expensive machinery update? Sometimes, organizations have to consider the expense of an improvement. Applying a Six Sigma project to all situations isn’t financially lucrative since those improvements take time and money. A Six Sigma culture is about continuous improvement, which means teams consider all options before embarking on the most lucrative improvement measures.

zh.text: 西格玛水平能让组织从高层次了解流程表现，但不同流程之间仅比较西格玛水平，并不总能指出最应该优先改进的流程。领导层还应考虑成本、资源以及改进的预期影响。
例如，在一家食品加工厂中，可能存在以下流程：

rows: 装饰位于食品中央且稳定，运输过程中不会脱落
产品及时送达正确客户
zh.text: 流程 绩效指标 当前西格玛水平 给食品添加装饰元素 装饰位于食品中央且稳定，运输过程中不会脱落 2.2 产品包装 产品密封以保持新鲜 3.1 产品运输 产品及时送达正确客户 4.3
只看西格玛水平，添加装饰元素的流程最需要改进，因为它缺陷率最高。但工厂领导还要问：这对客户有多重要？它对利润底线的影响有多大？
多数客户可能更在意产品是否密封保鲜、是否送达正确地点。由于变质产品必须丢弃，最昂贵的错误很可能来自包装密封不当。因此，工厂可能先把资源投入包装流程，而不是装饰元素流程。
包装流程改进后，工厂再考虑是否改进装饰流程或运输流程。若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。此时是否一定先处理成本更高的问题？如果运输流程只需员工培训即可改善，而装饰问题需要昂贵设备升级呢？有时组织必须把改进成本纳入考虑。六西格玛文化强调持续改进，团队应在启动最有价值的改进措施前综合评估所有选择。

en.text: Organizations can impact their sigma level by integrating core principles from the Six Sigma methodology into leadership styles, process management, and improvement endeavors. The principles of Six Sigma, and the tools used to achieve them, are covered in detail in various sections of this book, but some common ideas are introduced below.

zh.text: 组织可以通过把六西格玛核心原则融入领导方式、流程管理和改进行动，影响自身的西格玛水平。六西格玛原则及相关工具将在本书各部分详细展开，下面先介绍几个常见思想。

en.text: In the illustration about the food plant, we saw that the Six Sigma process doesn’t just make improvements for the sake of driving up sigma levels. A primary principle of the methodology is a focus on the customer. In Chapter 5, we’ll look at the Voice of the Customer (VoC) and ways for establishing what the customer really wants from a product or process. By combining that knowledge with measurements, statistics, and process improvement methods, organizations increase customer satisfaction, ultimately bolstering profits, customer retention, and loyalty.
A detailed understanding of the customer and customer desires not only lets businesses customize product offerings and services, but it also lets organizations:
Offer additional features customers want and are willing to pay for
Prioritize product development to meet current needs
Develop new ideas based on customer feedback
Understand changing trends in the market
Identify areas of concern
Prioritize work on challenges based on how customers perceive various problems or issues
Test solutions and ideas before investing time and money in them

zh.text: 从食品工厂的例子可以看到，六西格玛流程并不是为了提高西格玛水平而盲目改进。该方法的首要原则之一是关注客户。第 5 章会介绍客户之声（Voice of the Customer，VoC），以及如何确定客户真正希望从产品或流程中获得什么。将客户理解与测量、统计和流程改进方法结合起来，组织可以提升客户满意度，并最终增强利润、客户留存和忠诚度。
深入理解客户及其需求，不仅能帮助企业定制产品和服务，还能帮助组织：
提供客户想要且愿意付费的附加功能。
根据当前需求确定产品开发优先级。
基于客户反馈发展新想法。
理解市场趋势变化。
识别需要关注的领域。
根据客户对不同问题的感知，确定挑战处理优先级。
在投入时间和资金前测试解决方案与想法。

rows: 术语说明 VOC：Voice of the Customer，客户之声；指客户需求、抱怨、期望和偏好的系统化输入。
zh.text: 术语说明 VOC：Voice of the Customer，客户之声；指客户需求、抱怨、期望和偏好的系统化输入。

en.text: The value stream is the sequence of all items, events, and people required to produce an end result. For example, the value stream for serving a hotdog with ketchup to someone would include:
A hotdog supplier
A bun supplier
A ketchup supplier
Hotdogs
Buns
Ketchup
A cooking procedure for the hotdog
A pot
Tongs
Someone to do the cooking
A plate
Someone to put the hotdog into the bun
Someone to put the ketchup on the hotdog
Someone to put the completed hotdog onto a plate
Someone to serve the hotdog to another
If you combine all of the above processes into a pictorial representation of exactly how these elements become the served hotdog, then you have a value stream map.

The purpose for determining a value stream for a process is that you can identify areas of concern, waste, and improvement. In the above process, are there four different people putting the hotdog together and serving it, or is one person doing all four of those tasks? Is the supplier a single grocery store, or are you shopping for items at various stores and why? Do you get savings benefits to offset the
added time spent working with multiple suppliers? These are some examples of the questions you can reveal and answer during value stream mapping.

zh.text: 价值流是为了产生最终结果而需要的所有事项、事件和人员的序列。例如，为某人提供一个加番茄酱的热狗，其价值流可能包括：
热狗供应商、面包供应商、番茄酱供应商。
热狗、面包、番茄酱，以及烹制热狗的程序。
锅、夹子、负责烹制的人、盘子。
把热狗放入面包的人、添加番茄酱的人、装盘的人、把热狗端给顾客的人。

如果把上述所有过程用图形准确表示出来，说明这些要素如何变成最终端出的热狗，就形成了价值流图。确定流程价值流的目的，是识别关注点、浪费和改进机会。在上述流程中，是否有四个人分别完成夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘和端送？若是，产品在四个人之间转手是否增加了时间？是否由一个人完成会更快？供应商是否是一家杂货店，还是从多家商店采购，原因是什么？多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？这些都是价值流图能帮助揭示并回答的问题。

rows: 术语说明 Value Stream：从需求到交付结果的完整活动链，包含增值活动和非增值活动；用于识别浪费和改进机会。
zh.text: 术语说明 Value Stream：从需求到交付结果的完整活动链，包含增值活动和非增值活动；用于识别浪费和改进机会。

en.text: Inherent in the Six Sigma method is continuous process improvement. An organization that completely adopts a Six Sigma methodology never stops improving. It identifies and prioritizes areas of opportunity on a continuous basis. Once one area is improved upon, the organization moves on to improving another area. If a process is improved from 4 Sigma to 4.4 Sigma, the organization considers ways to move the sigma level up further. The goal is to move ever closer to the “perfect” level of 99.99966 accuracy for all processes within an organization while maintaining other goals and requirements, such as financial stability, as quickly as possible.

zh.text: 持续流程改进是六西格玛方法的内在要求。真正采用六西格玛方法的组织不会停止改进，而会持续识别并优先处理机会领域。一个领域改进后，组织会继续改进另一个领域。如果某流程从 4 西格玛提升到 4.4 西格玛，组织还会继续寻找进一步提升的方法。目标是在尽快满足财务稳定等其他要求的同时，使组织内所有流程逐步接近 99.99966% 准确率的“近乎完美”水平。

en.text: One of the ways to continuously improve a process is to reduce the variation in the process. Every process contains inherent variation: in a call center with 20 employees, variation will exist in each phone call even if the calls are scripted. Inflection, accents, environmental concerns, and caller moods are just some things that lead to variation in this circumstance. By providing employees with a script or suggested comments for common scenarios, the call center reduces variation to some degree.

Consider another example: A pizzeria. The employees are instructed to use certain amounts of ingredients for each size of pizza. A small gets one cup of cheese; a large gets two cups. The pizzeria owner notes a great deal of variation in how much cheese is on each pizza, and he fears it will lead to inconsistent customer experiences. To reduce variation, he provides employees with two measuring cups: a 1-cup container for small pizzas and a 2-cup container for large pizzas.

The variation is reduced, but it is still present. Some employees pour cheese into the cups and some scoop it. Some fill the cups just to the rim; others let the cheese create a mound above the rim. The owner acts to reduce variation again: he trains all employees to fill the cup over the rim and use a flat spatula to scrape excess cheese off. While variation will still exist due to factors such as air pockets or how cheese settles in the cup, it is greatly reduced, and customers experience more consistent pizzas.

zh.text: 持续改进流程的一种方式是减少流程变异。每个流程都有固有变异：例如一个有 20 名员工的呼叫中心，即便所有电话都有脚本，不同电话之间仍会因为语调、口音、环境和来电者情绪而产生差异。通过为员工提供脚本或常见场景建议话术，呼叫中心可以在一定程度上减少变异。
再看一家披萨店。员工被要求按披萨尺寸使用固定配料量：小披萨一杯奶酪，大披萨两杯奶酪。店主发现每个披萨上的奶酪量差异很大，担心客户体验不一致。为减少变异，他给员工提供两个量杯：小披萨用一杯量杯，大披萨用两杯量杯。
变异降低了，但并未消失。有的员工把奶酪倒入量杯，有的用勺舀；有人只装到杯口，有人让奶酪高出杯口形成小堆。店主再次减少变异：培训所有员工把奶酪装到超过杯口，然后用平刮刀刮去多余奶酪。虽然空气间隙或奶酪沉降方式仍会造成变异，但整体变异大幅减少，客户得到的披萨也更一致。

rows: 术语说明 Variation：流程输出的波动程度。减少不必要的变异，是稳定质量和提升客户体验的前提。
zh.text: 术语说明 Variation：流程输出的波动程度。减少不必要的变异，是稳定质量和提升客户体验的前提。

en.text: Remember the hotdog example for value streams? We asked the question: do four different people act to place the hotdog in the bun, put the ketchup on the hotdog, plate the hotdog, and serve it? If so, does the process take more time because the product has to be transferred between four people? Would it be faster to have one person perform all those actions? If so, then we’ve identified some waste in the process—in this case, waste of conveyance.

Removing waste—items, actions, or people that are unnecessary to the outcome of a process—reduces processing time, opportunities for errors, and overall costs. While waste is a major concern in the Six Sigma methodology, the concept of waste comes from a methodology known as Lean Process Management..

zh.text: 还记得热狗价值流的例子吗？如果夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘、端送分别由四个人完成，流程是否因为产品要在四个人之间传递而耗时更长？如果一个人能完成所有动作，是否会更快？若答案是肯定的，我们就识别出流程中的一种浪费，在这个例子里是搬运浪费。
消除浪费，即去除对流程结果并非必要的事项、动作或人员，可以减少处理时间、出错机会和总体成本。虽然浪费是六西格玛方法中的重要关注点，但“浪费”这一概念来自精益流程管理。

rows: 术语说明 Waste / Lean：Waste 是消耗资源但不为客户增加价值的活动；Lean 强调识别并消除浪费，使流程更快、更顺、更少返工。
zh.text: 术语说明 Waste / Lean：Waste 是消耗资源但不为客户增加价值的活动；Lean 强调识别并消除浪费，使流程更快、更顺、更少返工。

en.text: Implementing improved processes is a temporary measure unless organizations equip their employees working with processes to monitor and maintain improvements. In most organizations, process improvement includes a two-pronged approach. First, a process improvement team comprised of

project management, methodology experts, and subject-matter experts define, plan, and implement an improvement. That team then equips the employees who work directly with the process daily to control and manage the process in its improved state.

zh.text: 如果组织没有让直接参与流程的员工掌握监控和维持改进的方法，改进流程只能是暂时措施。多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；随后，该团队赋能每天直接处理流程的员工，使他们能够在改进后的状态下控制和管理流程。

en.text: Often, Six Sigma improvements address processes that are out of control. Out of control processes meet specific statistical requirements. The goal of improvement is to bring a process back within a state of statistical control. Then, after improvements are implemented, measurements, statistics, and other Six Sigma tools are used to ensure the process remains in control. Part of any continuous improvement process is ensuring such controls are put in place and that the employees who are hands-on with the process on a regular basis know how to use the controls.

zh.text: 六西格玛改进通常针对失控流程。所谓失控流程，是指满足特定统计条件、表现出不受控状态的流程。改进目标是让流程回到统计受控状态。改进实施后，组织继续使用测量、统计和其他六西格玛工具，确保流程保持受控。任何持续改进流程的一部分，都是建立这些控制，并确保经常接触流程的一线员工知道如何使用这些控制。

rows: 术语说明 Control：控制不是事后检查，而是通过指标、规则和反馈机制，让改进后的流程持续保持稳定。
zh.text: 术语说明 Control：控制不是事后检查，而是通过指标、规则和反馈机制，让改进后的流程持续保持稳定。

en.text: Six Sigma is not without its own challenges. As an expansive method that requires commitment to continuous improvement, Six Sigma is often viewed as an expensive or unnecessary process, especially for small or mid-sized organizations. Leadership at Ideal Aerosmith, a manufacturing and engineering company in Minnesota, was skeptical of Six Sigma ideas and the costs associated with implementing them. Despite reservations, the company waded into Six Sigma implementations, eventually seeing worthwhile results after only 18 months. Those results included a production improvement of 25 percent, a 5 percent improvement in profits within the first year, and a 30 percent improvement in timely deliverables.4

Some obstacles and challenges that often stand in the way of positive results from Six Sigma include lack of support, resources, or knowledge, poor execution of projects, inconsistent access to valid statistical data, and concerns about using the methodology in new industries.

zh.text: 六西格玛也有自身挑战。作为一种范围广、需要持续改进承诺的方法，六西格玛常被视为昂贵或不必要的流程，尤其对中小型组织而言更是如此。位于明尼苏达州的制造和工程公司 Ideal Aerosmith 的领导层曾对六西格玛理念及实施成本持怀疑态度。尽管有所保留，该公司仍开始实施六西格玛，并在 18 个月后看到有价值的成果，包括产量提升 25%、第一年利润提升 5%、按时交付提升 30%。
阻碍六西格玛取得积极成果的常见障碍包括：缺乏支持、资源或知识；项目执行不佳；无法持续获得有效统计数据；以及对在新行业中使用该方法的顾虑。

en.text: Six Sigma requires support and buy-in at all levels of an organization. Leaders and executives must be willing to back initiatives with resources—financial and labor related. Subject-matter experts must be open to sharing information about their processes with project teams, and employees at all levels must embrace the idea of change and improvement and participate in training. Common barriers to support include:
Leaders that are unfamiliar with or don’t understand the Six Sigma process
Leaders willing to pursue improvements initially but who lose interest in overseeing and championing projects before they are completed
Staff that is fearful of change, especially in an environment when change has historically caused negative consequences for employees
Employees who are resistant to change because they believe improvements might make them obsolete, drastically change their jobs, or make their jobs harder
Department heads or employees who constantly champion their own processes and needs and are unwilling to enter into big-picture thinking

zh.text: 六西格玛需要组织各层级的支持和认同。领导者和高管必须愿意以资金和人力资源支持改进行动；主题专家应愿意向项目团队分享流程信息；各层级员工也需要接受变化和改进理念，并参与培训。常见支持障碍包括：
领导者不熟悉或不了解六西格玛流程。
领导者起初愿意推动改进，但在项目完成前失去监督和倡导兴趣。
员工害怕改变，尤其是在历史上改变曾给员工带来负面后果的环境中。
员工抵触改变，因为担心改进会让自己被替代、显著改变工作，或让工作更难。
部门负责人或员工持续维护本部门流程和需求，不愿从整体视角思考。

en.text: Lack of resources can be a challenge to Six Sigma initiatives, but they don’t have to be a barrier. Lack of knowledge about how to use and implement Six Sigma is one of the first issues small- and mid-sized companies face. Smaller businesses can’t always afford to hire dedicated resources to handle continuous process improvement, but the availability of resources and Six Sigma training makes it increasingly possible for organizations to use some of the tools without an expert or to send in-house staff to be certified in Six Sigma.

zh.text: 缺乏资源可能是六西格玛项目的挑战，但并不一定构成障碍。中小企业首先面临的问题之一，是缺乏使用和实施六西格玛的知识。小企业并不总能聘请专职人员处理持续流程改进，但随着培训资源和六西格玛课程更容易获得，组织越来越可以在没有专家的情况下使用部分工具，或派内部员工取得六西格玛认证。

en.text: Companies implementing Six Sigma for the first time, especially in a project environment, often turn away from the entire methodology if the first project or improvement falls flat. Proponents of Six Sigma within any organization really have to hit it out of the ballpark with the first project if leadership and others are on the fence about the methodology. Teams can help avoid poor project performance by taking extreme care to execute every phase of the project correctly. By choosing low-risk, high-reward improvements, teams can also stack the deck in their favor with first-time projects. The only disadvantage with such a tactic is that it can be hard to duplicate the wow factor with subsequent improvements, making it important to remember that long-term implementation and commitment is vital in Six Sigma.

zh.text: 首次实施六西格玛的公司，尤其是在项目制环境中，如果第一个项目或改进效果不佳，往往会转而放弃整个方法。若领导层和其他相关人员仍在观望，组织内的六西格玛推动者必须让第一个项目取得足够有说服力的成果。团队可以通过谨慎、正确地执行项目每个阶段来避免绩效不佳；也可以选择低风险、高回报的改进，为首个项目创造有利条件。这种策略的不足在于，后续改进未必总能复制第一次的惊艳效果，因此长期实施和持续承诺对六西格玛至关重要。

en.text: Data and analytics issues are a common challenge for organizations of all sizes. Gaining access to consistent and accurate data streams—and applying statistical analysis to that data in an appropriate manner—is difficult. Some data-related challenges include:
Discovering that an important process metric is not being captured
The use of manual data processes in many processes
Automated data processes that capture enormous amounts and create scope challenges
Data that is skewed due to assumptions, human interaction in the process, or incorrect capture
Lengthy times between raw data capture and access
Industry or company compliance rules that make it difficult to gain access to necessary data

zh.text: 数据和分析问题是各种规模组织共同面对的挑战。获得一致、准确的数据流，并以适当方式对数据进行统计分析并不容易。常见数据挑战包括：
发现重要流程指标没有被采集。
许多流程仍依赖手工数据处理。
自动化数据流程捕获了海量数据，反而带来范围界定挑战。
数据因假设、人为交互或采集错误而产生偏差。
从原始数据采集到可访问之间耗时过长。
行业或公司合规规则使获取必要数据变得困难。

title.en: Concerns about Using Six Sigma in a Specific Industry
title.zh: 对特定行业使用六西格玛的顾虑

en.text: Six Sigma originated in the manufacturing industry and many of the concepts and tools of the methodology are still taught in the context of a factory or industrial environment. Because of this, organizations often discount the methods or believe they will be too difficult to implement in other industries. In reality, Six Sigma can be customized to any industry.

zh.text: 六西格玛起源于制造业，许多概念和工具至今仍在工厂或工业环境语境下教授。因此，组织常常低估这些方法，或认为它们很难在其他行业实施。事实上，六西格玛可以针对任何行业进行定制。

title.en: History and Application of Six Sigma
title.zh: 六西格玛的历史与应用

en.text: While the roots of Six Sigma are commonly attributed to companies such as Toyota and Motorola, the methodology is actually grounded in concepts that date as far back as the 19th century. Before delving into the history of Six Sigma, it’s important to understand the difference between traditional quality programs, such as Total Quality Management, and continuous process improvement methods, such as Six Sigma.

Most modern quality and improvement programs can be traced back to the same roots. Both quality programs and continuous process improvement methods look to achieve goals such as reducing errors and defects, making processes more efficient, improving customer satisfaction, and boosting profits. But quality programs are concerned with achieving a specific goal. The program either runs forever, constantly working toward the same goal, or it achieves the end goal and must be reset for a new goal.

Six Sigma seeks to instill a culture of continuous improvement and quality that optimizes performance of an organization from the inside out. It’s the cultural element inherent in Six Sigma that lets organizations enact both small and sweeping improvements that drastically impact efficiencies and costs. Six Sigma does work toward individual goals with regard to each project, but the projects are part of the overall culture of improvement that, in practice, is never done. Six Sigma creates safeguards and tactics so that, even after a project is considered complete, controls are in place to ensure progress continues and it is impossible to revert to old ways.

zh.text: 虽然六西格玛的根源通常归因于丰田和摩托罗拉等公司，但该方法实际上植根于可以追溯到 19 世纪的概念。在深入研究六西格玛的历史之前，了解传统质量计划（如全面质量管理）和持续过程改进方法（如六西格玛）之间的区别非常重要。

rows: 术语说明 TQM（全面质量管理）：以全员参与和持续改进为核心的质量管理思想。
zh.text: 术语说明 TQM（全面质量管理）：以全员参与和持续改进为核心的质量管理思想。
大多数现代质量和改进计划都可以追溯到相同的根源。质量计划和持续流程改进方法都旨在实现减少错误和缺陷、提高流程效率、提高客户满意度和提高利润等目标。但质量计划关注的是实现特定目标。该程序要么永远运行，不断地朝着同一个目标努力，要么实现了最终目标，并且必须为新目标重新设置。
六西格玛致力于灌输一种持续改进和质量的文化，从内到外优化组织的绩效。六西格玛固有的文化元素使组织能够实施小规模和全面的改进，从而极大地影响效率和成本。 六西格玛确实致力于每个项目的个人目标，但这些项目是整体改进文化的一部分，而在实践中，这种改进永远不会完成。 六西格玛制定了保障措施和策略，以便即使在项目被认为完成后，也可以采取控制措施以确保进展继续进行，并且不可能回到旧的方式。
统计过程控制的发展

title.en: The Development of Statistical Process Control

en.text: Six Sigma applies statistics to define, measure, analyze, verify, and control processes. In fact, Six Sigma teams usually use methodologies known as DMAIC or DMADV to accomplish improvements and develop controls for processes. DMAIC stands for Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control. These are the five phases of a Six Sigma project to improve a process that already exists. When developing a new process, teams use DMADV, which stands for Define, Measure, Analyze, Design, and Verify. Both methods are discussed in Chapter 11, and Unit 3 provides in-depth information about each phase of DMAIC.

The roots of statistical process control, which provide a backbone for Six Sigma methods, began with the development of the normal curve by Carl Friedrich Gauss in the 19th century. We know today that the normal curve is just one of several possible probability distribution models. It is perhaps the most widely used model, and the other models developed from the normal curve. Probability distribution models are discussed in later chapters on statistics

In the early part of the 20th century, statistical process control received another big boost thanks to contributions from an engineer and scholar named Walter Shewhart. Shewhart's contributions to quality are many, but two specific ideas stand out. First, Shewhart was the first person

to closely relate sigma level and quality. He defined a process in need of correction as one that is performing at three sigma. If you look back to Chapter 1 and the theoretical Amazon example, the cost difference between four sigma and three sigma is over $78 million; in comparison, the difference between five and four sigma is only approximately $7.6 million. Because errors and costs exponentially increase as sigma level decreases, Shewhart’s definition has very practical applications in business. While Six Sigma as a method seeks to move ever toward less than 3.4 defects per million opportunities (dpmo), it is also true that if the quality of a process decreases, as it approaches three sigma, the costs associated with errors increase substantially.

Second, Shewhart is considered the father of control charts. Control charts, which are covered in depth in the chapters on advanced statistics, are a critical component of statistical process control that lets organizations maintain improved performance after a Six Sigma initiative. At a time when scholars were writing about the theoretical application of statistics in a growing number of fields, Shewhart developed ways to apply these concepts to manufacturing and industrial processes specifically.

During the same time period, W. Edwards Deming was working for the U.S. Department of Agriculture. A physicist and mathematician, Deming was in charge of teaching courses at the agency’s graduate school and he arranged for Shewhart to come and speak there. Later, Deming brought Shewhart's statistical concepts to the United States Census Bureau, applying his theories outside of an industrial or manufacturing environment for possibly the first time.

One of Deming’s ideas is called the PDCA cycle, or plan-do-check-act cycle. The idea is that improvement comes when you recognize there is a need for change and make a plan to create improvement. Next, you do something by testing your ideas. Using the results of the test, you check or verify that your improvements are working. Then you act, bringing your improvements to a production environment or scaling improvements outside of the test environment. The fact that PDCA is a cycle means it never ends; there are always improvements to be made. This is a core tenet of Six Sigma.

Following World War II, Deming worked in Japan on behalf of the United States government in several capacities. While in post-war Japan, Deming befriended statisticians and convinced at least one notable engineer that statistical process control was relevant to Japan's need to drastically drive economic and production performance to overcome damage from the war. In the end, Deming became a valued teacher and consultant to manufacturing companies in Japan, planting the ideas and concepts that would soon become the Toyota Production System, or Lean Six Sigma.

rows: 术语说明 SPC（统计过程控制）：用统计方法监控过程表现，区分普通波动和异常信号。
zh.text: 术语说明 SPC（统计过程控制）：用统计方法监控过程表现，区分普通波动和异常信号。

六西格玛应用统计学来定义、测量、分析、验证和控制流程。事实上，六西格玛团队通常使用称为 DMAIC 或 DMADV 的方法来完成改进并开发流程控制。 DMAIC 代表定义、测量、分析、改进和控制。这是六西格玛项目的五个阶段，旨在改进现有流程。在开发新流程时，团队使用 DMADV，它代表定义、测量、分析、设计和验证。第 11 章讨论了这两种方法，第 3 单元提供了有关 DMAIC 每个阶段的深入信息。

rows: 术语说明 DMAIC：定义、测量、分析、改进、控制；适用于改进已有流程。
zh.text: 术语说明 DMAIC：定义、测量、分析、改进、控制；适用于改进已有流程。

rows: 术语说明 DMADV：定义、测量、分析、设计、验证；常用于设计新流程或新产品。
zh.text: 术语说明 DMADV：定义、测量、分析、设计、验证；常用于设计新流程或新产品。
为六西格玛方法提供支柱的统计过程控制的根源始于卡尔·弗里德里希·高斯 (Carl Friedrich Gauss) 在 19 世纪对正态曲线的发展。 今天我们知道，正态曲线只是几种可能的概率分布模型之一。它可能是使用最广泛的模型，其他模型都是从正态曲线发展而来的。概率分布模型将在后面的统计章节中讨论
20 世纪初，由于工程师兼学者沃尔特·休哈特 (Walter Shewhart) 的贡献，统计过程控制再次得到了巨大的推动。休哈特对质量的贡献很多，但有两个具体的想法脱颖而出。首先，休哈特是第一人

将西格玛水平和质量密切相关。他将需要修正的流程定义为正在三西格玛执行的流程。如果你回顾一下第一章和理论上的亚马逊例子，四西格玛和三西格玛之间的成本差异超过 7800 万美元；相比之下，五格玛和四西格玛之间的差距仅约为760万美元。由于随着西格玛水平的降低，错误和成本呈指数级增加，因此休哈特的定义在商业中具有非常实际的应用。虽然六西格玛作为一种方法力求朝着每百万机会缺陷数数数数 (DPMO) 低于 3.4 的目标迈进，但如果流程的质量随着接近三西格玛而下降，与错误相关的成本也会大幅增加，这也是事实。

rows: 术语说明 Sigma level（西格玛水平）：衡量过程缺陷率的尺度；水平越高，单位机会中产生缺陷的概率越低。
zh.text: 术语说明 Sigma level（西格玛水平）：衡量过程缺陷率的尺度；水平越高，单位机会中产生缺陷的概率越低。
其次，休哈特被认为是控制图之父。控制图在高级统计章节中进行了深入介绍，它是统计过程控制的重要组成部分，可以让组织在实施六西格玛计划后保持改进的绩效。当学者们在越来越多的领域撰写有关统计理论应用的文章时，休哈特开发了将这些概念专门应用于制造和工业过程的方法。

rows: 术语说明 Control Chart（控制图）：用时间序列和控制界限判断过程是否处于受控状态。
zh.text: 术语说明 Control Chart（控制图）：用时间序列和控制界限判断过程是否处于受控状态。
同一时期，爱德华兹·戴明在美国农业部工作。戴明是一位物理学家和数学家，负责该机构研究生院的课程教学，他安排休哈特到那里演讲。后来，戴明将休哈特的统计概念带到了美国人口普查局，这可能是第一次将他的理论应用到工业或制造环境之外。
戴明的想法之一被称为 PDCA 循环，或计划-执行-检查-行动循环。 这个想法是，当您认识到需要改变并制定改进计划时，就会出现改进。接下来，你通过测试你的想法来做一些事情。使用测试结果，您可以检查或验证您的改进是否有效。然后您采取行动，将您的改进引入生产环境或将改进扩展到测试环境之外。 PDCA 是一个循环，这意味着它永远不会结束；总有需要改进的地方。这是六西格玛的核心宗旨。
第二次世界大战后，戴明在日本代表美国政府担任多种职务。在战后的日本，戴明与统计学家成为了朋友，并说服了至少一位著名工程师，统计过程控制与日本需要大幅推动经济和生产绩效以克服战争造成的损害有关。最终，戴明成为日本制造公司的一位受人尊敬的老师和顾问，植入了很快成为丰田生产系统（Toyota Production System）或精益六西格玛的思想和概念。

title.en: Continuous Process Improvement: Toyota and Lean
title.zh: 持续流程改进：丰田和精益

en.text: Deming's teachings and the need for Japanese industry to make a successful comeback following a catastrophic war combined to bear fruit for Toyota. Toyota’s leadership had visited the concepts of quality prior to WWII, but improved performance and efficiency became a more critical goal given the nature of Japan's economy and resources in the 1940s and 50s. Taking manufacturing ideas attributed to Henry Ford, Toyota leaders applied statistics and new quality concepts to create a system they felt would increase production and allow for variable products while reducing costs and ensuring quality.

Several individuals were instrumental in the ultimate development of the Toyota Production System. They infused the process with automated machinery, quality controls to keep defects from occurring, and efficiency tools that had not yet been applied with such detail and consistency. One man, Kiichiro Toyoda, had previous factory experience. In his previous jobs, he added efficiencies to processes in textile mills through conveyor and other automated systems. Toyoda introduced the same concepts on certain lines in the Toyota manufacturing process. Later, Eiji Toyoda and Taiichi Ohno introduced concepts known as Just-in-Time and jidoka, which are the pillars of the Toyota Production System.
The principles driving Toyota's system, and later, the foundation of Lean Process Management or Lean Six Sigma, include:
Defining customer values
Identifying the value stream for customer needs and desires
Identifying waste in the process
Creation of a continuous process flow
Continually working to reduce the number of steps and time it takes to reach customer satisfaction
Lean management is highly concerned with removing waste from any process. Waste increases costs and time spent on a process, making it undesirable in any form.

zh.text: 戴明的教导和日本工业在灾难性战争后成功东山再起的需要相结合，为丰田带来了成果。丰田领导层在二战之前就已经考虑过质量概念，但考虑到 20 世纪 40 年代和 50 年代日本经济和资源的性质，提高性能和效率成为更重要的目标。丰田领导者借鉴亨利·福特的制造理念，应用统计数据和新的质量概念创建了一个系统，他们认为该系统可以提高产量并允许生产可变产品，同时降低成本并确保质量。

有几个人在丰田生产系统的最终发展中发挥了重要作用。他们在流程中注入了自动化机械、防止缺陷发生的质量控制以及尚未应用如此详细和一致性的效率工具。丰田喜一郎（Kiichiro Toyoda）曾有过工厂工作经验。在之前的工作中，他通过输送机和其他自动化系统提高了纺织厂的流程效率。丰田章男在丰田制造过程中的某些生产线上引入了相同的概念。后来，丰田英二（Eiji Toyoda）和大野耐一（Taiichi Ohno）引入了“准时生产”（Just-in-Time）和“自动化”（Jidoka）的概念，它们是丰田生产系统的支柱。
驱动丰田系统的原则以及后来的精益流程管理或精益六西格玛的基础包括：
定义客户价值
确定客户需求和愿望的价值流
识别过程中的浪费
创建连续的工艺流程
不断努力减少达到客户满意度所需的步骤数量和时间
精益管理高度关注消除任何流程中的浪费。浪费会增加流程的成本和时间，因此任何形式的浪费都是不可取的。

title.zh: 摩托罗拉对缺陷的关注

en.text: Though the basis for Six Sigma was laid in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it wasn't until the mid- 1980s that these concepts saw large-scale success in the United States. Decades after Toyota developed its system, engineers at Motorola began to question how effective their quality management programs were. Those questions first arose after a Japanese company took over a Motorola television
manufacturing plant. By applying Lean concepts, the new company began creating televisions that demonstrated 1/20th the amount of defects as Motorola’s own television sets.

At the time, departments across Motorola measured defects as a ratio of a thousand opportunities. Bob Galvin, the CEO of Motorola, issued a challenge to his team. He wanted to see an improvement in quality and production—not just any improvement; he wanted a ten-fold improvement in half a decade. Engineer Bill Smith and a new addition to the Motorola team – Dr. Mikel Harry – began to work on the problem.

The team realized that measuring errors against a thousand opportunities didn't provide the level of detail needed for true statistical process control. Instead, the engineers wanted to measure defects against a million opportunities. We know that sigma levels were already defined and the idea of using sigma levels as a measure of quality began with Shewhart. It wasn't a long jump for the Motorola engineers to make from their desire for more accurate data to the basic concepts of Six Sigma as both a goal and a methodology.

Throughout the next two decades, Motorola worked to perfect its Six Sigma methodology, seeing positive results along the way. In addition to statistical tools, the team created a step-by-step process by which any team--in almost any industry--could make gains and improvements. For the first time, this type of statistical process control was taken out of the manufacturing environment on a large scale company-wide. Motorola applied the method to customer service, engineering, and technical support. It used the process to create a collaborative environment between stakeholders inside and outside of the organization. It was highly successful; according to Motorola, the company saved more than $16 billion as a result of continuous process improvement initiatives within 12 years.5

Motorola did more than improve its own systems and products, though. Galvin directed his team to share Six Sigma with the world. Motorola and its team published articles and books on the Six Sigma method and implemented efforts to train others. In this way, they created a methodology based on statistics that could be taught and implemented within any organization or industry.

zh.text: 虽然六西格玛的基础是在19世纪末20世纪初奠定的，但直到20世纪80年代中期这些概念才在美国获得大规模成功。丰田开发其系统几十年后，摩托罗拉的工程师开始质疑他们的质量管理计划的有效性。这些问题在一家日本公司收购摩托罗拉电视后首次出现
制造工厂。通过应用精益概念，新公司开始生产缺陷数量仅为摩托罗拉自家电视机 1/20 的电视机。
当时，摩托罗拉各部门将缺陷与一千个机会的比率来衡量。摩托罗拉首席执行官鲍勃·高尔文(Bob Galvin)向他的团队提出了挑战。他希望看到质量和产量的提高——不仅仅是任何改进；而是任何改进。他希望在五年内将业绩提高十倍。工程师 Bill Smith 和摩托罗拉团队的新成员 Mikel Harry 博士开始研究这个问题。
该团队意识到，根据一千个机会来衡量错误并不能提供真正的统计过程控制所需的详细程度。相反，工程师们想要针对一百万个机会来衡量缺陷。我们知道西格玛水平已经被定义，使用西格玛水平作为质量衡量标准的想法始于休哈特。对于摩托罗拉工程师来说，从对更准确数据的渴望到将六西格玛的基本概念作为目标和方法论，并不是一个漫长的跳跃。

在接下来的二十年里，摩托罗拉致力于完善其六西格玛方法论，并在此过程中看到了积极的成果。 除了统计工具之外，该团队还创建了一个循序渐进的流程，几乎任何行业的任何团队都可以通过该流程取得收益和改进。这种类型的统计过程控制首次在全公司范围内大规模地脱离制造环境。摩托罗拉将该方法应用于客户服务、工程和技术支持。它使用该流程在组织内部和外部的利益相关者之间创建协作环境。它非常成功；据摩托罗拉称，该公司在 12 年内通过持续的流程改进举措节省了超过 160 亿美元。 5

rows: 术语说明 Stakeholder（相关方）：会影响项目或被项目影响的人或组织。
zh.text: 术语说明 Stakeholder（相关方）：会影响项目或被项目影响的人或组织。
不过，摩托罗拉所做的不仅仅是改进自己的系统和产品。高尔文带领他的团队与世界分享六西格玛。摩托罗拉及其团队发表了有关六西格玛方法的文章和书籍，并努力培训其他人。通过这种方式，他们创建了一种基于统计的方法，可以在任何组织或行业内教授和实施。

title.en: ABB, Allied Signal, and General Electric

en.text: After leaving Motorola, Dr. Harry joined Asea Brown Boveri. At ABB, Harry worked with Richard Schroeder, who would also become a champion for Six Sigma. In fact, the two men later cofounded the Six Sigma Academy. At ABB, Harry came to realize a key idea in the evolution of Six Sigma: business, or profits, in some ways came before quality. Quality, in fact, was a driving factor of business. Customers didn’t make purchases if quality was poor. Because the individuals with the ability to decide in favor of Six Sigma initiatives were highly motivated by dollars, Harry incorporated financial tactics into the Six Sigma methodology. For the first time, the method was focused on the bottom-line as a primary goal with other concerns and goals stemming from financially-led goals.

In 1993, both Schroeder and Harry changed jobs, joining the team at Allied Signal. Allied Signal’s CEO at the time was Larry Bossidy. He was interested in Six Sigma but realized that executives and other high- level leaders experienced knowledge barriers while attempting to interact and collaborate with analysts, process engineers, and Six Sigma experts. Bossidy suggested that leadership at a company had to be
5 “The History of Six Sigma,” iSixSigma. http://www.isixsigma.com/new-to-six-sigma/history/history-six-sigma/
well-versed in Six Sigma to pick the right projects for success and support those projects on a company- wide basis to ensure success.

Harry, who is sometimes referred to as the father of Six Sigma, created a system for educating executive leaders. In conjunction with others at Allied Signal, he developed systems that allowed Six Sigma to be effectively deployed by leadership throughout an organization in its entirety.

Around the same time, GE CEO Jack Welch entered into the Six Sigma arena. Prior to learning about Six Sigma, Welch had stated he was not a proponent of quality measures. He’d previously criticized quality programs as heavy-handed approaches that did little to deliver results. Welch invited Larry Bossidy to speak at a GE corporate meeting in 1995. He also requested an analysis regarding the benefits of implementing Six Sigma at GE. At that time, GE was performing at between three and four sigma. The potential savings should the company rise to six sigma were enormous; estimates were $7 to $10 billion.6

Welch is known as a champion of Six Sigma not because he contributed in major ways to the development of statistical process controls or the Six Sigma toolsets, but because he demonstrated exactly how leaders should approach Six Sigma. He also made GE a historically successful Six Sigma organization by tying Six Sigma goals to employee reward structures. Employees were no longer only compensated based on financial performance factors; they were also evaluated based on Six Sigma performance. Suddenly, employees at every level had a personal reason to become involved in continuous process improvement, and employees and managers were supplied with the Six Sigma training to succeed.

zh.text: 离开摩托罗拉后，Harry 博士加入了 Asea Brown Boveri。在ABB，哈利与理查德·施罗德合作，后者也成为了六西格玛的冠军。事实上，两人后来共同创办了六西格玛学院。在ABB，哈利逐渐认识到六西格玛演变过程中的一个关键理念：商业，或者说利润，在某些方面先于质量。事实上，质量是业务的驱动因素。如果质量不好，顾客就不会购买。由于有能力做出支持六西格玛计划的个人都受到金钱的高度激励，哈利将财务策略纳入了六西格玛的方法论中。该方法首次将利润底线作为主要目标，其他关注点和目标源于财务主导的目标。
1993 年，施罗德和哈利都换了工作，加入了 Allied Signal 的团队。 Allied Signal 当时的首席执行官是拉里·博西迪 (Larry Bossidy)。他对六西格玛很感兴趣，但意识到高管和其他高层领导在尝试与分析师、流程工程师和六西格玛专家互动和协作时遇到了知识障碍。 Bossidy 建议公司的领导力必须是
5 《六西格玛的历史》，iSixSigma。 http://www.isixsigma.com/new-to-six-sigma/history/history-six-sigma/
精通六西格玛，能够选择成功的正确项目，并在全公司范围内支持这些项目，以确保成功。
哈利有时被称为六西格玛之父，他创建了一个教育行政领导人的系统。他与 Allied Signal 的其他人一起开发了系统，使六西格玛能够由整个组织的领导层有效部署。

大约在同一时间，GE首席执行官杰克·韦尔奇进入了六西格玛的舞台。在了解六西格玛之前，韦尔奇曾表示他并不是质量衡量标准的支持者。他此前曾批评质量计划是一种严厉的方法，对取得成果几乎没有作用。 1995年，韦尔奇邀请Larry Bossidy在GE公司会议上发言。他还要求分析GE实施六西格玛的好处。当时，GE正在三点到四西格玛之间表演。如果公司升级到六西格玛，潜在的节省成本是巨大的；估计为 7 至 100 亿美元。6
韦尔奇被称为六西格玛的拥护者，并不是因为他对统计过程控制或六西格玛工具集的开发做出了重大贡献，而是因为他准确地展示了领导者应该如何对待六西格玛。他还将六西格玛目标与员工奖励结构挂钩，使通用电气成为历史上成功的六西格玛组织。员工的薪酬不再仅仅基于财务绩效因素；他们还根据六西格玛的表现进行评估。突然之间，各级员工都有了参与持续流程改进的个人理由，并且为员工和经理提供了六西格玛培训以取得成功。

en.text: Following the success of corporations such as GE and Motorola, companies across the country rushed to implement Six Sigma. Unfortunately, in the rush to implement the process, many organizations executed improvements poorly or failed to gain an adequate understanding of statistical process control before moving forward with improvements. Although Six Sigma methods have been used by organizations to gain millions—even billions—in savings and efficiencies, some companies walked away with a bad taste for the process. That bad taste has resulted in the following misconceptions and myths that are still prevalent today in many industries:

Six Sigma is solely concerned with metrics and ignores common sense. The opposite is actually true: Six Sigma often starts with traditional common sense ideas, often arrived at through brainstorming, and validates those assumptions with data. The reason for this myth is twofold. First, managers and others who are used to making calls without being questioned are suddenly questioned in a Six Sigma environment. Not only are they questioned, but hard data sometimes proves them wrong. Second, in some cases data is improperly used to support conclusions that are against common sense or tradition. When those conclusions turn out to be faulty, it’s easy to blame the process of Six Sigma there is a lack of adequate understanding of the statistical theories involved.
Six Sigma is too expensive. While enterprise-wide adoption of Six Sigma can be costly at first, due in part to training needs, slowly integrating the concepts into a company often costs very
6 “The Evolution of Six Sigma,” PQA.net. http://www.pqa.net/ProdServices/sixsigma/W06002009.html

little in the long run. Organizations have to balance how they adopt Six Sigma with budgetary concerns—but when implemented correctly, Six Sigma generally leads to savings that more than cover its initial investment.

Six Sigma can fix anything. Opposite the nay-sayers are Six Sigma cheerleaders who believe they can apply the method like a salve to any problem. While Six Sigma can be applied to any problem of process, it’s not always relevant to problems of culture or people. If morale or other human resource problems are at the root of an issue, statistics can’t help. However, if morale is low because a process is difficult to work with or is performing poorly, Six Sigma can be used to improve the process, thereby improving morale.

zh.text: 继GE、摩托罗拉等企业的成功之后，全国各地企业纷纷实施六西格玛。不幸的是，在急于实施该流程的过程中，许多组织执行的改进效果不佳，或者在继续改进之前未能充分了解统计过程控制。尽管六西格玛方法已被各组织用来节省数百万甚至数十亿美元并提高效率，但一些公司对这一过程的品味不佳。这种糟糕的品味导致了以下误解和神话，这些误解和神话至今在许多行业仍然普遍存在：

六西格玛只关注指标，忽视常识。事实上恰恰相反：六西格玛通常从传统的常识想法开始，通常是通过头脑风暴得出的，并用数据验证这些假设。这个神话的原因是双重的。首先，习惯于打电话而不被询问的管理者和其他人突然在六西格玛的环境中受到询问。他们不仅受到质疑，而且有时硬数据证明他们是错误的。其次，在某些情况下，数据被不适当地用于支持违背常识或传统的结论。当这些结论被证明是错误的时，人们很容易指责六西格玛的过程对所涉及的统计理论缺乏足够的理解。
六西格玛太贵了。虽然一开始在整个企业范围内采用六西格玛的成本可能会很高，部分原因是培训需要，但慢慢地将这些概念融入公司往往成本非常高
6 “六西格玛的演变”，PQA.net。 http://www.pqa.net/ProdServices/sixsigma/W06002009.html
从长远来看很少。组织必须在采用六西格玛的方式与预算问题之间取得平衡，但如果实施得当，六西格玛所带来的节省通常会超过其初始投资。
六西格玛可以解决任何问题。与反对者相反的是六西格玛的热烈拥护者，他们相信自己可以像药膏一样使用这种方法来解决任何问题。虽然六西格玛可以应用于任何流程问题，但它并不总是与文化或人的问题相关。如果士气或其他人力资源问题是问题的根源，那么统计数据就无济于事。然而，如果由于流程难以配合或表现不佳而导致士气低落，则可以使用六西格玛来改进流程，从而提高士气。

en.text: Six Sigma is applied via a controlled project selection and management process. Once areas of concern are identified, leaders usually turn to analysts, Six Sigma experts, and subject-matter-experts for cost- benefit analyses. Six Sigma teams attempt to quantify how broken a process is (by calculating sigma level, costs of defects, downtime, and other metrics) and how much it might cost to address the problem. Problems are then prioritized according to severity as well as an organization’s ability to address the issue. Teams begin working through the priority list, returning to the analysis from time to time to ensure the list has not changed. The majority of this book covers the methods by which teams identify and address problems using Six Sigma.
The Levels of Six Sigma Certification

Possessing a Six Sigma certification proves that an individual has demonstrated practical applications and knowledge of Six Sigma. Some organizations offer in-house certification processes. Most people seek certification by enrolling in online or onsite Six Sigma training course. Most organizations that offer Six Sigma education also offer a path to certification. You can take courses for certification at various levels; Six Sigma levels are differentiated by belt level.
White Belt

A certified Six Sigma White belt is familiar with the basic tenets of the Six Sigma methodology, though they aren’t often regular members of process improvement teams. White belt training is a good introduction to Six Sigma for auxiliary staff members within an organization and can provide the information necessary for understanding why project teams do what they do. The training lets employees review project processes, understand information presented in milestone meetings, and better participate in project selection processes. White belt training can also be used across all levels of employees when organizations are attempting to implement a Six Sigma culture. It is worth noting that White Belt training usually only provides a very basic introduction and overview of Six Sigma, so much so that not all Six Sigma professionals recognize it as a true Six Sigma certification.
Yellow Belt

A yellow belt certification is a step above white belt: it is still considered a basic introduction to the concepts of Six Sigma, but a yellow belt learns basic information about the DMAIC method often used to improve processes. The following concepts are often included in Six Sigma yellow belt training:
Six Sigma roles
Team development and management
Basic quality tools such as Pareto charts, run charts, scatter diagrams and histograms
Common Six Sigma metrics
Data collection
Measurement system analysis
Root cause analysis
An introduction to hypothesis testing

At the yellow belt level, training is often geared toward understanding of the overall methodology and basic data collection. Yellow belts don’t need to know how to conduct hypothesis testing, but they must understand the language of hypothesis testing and the conclusions that are drawn from such tests. Yellow belts are often employees who need to know about the overall process and why it is being implemented.
Green Belt

Certified green belts work within Six Sigma teams, usually under the supervision of a black belt or master black belt. In some cases, green belts might lead or handle smaller projects on their own. Green belts are generally equipped with intermediate statistical analysis capabilities; they might address data and analysis concerns, help Black Belts apply Six Sigma tools to a project, or teach others within an organization about the overall Six Sigma methodology.

Green Belts can be middle managers, business analysts, project managers, and others who have a reason to be involved regularly with process improvement initiatives but who might not be a full-time Six Sigma expert within an organization. Sometimes, Green Belts are considered the worker bees of the Six Sigma methodology because they undertake most of the statistical data collection and analysis under the supervision of certified Black Belts.
The following concepts are often included in Green Belt training:
All of the information listed for yellow belt certification
Failure mode and effects analysis
Project and team management
Probability and the Central Limit Theorem
Statistical distributions
Descriptive statistics
How to perform basic hypothesis testing
Waste elimination and Kaizen
Basic control charts
Black Belt

A certified Six Sigma Black Belt usually works as the project leader on process improvement projects. They might also work within management, analyst, or planning roles throughout a company. Common minimum requirements for black belt certification include everything listed for yellow and green belts in addition to:
Advanced project and team management skills
Knowledge of the expansive list of Six Sigma brainstorming and project tools
Intermediate to advanced statistics
An understanding of other process improvement and quality programs, including Lean and Total Quality Management
An ability to design processes
Advanced capabilities for diagraming processes, including flow charts and value stream maps
Use of software to conduct analysis, such as Excel or Minitab
Master Black Belt

A Master Black Belt is the highest certification level achievable for Six Sigma. Within a business organization, Master Black Belts usually manage Black Belts and Green Belts, consult on especially difficult project concerns, offer advice and education about challenging statistical concepts, and train others in Six Sigma methodology.
Certification Exams

Most certification programs require individuals to pass an exam for certification; some require that green and black belt candidates also demonstrate their knowledge in the form of Six Sigma project experience.

If an exam is required for white or yellow belt certification, it is usually fairly short and covers basic concepts about the methodology. Green belt exams are longer and might include questions about statistics and some basic calculations. Black belt exams often take up to four hours to complete; they test for understanding and application. Exams might include difficult statistical problems or questions about how a project leader might handle various situations. While exams differ by organization, this book is designed based on The Council for Six Sigma Certification’s (CSSC) published body-of-knowledge requirements.

zh.text: 六西格玛是通过受控的项目选择和管理流程来应用的。一旦确定了关注领域，领导者通常会向分析师、六西格玛专家和主题专家寻求成本效益分析。 六西格玛团队试图量化流程的损坏程度（通过计算西格玛水平、缺陷成本、停机时间和其他指标）以及解决问题可能需要花费多少费用。然后根据严重性以及组织解决问题的能力对问题进行优先级排序。团队开始研究优先级列表，不时返回分析以确保列表没有改变。 本书的大部分内容涵盖了团队使用六西格玛识别和解决问题的方法。
六西格玛认证的级别
拥有六西格玛认证证明个人已表现出六西格玛的实际应用和知识。一些组织提供内部认证流程。大多数人通过参加在线或现场六西格玛培训课程来寻求认证。大多数提供六西格玛教育的组织也提供认证途径。您可以参加各种级别的认证课程； 六西格玛的等级是根据腰带等级来区分的。
白带

经过认证的六西格玛白带熟悉六西格玛方法论的基本原则，尽管他们通常不是流程改进团队的正式成员。 白带培训对于组织内的辅助人员来说是对六西格玛的一个很好的介绍，并且可以提供理解项目团队为何这样做所需的信息。该培训使员工能够审查项目流程，了解里程碑会议中提供的信息，并更好地参与项目选择流程。 当组织试图实施六西格玛文化时，白带培训也可以应用于所有级别的员工。值得注意的是，白带培训通常只提供对六西格玛非常基本的介绍和概述，以至于并非所有六西格玛专业人士都认可它是真正的六西格玛认证。
黄带
黄带认证比白带高一级：它仍然被认为是六西格玛概念的基本介绍，但黄带学习了经常用于改进流程的 DMAIC 方法的基本信息。六西格玛黄带培训中经常包含以下概念：
六西格玛角色
团队发展与管理
基本质量工具，例如帕累托图、运行图、散点图和直方图

zh.text: 术语说明 Hypothesis Test（假设检验）：用样本数据判断某个统计假设是否有足够证据被拒绝。
在黄带层面，培训通常旨在了解整体方法和基本数据收集。 黄带人员不需要知道如何进行假设检验，但必须了解假设检验的语言以及从假设检验中得出的结论。 黄带人员通常是需要了解整个流程以及实施原因的员工。
绿带
获得认证的绿带人员在六西格玛团队内工作，通常在黑带或黑带大师的监督下。在某些情况下，绿带人员可能会自己领导或处理较小的项目。 绿带人员一般具备中级统计分析能力；他们可能会解决数据和分析问题，帮助黑带人员将六西格玛工具应用到项目中，或者向组织内的其他人传授整体六西格玛方法论。
绿带人员可以是中层管理人员、业务分析师、项目经理以及其他有理由定期参与流程改进计划但可能不是组织内全职六西格玛专家的人员。有时，绿带人员被认为是六西格玛方法论的工蜂，因为他们在经过认证的黑带人员的监督下承担了大部分统计数据的收集和分析工作。
绿带培训中经常包含以下概念：
黄带认证所列全部信息
失效模式及影响分析
项目和团队管理
概率和中心极限定理
统计分布
描述性统计
如何进行基本假设检验
消除废物和改善

zh.text: 术语说明 Kaizen（改善）：强调小步、持续、全员参与的改进方式。
基本控制图
黑带
经过认证的六西格玛黑带通常担任流程改进项目的项目负责人。他们还可能在整个公司担任管理、分析师或规划职务。黑带认证的常见最低要求包括为黄带和绿带人员列出的所有内容，此外还包括：
先进的项目和团队管理技能
了解六西格玛头脑风暴和项目工具的广泛列表
中级到高级统计
了解其他流程改进和质量计划，包括精益和全面质量管理
设计流程的能力
用于绘制流程图表的高级功能，包括流程图和价值流图
使用Excel或Minitab等软件进行分析
黑带大师
黑带大师是六西格玛所能达到的最高认证级别。 在商业组织内，黑带人员大师通常管理黑带人员和绿带人员，就特别困难的项目问题提供咨询，提供有关挑战性统计概念的建议和教育，并对其他人进行六西格玛方法论的培训。
认证考试
大多数认证计划要求个人通过认证考试；有些要求绿带和黑带候选人还以六西格玛项目经验的形式展示他们的知识。
如果白人或黄带认证需要考试，考试通常相当短，涵盖了方法论的基本概念。 绿带考试时间较长，可能包括有关统计和一些基本计算的问题。 黑带考试通常需要四个小时才能完成；他们测试理解和应用。考试可能包括困难的统计问题或有关项目负责人如何处理各种情况的问题。虽然考试因组织而异，但本书是根据六西格玛认证委员会 (CSSC) 发布的知识体系要求设计的。
