en.text: In Unit 1, we introduced Six Sigma as a concept and covered a lot of principles that are foundational to creating and maintaining improvement in a business. In Unit 2, we’ll begin looking at what a process is, why quality is important in a process, and how Six Sigma projects can improve processes. The concepts you learn in Units 1 and 2 become the bricks used to build project work that we discuss throughout the rest of the book.
What is a Process?

A process is a collection of tasks, steps, or activities that are performed, usually in a specific order, and result in an end product such as a tangible good or the provision of a service. In a business, multiple processes work together to achieve organizational goals. Technically, the business or organization itself can be seen as one enormous process. For example, a law firm that handles criminal defense cases operates via a huge, complex process. Defendants and their cases enter the process. The output of the process is the result of the case: a bargain with prosecutors, a win or loss in court, or dismissal of charges prior to court.

Within the huge process that sees the defendant through to his or her outcome, there are hundreds, possibly thousands, of smaller processes. There are processes within processes. A lawyer and team of paralegals might move through the process of negotiation; a legal secretary might go through the process of setting appointments. Holding depositions, making copies, sending letters, and filing legal documents are all examples of processes. At the most detailed level, even answering the phone or typing a letter can be considered processes.

In Chapter 6, we briefly introduced the idea of scope and scope creep. To define and maintain proper scope, we said that a Six Sigma team had to identify the processes that were related to a process improvement or project. In the legal firm example, a project to reduce the time it takes to set appointments would likely not include a process for filing a legal brief. To know that, however, you have to know that the legal brief process doesn’t share components with the appointment setting process. In this chapter, we’ll cover the components of processes and a format for mapping those components known as a SIPOC.
Four Layers of the Process Definition

As you continue with this chapter, you’ll see that processes can be very complex. Our basic definition above is just that: Basic. Before we begin defining the components of a process, let’s peel back the layers of this concept known as “a process.”
The Steps

Whether physical, digital, or ideological, every process is a series of some number of steps. You can put those steps on paper in the form of instructions—often called a standard operating procedure in a formal business training or policy document -- or a visual diagram known as a process map. A process
map uses standard shapes and connections to create a map of a process that can be understood by most employees and any Six Sigma team member.
Processing Time

Processes all take a certain amount of time, and processing time can change with a variety of factors. Process maps and documents can only record information such as the average time a process takes or measures of variation in the processing time. This information is often noted in such documents because it provides valuable information to teams, but real-time observation of a process almost always provides better information about processing time.

A retail chain might create a process map for restocking a certain area. The process documentation notes an average time of two hours to fully restock the shelves in the defined area. In an effort to obtain more data about the process, a Six Sigma team observes employees actually performing job functions in real time at various times of day for two weeks. Some notes that come from those observations include:
Stocking in the evening takes only minutes.
Stocking during the day is hampered by the movements of customers.
Stocking work performed during peak shopping hours usually takes the longest.

With just this information, you can probably see an easy way to reduce stocking time in this example: move stocking duties to non-peak times when possible. Simply understanding the steps to stock the area is not enough to understand the process; you also have to gather data about process times.
Interdependencies

Almost any process in a business will be dependent upon one or more other processes. Remember, the business itself is a series of linked processes all working toward the same goal or goals. Sometimes, interdependencies are noted on processes maps. Other times, interdependencies are resource-related.

For example, consider a very simple passenger train scenario. The train leaves station A with passengers, carrying them to station B. Before the train can leave, the engineer must be on board and prepared to operate the machine. Safety checks, clearance from the rail yard, the closing of all the doors: these are all processes that must be completed before the train leaves the station. The process of the train transporting passengers is dependent upon the completion of other processes.

When working with processes during a Six Sigma improvement project, teams must be aware of interdependencies. What does any process you are working on rely? What relies on your process? The first is important because you might need help from processes or people upstream from your process when making improvements. The second is important because you have to know how your improvements will impact downstream processes and people – and improvement in the performance of your process doesn’t do any good for the company or organization as a whole if it hinders the
performance of a downstream process.
Resources and Assignment

Processes require resources. Like a motor vehicle requires fuel or electricity to run, a process requires resources such as power, people, cash, digital bandwidth, computer equipment, machinery, supplies, parts, and even skill. Since someone in an organization has to approve and pay for resources, project teams must understand the resources involved, the cost of those resources, and the owners of the processes and resources in question so they can make appropriate requests about needing additional resources.

zh.text: 在第一单元中，我们介绍了六西格玛这一概念，并涵盖了许多对于创造和维持企业改进的基础原则。在第二单元中，我们将开始了解什么是流程、为什么质量在流程中很重要，以及六西格玛项目如何改进流程。您在第 1 单元和第 2 单元中学到的概念将成为构建项目工作的基石，我们将在本书的其余部分中讨论这些项目工作。
什么是进程？
流程是通常按特定顺序执行并产生最终产品（例如有形商品或提供服务）的任务、步骤或活动的集合。在企业中，多个流程协同工作以实现组织目标。从技术上讲，企业或组织本身可以被视为一个巨大的过程。例如，一家处理刑事辩护案件的律师事务所的运作流程庞大、复杂。被告及其案件进入程序。该过程的输出就是案件的结果：与检察官讨价还价、法庭上的胜负或在法庭上驳回指控。
在被告达成其结果的庞大过程中，存在数百个甚至可能数千个较小的过程。流程中还有流程。律师和律师助理团队可能会完成谈判过程；法律秘书可能会经历任命的过程。持有证词、复印、发送信件和提交法律文件都是流程的例子。在最详细的层面上，甚至接电话或写信都可以被视为流程。
在第六章中，我们简要介绍了范围和范围蠕变的概念。为了定义和维护适当的范围，我们说六西格玛团队必须识别与流程改进或项目相关的流程。在律师事务所的例子中，减少预约时间的项目可能不包括提交法律摘要的过程。然而，要知道这一点，您必须知道法律简要流程并不与预约设置流程共享组件。在本章中，我们将介绍流程的组件以及映射这些组件的格式（称为 SIPOC）。

rows: 术语说明 SIPOC：供应商、输入、流程、输出、客户；用于快速界定流程边界。
zh.text: 术语说明 SIPOC：供应商、输入、流程、输出、客户；用于快速界定流程边界。

rows: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
zh.text: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
流程定义的四层
当您继续阅读本章时，您会发现流程可能非常复杂。我们上面的基本定义就是：基本。在开始定义流程的组成部分之前，让我们剥开这个称为“流程”的概念的各个层次。
步骤
无论是物理的、数字的还是意识形态的，每个过程都是一系列的一些步骤。您可以将这些步骤以说明的形式写在纸上（在正式的业务培训或政策文档中通常称为标准操作程序）或称为流程图的可视化图表。一个过程

rows: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
zh.text: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
地图使用标准形状和连接来创建大多数员工和任何六西格玛团队成员都可以理解的流程地图。
处理时间
所有流程都需要一定的时间，并且处理时间可能会因多种因素而变化。流程图和文档只能记录诸如流程平均时间或处理时间变化的度量等信息。这些信息通常会在此类文档中注明，因为它为团队提供了有价值的信息，但对流程的实时观察几乎总是可以提供有关处理时间的更好信息。
零售连锁店可能会创建一个流程图来补充特定区域的库存。流程文件指出，在指定区域的货架上重新装满货物的平均时间为两个小时。为了获得更多有关流程的数据，六西格玛团队连续两周在一天中的不同时间实时观察员工实际履行工作职能的情况。来自这些观察的一些注释包括：
晚上放养只需要几分钟。
白天的备货会因顾客的活动而受到阻碍。
在购物高峰时段进行的备货工作通常需要最长的时间。
仅凭这些信息，您可能就可以在此示例中找到一种减少库存时间的简单方法：尽可能将库存工作转移到非高峰时间。仅仅了解该区域库存的步骤并不足以了解该过程；您还必须收集有关处理时间的数据。
相互依赖性
企业中几乎任何流程都将依赖于一个或多个其他流程。 请记住，业务本身是一系列相互关联的流程，所有流程都致力于实现相同的目标。有时，相互依赖性会在流程图上注明。其他时候，相互依赖性与资源相关。
例如，考虑一个非常简单的客运列车场景。火车载着乘客离开 A 站，将他们带到 B 站。在火车出发之前，工程师必须在车上并准备操作机器。安全检查、出站、关闭所有车门：这些都是火车出站前必须完成的程序。火车运送乘客的过程取决于其他过程的完成。
在六西格玛改进项目中处理流程时，团队必须意识到相互依赖性。您正在处理的流程依赖什么？什么依赖于你的流程？第一个很重要，因为在进行改进时，您可能需要流程或流程上游人员的帮助。第二点很重要，因为你必须知道你的改进将如何影响下游流程和人员——如果流程性能的改进阻碍了整个公司或组织的发展，那么它对整个公司或组织没有任何好处。
下游过程的性能。
资源和分配
流程需要资源。就像机动车辆需要燃料或电力才能运行一样，一个流程也需要电力、人力、现金、数字带宽、计算机设备、机械、供应品、零件甚至技能等资源。由于组织中的某人必须批准资源并为其付费，因此项目团队必须了解所涉及的资源、这些资源的成本以及相关流程和资源的所有者，以便他们可以就需要额外资源提出适当的请求。
主要工艺组件

en.text: Processes are made up of components that include inputs, outputs, events, tasks (activities), and decisions. Inputs enter the process when a specific event occurs; tasks and decisions are performed upon or with the inputs. At the end of the process, an output is generated. Most of the time, the idea of process components is introduced with a simple factory-based illustration: raw goods of some type enter the factory, work is performed, and finished goods leave the factory. For example, if a factory makes hard candy, things such as sugar, water, plastic, and electrical power enter the factory. Equipment and employees take the inputs and work with them. The end result is a wrapped piece of candy ready for the store.

The figure below illustrates the idea of process components using a pizza shop example. An event – the ordering of a certain pizza – begins the process. You can see all of the components in the diagram, and we’ll talk about each component in detail in the section that follows.
Figure 1 Medium Cheese Pizza Process
Inputs

Input refers to anything that enters a process or is required to enter a process to drive the creation of an output. In the pizza example above, the inputs are all the ingredients needed to make the pizza. You might also consider factors such as oven temperature, type of oven, and the cook’s skill level to be inputs in the process.

Understanding all inputs to a process is important in Six Sigma because inputs are often causal – or related to causal – factors regarding a process. Inputs or the results of those inputs can cause errors or

defects in the process. The cookies burn when the oven is too hot. The computers made in a factory don’t function when the circuit boards are bad. A lawyer doesn’t win his case if his or her information is wrong. The oven temperature, the circuit boards, and the lawyer’s information: these are all inputs into processes that are also causing problems within the processes.
Other reasons for defining inputs when working with a process include:
Understanding the resources required for a process to run
Identifying extraneous inputs that aren’t required
Understanding costs for the process
Understanding how the process relates to processes that come before it
Remember, in a business, processes are linked together to accomplish a final goal or goals. The inputs entering process B might be the outputs leaving process A.
Outputs

The output of a process is the service or product that is used by the customer of the process. In the pizza example, the output is the cheese pizza the customer is going to eat. In the candy factory example, the output is the hard candy that will be sold by the retail store.

The process customer is not always the traditional end customer who purchases a product or service. Customers can be internal or external. An example of a process serving an internal customer might be seen in a business office that employees a receptionist to answer phone calls. If the receptionist takes messages or transfers phone calls, he or she is serving both the person on the phone and the person who is receiving the call or message.

In some cases, the customer of a process is not even a person. Many processes feed other processes. In a pharmacy, the process of entering data about a prescription feeds the process that bills an insurance company for the medication.

From a Six Sigma perspective, an output is almost always of more value to the ultimate process than the input is. The process itself involves adding value of some kind to the inputs. A bakery puts raw bread dough through the oven to add value to it: the result is an edible and tasty product that a consumer is more likely to purchase or to pay more for.
Events

Events are specific, predefined criteria or actions that cause a process to begin working. A process that performs well responds to an event just like a light bulb responds to the action of a switch being pulled. Six Sigma teams must determine what events trigger a process because it helps them understand why a process is being performed and whether the process is being run when it isn’t needed.

Consider an example about compliance audits in a financial sector company. Perhaps a company created a specific audit process that initiates when red flags on accounts are raised; the audit process is comprehensive and usually takes an average of 80 labor hours. You can imagine that it is an expensive process to run. In investigating, a Six Sigma team identifies the event associated with the process: anytime a discrepancy in an account is noted by a clerk, the compliance process is triggered.

The team investigates and realizes that this is true even when the discrepancy was minor – a few dollars or less – or the clerk was able to reconcile the discrepancy later in the day. The team might suggest that the relationship between the process and the event is a problem. The process is running at times when it might not be valuable for it to do so.
Tasks

Tasks, or activities, are the heart of a process. Just as the heart pumps blood through your body, the tasks within a process pump the inputs through, turning them into the outputs. Tasks are the physical, automated, or computerized actions within a process. Examples of tasks include:
A machine joining two metal parts with a weld
A person entering data into a software program
A computer processing data to create a report
An email being written
A piece of computerized work being routed within a workflow system
A chef chopping ingredients for a recipe
Decisions

Decisions are closely related to tasks and can be tasks themselves. A chef preparing ingredients for a soup dish has to chop those ingredients, but he also has to decide how much of each ingredient he needs. His decision will likely be guided by the recipe and the number of people he has to feed.

Decisions within a process are typically governed by a set of rules. Sometimes those rules are formally documented; other times, decisions are made via informal rules along with staff knowledge and experience. Processes that are governed by informal rules can have problems of consistency; even when all staff are experienced, they could have individual variations on performing a task. And, as we discussed in Unit 1, variation can lead to more opportunities for defects and a reduction in quality.
Using the task examples above, here are examples of decisions in a process:
A person entering data into a software program makes a decision to select a certain drop down category because of training or rules provided by the software
A computer processes a report; the result of that report is a number above a set threshold, so the computer sends the report to a person
When writing an email, a person chooses to include certain specific information, such as an order number or customer number, because it is protocol to do so when sending this type of email
All Components Are Related

You’re probably noticing that processes can be extremely complex, and the relationships between all the components are equally complex. Inputs can be outputs from previous processes; outputs can be inputs in the next process. A decision might result in an event that starts a new process, but it can also be the factor that decides which task begins. As Six Sigma teams work with processes – observing them, diagramming them, and measuring them – the teams begin to understand the relationships of the components, and that helps them make decisions about possible improvements and changes.

zh.text: 流程由输入、输出、事件、任务（活动）和决策等组件组成。当特定事件发生时，输入进入流程；任务和决策是根据输入执行的。在该过程结束时，会生成输出。大多数时候，流程组件的概念是通过一个简单的基于工厂的说明来介绍的：某种类型的原材料进入工厂，进行工作，然后成品离开工厂。 例如，如果一家工厂生产硬糖，糖、水、塑料和电力等物质就会进入工厂。设备和员工接受输入并与之合作。最终的结果是一块包装好的糖果可供商店使用。
下图使用披萨店示例说明了流程组件的想法。一个事件——订购某种披萨——开始了这个过程。您可以在图中看到所有组件，我们将在接下来的部分中详细讨论每个组件。
图1 中型奶酪披萨流程
输入
输入是指进入流程或进入流程以驱动输出的创建所需的任何内容。在上面的披萨示例中，输入是制作披萨所需的所有原料。您还可以考虑烤箱温度、烤箱类型和厨师的技能水平等因素作为该过程的输入。
在六西格玛中，了解流程的所有输入非常重要，因为输入通常是流程的因果因素（或与因果因素相关）。输入或这些输入的结果可能会导致错误或
过程中的缺陷。当烤箱太热时，饼干会烧焦。当电路板损坏时，工厂制造的计算机就无法运行。如果律师的信息有误，他或她就不会赢得诉讼。烤箱温度、电路板和律师信息：这些都是流程的输入，也会在流程中引起问题。
使用流程时定义输入的其他原因包括：
了解进程运行所需的资源
识别不需要的无关输入
了解流程的成本
了解该流程与其之前的流程有何关系
请记住，在企业中，流程链接在一起以实现一个或多个最终目标。进入流程 B 的输入可能是离开流程 A 的输出。
输出
流程的输出是流程的客户使用的服务或产品。在披萨示例中，输出是顾客要吃的奶酪披萨。在糖果工厂的示例中，产出是将由零售店出售的硬糖。
流程客户并不总是购买产品或服务的传统最终客户。客户可以是内部客户，也可以是外部客户。为内部客户提供服务的流程示例可以在商务办公室中看到，该办公室雇用接待员接听电话。如果接待员接听消息或转接电话，他或她同时为打电话的人和接收电话或消息的人提供服务。
在某些情况下，流程的客户甚至不是一个人。许多进程为其他进程提供支持。在药房中，输入处方数据的过程为向保险公司收取药物费用的过程提供支持。
从六西格玛的角度来看，对于最终过程来说，输出几乎总是比输入更有价值。该过程本身涉及为输入增加某种价值。面包店将生面包面团放入烤箱以增加其价值：结果是消费者更有可能购买或支付更多费用的可食用且美味的产品。
活动
事件是导致流程开始工作的特定的、预定义的标准或操作。执行良好的流程对事件的响应就像灯泡对拉动开关的动作做出响应一样。 六西格玛团队必须确定哪些事件触发流程，因为这有助于他们了解执行流程的原因以及流程是否在不需要时运行。
考虑一个有关金融部门公司合规审计的示例。也许一家公司创建了一个特定的审计流程，当账户出现危险信号时就会启动该流程；审核过程非常全面，通常平均需要80个工时。您可以想象这是一个运行成本高昂的过程。在调查中，六西格玛团队确定了与该流程相关的事件：只要职员发现账户存在差异，就会触发合规流程。
团队进行调查并意识到，即使差异很小（几美元或更少），或者店员能够在当天晚些时候协调差异，情况也是如此。团队可能会认为流程和事件之间的关系存在问题。该进程有时会在其运行可能没有价值的情况下运行。
任务
任务或活动是流程的核心。 正如心脏将血液泵入您的身体一样，流程中的任务将输入泵入体内，将其转化为输出。任务是流程中的物理、自动或计算机化操作。任务示例包括：
通过焊缝连接两个金属部件的机器
将数据输入软件程序的人
计算机处理数据以创建报告
正在写一封电子邮件
在工作流程系统中传送的一项计算机化工作
厨师正在切菜谱的原料
决定
决策与任务密切相关，并且可以是任务本身。准备汤菜原料的厨师必须将这些原料切碎，但他还必须决定每种原料需要多少。他的决定可能会受到食谱和他必须喂养的人数的指导。
流程中的决策通常受一组规则的约束。有时这些规则会被正式记录下来；其他时候，决策是通过非正式规则以及工作人员的知识和经验做出的。由非正式规则控制的流程可能存在一致性问题；即使所有员工都经验丰富，他们在执行任务时也可能存在个体差异。而且，正如我们在第 1 单元中讨论的那样，变化可能会导致更多的缺陷机会和质量下降。
使用上面的任务示例，以下是流程中的决策示例：
由于软件提供的培训或规则，将数据输入软件程序的人决定选择某个下拉类别
计算机处理报告；该报告的结果是高于设定阈值的数字，因此计算机将报告发送给某人
在撰写电子邮件时，人们选择包含某些特定信息，例如订单号或客户编号，因为发送此类电子邮件时这样做是协议
所有组件都是相关的
您可能注意到流程可能极其复杂，并且所有组件之间的关系同样复杂。输入可以是先前流程的输出；输出可以作为下一个过程的输入。决策可能会导致启动新流程的事件，但它也可能是决定启动哪个任务的因素。 当六西格玛团队处理流程时（观察它们、绘制图表并测量它们），团队开始了解组件之间的关系，这有助于他们就可能的改进和变更做出决策。

en.text: As teams work to improve processes, they need to understand who the process owners are. Depending on the business organization, process owners can be the people with the power to approve changes. In some organizations, the lowest-level owner might not have veto or decision power about all changes, but he or she is held responsible for the performance of the process.
A process owner can be:
A person in charge of a very specific process or function
A team supervisor or department manager
An executive-level individual who is probably responsible for a number of processes in his or her division
What does a process owner do?
The responsibilities of a process owner are often defined by the infrastructure of a specific business, but commonly, a process owner will:
Monitor how the process performs, usually using one or more metrics or regularly reported data elements.
Understand how the process fits into the overall business, why the output of the process is critical to business goals, and what inputs feed the process.
Ensures the process is documented via standard operating procedures (SOPs) and that process documentation is kept current and accurate.
Ensures operators within the process have the resources and training they need to complete their jobs.
In a Six Sigma environment, process owners might also ensure a control plan is in place and regularly review the process for possible improvement opportunities.
Data

Finally, all processes generate some form of data. Even if data isn’t yet being captured, information is inherent in any process. A computer program that automatically routes work in a workflow might generate data such as the number of items in work queues, how many items were worked that day, the time items have been waiting in queues, how many items were transferred, and where those items were transferred to. A process for filling bottles with liquid might generate data such as how much liquid is placed in each bottle, how many bottles per hour are filled, and perhaps variation between bottles.
Data is extremely valuable to Six Sigma teams because it’s often how they define whether a process is in control and successful.

zh.text: 当团队努力改进流程时，他们需要了解流程所有者是谁。根据业务组织的不同，流程所有者可以是有权批准变更的人员。在某些组织中，最低级别的所有者可能对所有变更没有否决权或决策权，但他或她对流程的执行负责。
流程所有者可以是：
负责非常具体的流程或职能的人
团队主管或部门经理
可能负责其部门的许多流程的高管级别人员
流程所有者做什么？
流程所有者的职责通常由特定业务的基础设施定义，但通常流程所有者将：
通常使用一个或多个指标或定期报告的数据元素来监视流程的执行情况。
了解流程如何融入整体业务、为什么流程的输出对于业务目标至关重要，以及流程的输入是什么。
确保通过标准操作程序 (SOP) 记录流程，并确保流程文档保持最新且准确。
确保流程中的操作员拥有完成工作所需的资源和培训。
在六西格玛环境中，流程所有者还可以确保控制计划到位，并定期审查流程以寻找可能的改进机会。
数据
最后，所有进程都会生成某种形式的数据。即使尚未捕获数据，信息也是任何流程中固有的。在工作流中自动路由工作的计算机程序可能会生成数据，例如工作队列中的项目数量、当天工作的项目数量、项目在队列中等待的时间、转移的项目数量以及这些项目转移到的位置。 用液体填充瓶子的过程可能会生成数据，例如每个瓶子中放入了多少液体、每小时填充了多少个瓶子以及瓶子之间的差异。
数据对于六西格玛团队来说非常有价值，因为他们通常通过数据来定义流程是否受控且成功。

en.text: The SIPOC diagram is often an important part of the define stage of a Six Sigma project. But you can use the SIPOC diagram anytime you want to learn more about a process or understand how a process in a business environment is linked to other processes.

SIPOC stands for Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, and Customer. For the purposes of a SIPOC, inputs and outputs follow the same guidelines described previously in this chapter. Suppliers are the people, processes, and organizations that supply inputs to your process. Customers are the people, processes, and organizations that make use of the outputs of your process. The process itself is the series of steps that take the inputs and make them outputs.
Benefits of a SIPOC Diagram

The SIPOC diagram is one of the most often used tools for understanding process components and process relevance because it is so effective and simple. Teams can create SIPOC diagrams in a single brainstorming session, though effective diagramming usually requires the presence of a process owner and one or more SMEs who are familiar with the process on a daily level.

SIPOC diagrams are also infinitely scalable. Teams can diagram processes at a very minute level, but they can also use SIPOC to diagram an entire business. We’ll walk through creating a SIPOC diagram and then provide some examples of SIPOCs at various levels to illustrate scalability.
Creating a SIPOC Diagram

You can create a SIPOC diagram as an individual exercise or within a team environment. SIPOCs can be created using a computer and software tool such as Word or Excel, but you can also draw them freehand on a whiteboard or piece of paper. Freehand diagramming is a valuable brainstorming tool because teams can quickly edit the rough draft of the diagram as they discuss a process. Keep this in mind :many of the diagrams presented in this book look clean because they have already been typed and edited. As you diagram your own processes, they can tend to look messy at first with edits, arrows, scratch outs, and inserts. “Editing” or putting rules on the brainstorming process can limit the ideas and information that flow during the process. You can always create a clean copy of the diagram for presentation purposes when you are finished brainstorming.

Step 1: Create Swim Lanes A SIPOC diagram is based on swim lanes. Swim lanes let you show how cross-functional activities and resources relate to your process. A SIPOC diagram gets five lanes: one each for Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, and Customers. You’ll end up with something that looks like the figure below.

Step 2: Set Boundaries and Name Your Process Before beginning a SIPOC session, set a definition for where your process or responsibility begins and ends. If you don’t understand the scope of your process, then your SIPOC session can get out of hand or produce a diagram that isn’t useful for your project.

Naming your process helps the team identify more readily with a specific aspect of the business. For example, a team working to improve processes within a medical office might look at a process named “Gathering New Patient Information.” By naming the process, the team has put some scope limitations in place: the team will talk about things related to gathering information from patients. The scope is further limited to the process by which staff gathers information from new patients.
As you work through the SIPOC diagramming exercise, you can point back to the name and the scope you’ve defined to keep the team on task with the discussion.
Step 3: Complete Swim Lanes You can complete SIPOC swim lanes in any order, but best practices usually have teams enter data in the following order:
Process
Outputs
Customer
Inputs
Suppliers
Realistically, teams will think of things as they work through the process, so you’ll be returning to swim lanes repeatedly to move information around and add new information.

A SIPOC isn’t usually a low-level or detailed map of the actual process, so keep teams high-level when completing the process swim lane. You can simply enter the name of the process in that section, or you can list some of the high level steps required for the process. Listing steps is a good exercise if teams aren’t sure about outputs and inputs – beginning to visualize the process usually helps ideas flow about how the process is connected to other processes and resources in the company.

To keep the session from turning into a detailed process mapping activity, ask the team to describe the process in less than five to seven steps. Keep things simple by limiting process steps to short verb-noun combos such as “Enter information,” “Collect money,” or “Place labels.”
Name Outputs and Customers

Once you have a rudimentary process definition, begin with either inputs or outputs. Ask the team “What does this process make? What comes out of this process?” Those answers go into the outputs swim lane.

Next, ask the team “Who or what uses the things that come from this process?” Place those answers in the customer swim lane. Remember that customers can be external or internal, and another process can be the customer in cases of automation.
Name Inputs and Suppliers
Ask the team “What does the process need to perform? What raw goods or materials feed the process?” Record those answers in the inputs section.

You can divide the idea of inputs into two types, if you like. First, you have the actual inputs – the goods and services that are transformed by the process to create the outputs. Second, you have enablers of the process. These aren’t technically inputs because they don’t enter the process and aren’t changed by the process; instead, they are required for the process to function. Machinery is an enabler. In a process that cuts metal parts from a steel sheet, the machine that does the cutting is an enabler. While it’s not required, separating enablers on your SIPOC helps you define the process and provides additional information for later in the project.

Once you have a list of inputs, ask the team, “Where do the inputs come from? Who or what supplies the process with these things?” As with customers, suppliers can be external or internal. A vendor might provide the raw sugar that goes into the candy in a factory; the marketing department might provide the leads that the sales department uses to create orders.

Suppliers can also be other processes, particularly in an automated environment, and you can have a list of several suppliers for one input in a raw SIPOC diagram. For example, support tickets come into the Information Technology (IT) department. The supplier of the ticket could be both the end-user submitting the ticket and the automated process that routes the ticket to the appropriate work queue. If you are documenting enablers, you might record the end-user as the supplier and the automated process as the enabler.

Step 4: Validate the Information Ensure that your understanding of the process at this high level is accurate by validating your diagram. If you’ve put together a comprehensive team that includes SMEs, the team can validate most of the information on its own. It’s always a good idea to get a second opinion on anything the team isn’t sure about, though. Invite other SMEs or the process owner to review the diagram briefly with the team and provide feedback.

zh.text: SIPOC 图通常是六西格玛项目定义阶段的重要组成部分。但是，您可以随时使用 SIPOC 图来了解有关流程的更多信息或了解业务环境中的流程如何与其他流程链接。
SIPOC 代表供应商、输入、流程、输出和客户。就 SIPOC 而言，输入和输出遵循本章前面所述的相同准则。供应商是为您的流程提供输入的人员、流程和组织。客户是使用流程输出的人员、流程和组织。该过程本身是获取输入并将其输出的一系列步骤。
SIPOC 图的好处
SIPOC 图是理解流程组件和流程相关性最常用的工具之一，因为它非常有效且简单。团队可以在一次头脑风暴会议中创建 SIPOC 图，但有效的图表通常需要流程所有者和一个或多个日常熟悉该流程的 SME 在场。
SIPOC 图还可以无限扩展。团队可以在非常精细的层面上绘制流程图，但他们也可以使用 SIPOC 绘制整个业务图。我们将逐步创建 SIPOC 图，然后提供一些不同级别的 SIPOC 示例来说明可扩展性。
创建 SIPOC 图

您可以创建 SIPOC 图作为个人练习或在团队环境中。 SIPOC 可以使用计算机和软件工具（例如 Word 或 Excel）创建，但您也可以在白板或纸上徒手绘制它们。手绘图表是一种有价值的头脑风暴工具，因为团队可以在讨论流程时快速编辑图表的草稿。请记住这一点：本书中提供的许多图表看起来很干净，因为它们已经被输入和编辑过。 当您绘制自己的流程时，它们一开始可能会因编辑、箭头、草稿和插入而显得混乱。 “编辑”或在头脑风暴过程中制定规则可能会限制在此过程中流动的想法和信息。完成头脑风暴后，您始终可以创建图表的干净副本以供演示之用。
步骤 1：创建泳道 SIPOC 图基于泳道。泳道可让您展示跨职能活动和资源如何与您的流程相关。 SIPOC 图有五个通道：供应商、输入、流程、输出和客户各一个。您最终会得到如下图所示的结果。
步骤 2：设置边界并命名您的流程 在开始 SIPOC 会议之前，为您的流程或责任的开始和结束位置设置定义。如果您不了解流程的范围，那么您的 SIPOC 会议可能会失控或生成对您的项目无用的图表。
为流程命名有助于团队更轻松地识别业务的特定方面。例如，致力于改进医疗办公室内流程的团队可能会考虑名为“收集新患者信息”的流程。通过命名该流程，团队设置了一些范围限制：团队将讨论与从患者那里收集信息相关的事情。范围进一步限于工作人员从新患者收集信息的过程。
当您完成 SIPOC 图表练习时，您可以回顾您定义的名称和范围，以使团队能够专注于讨论任务。
步骤 3：完成泳道 您可以按任何顺序完成 SIPOC 泳道，但最佳实践通常让团队按以下顺序输入数据：
工艺流程
输出
客户
输入
供应商
实际上，团队会在整个流程中思考问题，因此您将反复返回泳道以移动信息并添加新信息。
SIPOC 通常不是实际流程的低级或详细地图，因此在完成流程泳道时让团队保持高水平。您可以简单地在该部分中输入流程的名称，也可以列出该流程所需的一些高级步骤。 如果团队不确定输出和输入，列出步骤是一个很好的练习——开始可视化流程通常有助于了解该流程如何与公司其他流程和资源连接。
为了防止会议变成详细的流程图活动，请要求团队用少于五到七个步骤来描述该流程。通过将流程步骤限制为简短的动词-名词组合（例如“输入信息”、“收钱”或“放置标签”）来使事情变得简单。
名称输出和客户
一旦有了基本的流程定义，就从输入或输出开始。询问团队“这个过程会产生什么？这个过程会产生什么结果？”这些答案进入输出泳道。
接下来，询问团队“谁或什么使用了此过程中产生的东西？”将这些答案放在客户泳道中。请记住，客户可以是外部的，也可以是内部的，在自动化的情况下，另一个流程可以是客户。
名称输入和供应商
询问团队“该流程需要执行什么？该流程需要哪些原材料或材料？”将这些答案记录在输入部分。
如果您愿意，您可以将输入的想法分为两种类型。首先，你有实际的输入——通过创建输出的过程转换的商品和服务。其次，你有这个过程的推动者。从技术上讲，这些不是输入，因为它们不进入流程，也不会被流程更改；相反，它们是流程正常运行所必需的。机械是推动者。在从钢板上切割金属零件的过程中，进行切割的机器是一个推动者。虽然这不是必需的，但在 SIPOC 上分离推动因素可以帮助您定义流程并为项目后期提供附加信息。
获得输入列表后，询问团队：“输入从哪里来？谁或什么为流程提供这些东西？”与客户一样，供应商可以是外部的，也可以是内部的。供应商可能会在工厂提供用于制作糖果的原糖；营销部门可能会提供销售部门用来创建订单的线索。
供应商也可以是其他流程，特别是在自动化环境中，并且您可以在原始 SIPOC 图中输入一个包含多个供应商的列表。 例如，支持票进入信息技术 (IT) 部门。票证的提供者既可以是提交票证的最终用户，也可以是将票证路由到适当的工作队列的自动化流程。如果您正在记录促成因素，则可以将最终用户记录为供应商，将自动化流程记录为促成因素。
步骤 4：验证信息 通过验证图表，确保您对高层次流程的理解是准确的。如果您组建了一个包含中小企业的综合团队，该团队可以自行验证大部分信息。不过，对于团队不确定的任何事情寻求第二意见总是一个好主意。邀请其他 SME 或流程负责人与团队一起简要查看图表并提供反馈。

title.en: Tips for a SIPOC Brainstorming Session
title.zh: SIPOC 头脑风暴会议的技巧

en.text: One of the best ways to create an initial SIPOC diagram during a team session is on large pieces of paper or a whiteboard. Create swim lanes by drawing them on the whiteboard or hanging a piece of paper for each swim lane on the wall. Provide the team with sticky notes and markers; write on sticky notes instead of writing directly on the board or paper. This lets you move components around quickly as you work through the diagram.

zh.text: 在团队会议期间创建初始 SIPOC 图的最佳方法之一是在大纸或白板上。通过在白板上绘制泳道或在墙上为每个泳道挂一张纸来创建泳道。为团队提供便利贴和记号笔；在便利贴上书写，而不是直接在黑板或纸上书写。这使您可以在处理图表时快速移动组件。

en.text: Here are some sample SIPOC diagrams. The first diagram is at the highest level: the process is the business itself. The second diagram features an automated process. The third diagram illustrates a people-powered factory process and includes enablers.
Business-Level SIPOC Diagram

This diagram shows the SIPOC for a mid-sized printing company. It’s a very high-level, simplified SIPOC that shows how customers and vendors provide information and items; the printing company then turns those inputs into products such as printed business cards. The final product goes to individuals, businesses, and marketing professionals who placed the order.

Most of the time, a Six Sigma team won’t deal with a business-level SIPOC diagram. However, if the team includes members from outside the division or company, such as vendors or consultants assisting with an improvement, then starting with a high-level diagram can help those outside of the business understand the overall goals of the company.
SIPOC of an Automated Process

The diagram below represents an automated process in a mail-order pharmacy. The process in question puts labels on bottles that are to be filled with corresponding medications. The scope of the process is only the labeling of the bottles.

Because this is a process within a chain of automated processes, almost all of the components are machines, processes, and things. Prior to labeling, a machine sorts bottles by size. That machine feeds the labeling station as needed. After the labeling is done, another station fills the bottles.
SIPOC with Enablers Noted

The SIPOC diagram below illustrates how enablers might be recorded for your process. The process in question takes place in a factory that makes furniture; in this process, a person attaches legs to a barstool on an assembly line. For the purposes of this illustration, leg attachment is the last step in the completion of the product, which means the product moves from the leg attachment station to packing and shipping.

Without the conveyor machine, the people in involved in this process would have to move items manually. The conveyor isn’t 100 percent required for legs to be added to the stool, but it enables the process to move at a more efficient pace. A case could be made that the drill isn’t required either – screws can be installed manually – but it’s certainly what enables the process to move at a speed required for mass production.

With just this simple SIPOC diagram of a process, a Six Sigma team would already have some idea about where variation could be hiding, what drives efficiencies in the process, and how the process relates to the overall business.
Create Your Own SIPOC Diagram

Whether working in a team or on your own, choose a process you know about and practice creating your own diagram. Pick a process associated with your business or a business example you have experience with. Use the templates on the next page to get you started.

rows: 术语说明 Sample / Sampling（样本/抽样）：从总体中选取部分数据进行分析；样本应尽量代表总体。
zh.text: 术语说明 Sample / Sampling（样本/抽样）：从总体中选取部分数据进行分析；样本应尽量代表总体。
以下是一些 SIPOC 图示例。第一个图位于最高级别：流程就是业务本身。第二张图展示了一个自动化流程。第三张图说明了以人为本的工厂流程并包括推动因素。
业务级 SIPOC 图
该图显示了一家中型印刷公司的 SIPOC。这是一个非常高级、简化的 SIPOC，显示客户和供应商如何提供信息和项目；然后，印刷公司将这些投入转化为印刷名片等产品。最终产品将交付给下订单的个人、企业和营销专业人士。
大多数时候，六西格玛团队不会处理业务级的SIPOC图。但是，如果团队包括来自部门或公司外部的成员，例如协助改进的供应商或顾问，那么从高级图表开始可以帮助业务外部的人员了解公司的总体目标。
自动化流程的 SIPOC
下图展示了邮购药房的自动化流程。该过程将标签贴在要填充相应药物的瓶子上。该过程的范围只是瓶子的标签。
因为这是自动化流程链中的一个流程，所以几乎所有组件都是机器、流程和事物。在贴标之前，机器会按尺寸对瓶子进行分类。该机器根据需要向贴标站供料。贴标完成后，另一个站将灌装瓶子。
SIPOC 已指出推动因素
下面的 SIPOC 图说明了如何为您的流程记录促成因素。所讨论的过程发生在一家制造家具的工厂；在此过程中，一个人在装配线上将腿固定在高脚凳上。出于本说明的目的，支腿连接是完成产品的最后一步，这意味着产品从支腿连接站移动到包装和运输。
如果没有输送机，参与此过程的人员将不得不手动移动物品。将腿添加到凳子上并不是 100% 需要传送带，但它可以使整个过程以更高效的速度进行。可以说，也不需要钻头——可以手动安装螺钉——但这确实可以使工艺以大规模生产所需的速度进行。
仅仅通过这个简单的流程 SIPOC 图，六西格玛团队就已经知道差异可能隐藏在哪里、流程中的效率驱动因素以及流程与整体业务的关系。
创建您自己的 SIPOC 图
无论是在团队中工作还是独自工作，选择一个您了解的流程并练习创建自己的图表。选择与您的业务相关的流程或您有经验的业务示例。使用下一页上的模板来帮助您入门。

en.text: One of the most concise definitions of quality comes from the International Organization for Standardization, or ISO. ISO 9000 defines quality as the “degree to which a set of inherent characteristics fulfills requirements.”7

The same document defines requirements as expectations or needs that are implied, obligatory, or stated, and the ISO notes that requirements can be generated by different interest points. A Six Sigma team should be interested in requirements generated by all interest points, but often focuses most on those generated by the customer. Various types of requirements might include:

Customer expectations, which are typically stated or implied values. It’s implied that a customer wants the product he or she ordered. Expectations of delivery speed might be stated in the form of feedback in customer surveys.

Compliance or regulatory rules, which are obligatory. For example, banks must protect credit card information—they are obligated by rules from government and the industry’s Payment Card Information Data Security Standards (PCI-DSS). Similarly, healthcare organizations must protect the confidentiality and security of patient data; they are obligated to do so under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Brand expectations, which come from in-house leadership. Brand expectations are typically stated; while not obligatory in the sense of being backed by regulation, companies for which high-quality, a specific voice, or other unique factor is a component of branding might treat brand expectations as obligatory. Coca-Cola, for example, has a brand that is recognizable around the globe. While components of that brand, such as the design of logos or soda cans, aren’t mandated by regulations and might not be required by customers, Coca-Cola itself holds these components as important and puts resources and effort into them because it values its brand.
In this chapter, we’ll take a look specifically at quality factors critical to processes and process improvement as well as costs associated with quality in general.

zh.text: 最简洁的质量定义之一来自国际标准化组织 (ISO)。 ISO 9000 将质量定义为“一组固有特性满足要求的程度。”7
同一份文件将需求定义为隐含的、强制性的或陈述的期望或需求，并且 ISO 指出需求可以由不同的兴趣点生成。六西格玛团队应该对所有兴趣点产生的需求感兴趣，但往往最关注的是客户产生的需求。各种类型的要求可能包括：
客户期望，通常是明示或暗示的值。这意味着客户想要他或她订购的产品。对交付速度的期望可以以客户调查反馈的形式表述。
合规性或监管规则是强制性的。例如，银行必须保护信用卡信息——它们有义务遵守政府规则和行业支付卡信息数据安全标准 (PCI-DSS)。同样，医疗保健组织必须保护患者数据的机密性和安全性；根据《健康保险流通与责任法案》(HIPAA)，他们有义务这样做。
品牌期望来自内部领导层。通常会说明品牌期望；虽然在监管支持的意义上不是强制性的，但对于高品质、特定的声音或其他独特因素是品牌塑造组成部分的公司来说，品牌期望可能会被视为强制性的。例如，可口可乐拥有一个全球知名的品牌。虽然该品牌的组成部分，例如徽标或汽水罐的设计，不受法规强制，也可能不是客户所要求的，但可口可乐本身认为这些组成部分很重要，并在其中投入资源和精力，因为它重视自己的品牌。
在本章中，我们将专门研究对流程和流程改进至关重要的质量因素以及与质量相关的总体成本。
关键质量特性（CTQ） 特点

title.zh: 关键质量特性（CTQ） 特点

en.text: Critical to quality characteristics, or CTQs, are the factors or parameters that are the major drivers of quality within an organization or process. Usually, CTQs are key characteristics that can be measured; where the performance of said metric provides information about whether or not the customer is going to be satisfied.

CTQs are closely related to CTCs, or critical to customer characteristics, but they are not the same thing. Something can be critical to quality – even critical to how a customer ultimately feels about a service or product – without being critical to the customer directly. CTQs are internal concerns, but they drive CTCs.
7 https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:9000:ed-3:v1:en:term:3.9.11
Let’s look at some examples of CTQs and CTCs to understand the difference and the relationship between these two factors.
A Pair of Pants

When a customer purchases a pair of pants, he or she is usually concerned with how the pants fit and look. Are they comfortable, is the size correct, and does the clothing match the customer’s personal style?

It’s hard to create a measurement for whether pants are comfortable, but a manufacturer can take customer feedback on various types of pants and learn that a certain fabric with a certain cut is most comfortable for the target audience. The manufacturer can also determine appropriate measurements for each size. During the manufacturing process, these critical-to-quality factors are applied: only fabric that meets the specifications identified is used. The fabric is then cut to specific measurements and sewn together in a specific manner – measurements and sewing methods are critical to quality.

The average customer, however, doesn’t want to hear about the exact measurements of each fabric piece or the way the seams were sewn. They want to put on a pair of pants and experience a comfortable fit.
Chocolate Bars

A chocolate company conducts a survey to find out why sales of its newest product haven’t performed as expected. The feedback suggests that the chocolate is too sweet – the taste and the sweetness of the chocolate is a critical to customer characteristic.

The company might tweak its formula, reducing the amount of sugar that goes into the chocolate. The recipe – and the amount of sugar -- is a critical to quality factor in this case. But what if the customer feedback indicated that health-conscious consumers simply didn’t want to buy a chocolate bar with so much sugar in it? Then the amount of sugar in the recipe becomes both a CTQ and a CTC. It is critical to the quality of the taste of the bar, but customers might also look at the nutritional information on the bar and make purchasing decisions based on the amount of sugar in the chocolate.
Mobile App Development

If a business wants to launch a mobile app for its customers, then an obvious customer-centric need is that the app works on the customer’s phone. The customer doesn’t care about the process the business needs to go through to launch the app on the platform in question, but the business must meet the criteria for Apple, Android, Windows, or other mobile operating systems. Those requirements become some of the CTQs for the mobile app development, even though certain requirements from the platforms might not appear to be at all related to statements from customers about desires or needs.
Why Identify CTQs?

In a process improvement environment, CTQs are critical to narrowing work scope and understanding how to enact change. Consider the 80/20 rule discussed in Chapter 5. Often, CTQs are the factors, characteristics, or outputs that drive 80 percent of customer satisfaction. By improving these few critical factors, teams can substantially impact customer satisfaction and the performance of the overall process. Identifying CTQs lets teams create the most improvement possible with the time, money, and people resources available.

Outside of a project environment, understanding CTQs lets organizations stay on top of quality. By managing a few critical metrics, teams can ensure excellent output in a continuous fashion and identify potential areas for improvement before they become customer-facing problems.

Using a CTQ Tree to Convert Customer Needs to Quality Metrics In Chapter 5, we introduced the concept of the Voice of the Customer, or VoC. Six Sigma teams usually start with some type of VoC data when they are defining a problem and working on goals for a project. Either the team conducts surveys to hear from a statistically relevant group of customers during the first few phases of a project, or the team receives feedback from internal customers about a process. Sometimes, the VoC information a team begins with is something as simple as a champion or executive- level individual making a statement about expectations for an internal process or project. When VoC data is limited in such a fashion, teams might have to work harder to validate assumptions with data before moving on to CTQ analysis.

To gain a better understanding of how to measure the quality of a process, teams must convert VoC statements to CTQs. One of the best ways to do this is through a diagramming process known as a CTQ tree.

A CTQ tree begins with specific and critical customer needs, breaks that need down into drivers, and uses the drivers to create requirements. Specific requirements are easier to convert to measurable quality components. While each CTQ tree is unique, they begin with a common form. The common structure of a CTQ tree is shown below.

When creating a CTQ tree, you don’t have to follow an equal pattern for drivers and requirements. Some customer needs will have more drivers than others; some drivers will have more requirements. You might also have multiple CTQ trees – you’ll want to create one for every need you identify that is critical to a customer.
Identify Critical-to-Customer Needs

Begin the CTQ tree process by creating a list of needs that are critical to the customer. A bank working on processes dealing with online checking access might identify accessibility, user-friendly interfaces, and security of information as the major critical-to-customer needs, for example. Define needs in broad terms to help catch all drivers and requirements later in the diagramming process.

The best way to define needs is to directly ask customers for feedback, but time and resources don’t always allow for surveys. Six Sigma teams might be able to take advantage of data collected via recent surveys or feedback forms, which is the next-best thing. In the absence of customer feedback, brainstorm critical needs with a group of employees who has knowledge of and experience with the customer. Subject matter experts from sales, customer service, and complaint departments can often provide viable information when the customer is the end-user. You can also begin a CTQ tree with the outputs of your SIPOC diagram; depending on how you structured the outputs on a SIPOC, you might need to define critical quality factors for the output as a starting point for your CTQ tree diagram.
Identify Drivers of Quality

Once you have a list of critical needs, work with one need at a time to create a tree similar to the diagram above. Identify quality drivers that must be present or met for the customer need to be fulfilled. For example, customers of an HVAC service company might require excellent service. Drivers for that need might include friendly service technicians, helpful and knowledgeable employees, and a timely response to service calls.

Drivers are the transition point between customer needs and requirements; you don’t necessarily have to be able to measure drivers, but you want them to be a bit more detailed than the broad customer needs you already identified and you want to be flowing in the direction of measureable factors when possible.
List Requirements for Each Driver

Requirements are the most detailed breakdown regarding critical to quality characteristics. These are the things that you can measure that lead you to understand whether drivers are performing appropriately so customer needs are met.
For example, let’s look at our HVAC example in a CTQ tree format.

You can see in the above CTQ tree that drivers have been converted to requirements – and each of those requirements can be measured with numbers. In some cases, driver-to-requirement conversions equate to a hard number. The chocolate bar example at the beginning of this chapter features such a scenario: if the company deems that the recipe with a quarter cup of sugar is the correct recipe, then the process metric for quality is exactly a quarter cup of sugar.

In other examples, companies might provide leeway for exceptions or the understanding that a process is not going to hit an exact number every single time. For example, an HVAC team cannot possibly arrive at a customer’s home exactly 24 hours after a phone call is made – and if the service technicians can arrive earlier than 24 hours, most people would want them to. That means the company has to create a definition for the requirement: how many hours is it before a customer considers a technician untimely? In the case of our example company, it’s 48 hours. The requirement in another situation might be 24 hours.

Because teams will use the requirements from the CTQ trees to develop process measurements and metrics for success, it is extremely important that each requirement is vetted before teams incorporate it into the project or process. Requirements should be compared to VoC data, to existing measurements, and to experience and knowledge from subject matter experts and leaders. The team should ask themselves and others “If these requirements are met, will the customer be satisfied?” If the answer is ever no, then the requirements need work. The team might also consider asking “Are these requirements possible in the real world.” If the answer is no, then either the process or the requirements needs work.

rows: 术语说明 CTQ（关键质量特性）：把客户需求转化为可测量的质量要求。
zh.text: 术语说明 CTQ（关键质量特性）：把客户需求转化为可测量的质量要求。
关键质量特性（CTQ）特性或 CTQ 是组织或过程中质量主要驱动因素或参数。通常，CTQ 是可以衡量的关键特征； 其中所述指标的表现提供了有关客户是否满意的信息。
CTQ 与 CTC 密切相关，或者对客户特征至关重要，但它们不是同一件事。有些东西可能是关键质量特性（CTQ）——甚至对客户对服务或产品的最终感受至关重要——但并不直接对客户至关重要。 CTQ 是内部问题，但它们推动 CTC。
7 参见 ISO 9000:2015 术语 3.9.11： https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:9000:ed-3:v1:en:term:3.9.11
让我们看一些 CTQ 和 CTC 的示例，以了解这两个因素之间的区别和关系。
一条裤子
当顾客购买裤子时，他或她通常关心裤子合身和外观。它们是否舒适、尺寸是否正确、服装是否符合顾客的个人风格？
很难衡量裤子是否舒适，但制造商可以根据客户对各种类型裤子的反馈，了解某种面料和某种剪裁对目标受众来说最舒适。制造商还可以为每种尺寸确定适当的尺寸。在制造过程中，应用了这些对质量至关重要的因素：仅使用符合确定规格的织物。然后将织物裁剪成特定的尺寸并以特定的方式缝制在一起——尺寸和缝制方法是关键质量特性（CTQ）。
然而，普通顾客并不想了解每块布料的精确尺寸或接缝的缝制方式。他们想要穿上一条裤子并体验舒适合身的感觉。
巧克力棒
一家巧克力公司进行了一项调查，以找出其最新产品的销售未达到预期的原因。反馈表明巧克力太甜了——巧克力的味道和甜度对顾客特征至关重要。
该公司可能会调整其配方，减少巧克力中的糖含量。在这种情况下，配方和糖的量是一个关键的质量特性（CTQ）因素。但是，如果客户反馈表明注重健康的消费者根本不想购买含这么多糖的巧克力棒怎么办？那么配方中的糖量就变成了 CTQ 和 CTC。 它对巧克力棒的口味质量至关重要，但顾客也可能会查看巧克力棒上的营养信息，并根据巧克力中的糖含量做出购买决定。
移动应用程序开发
如果企业想要为其客户推出移动应用程序，那么一个明显的以客户为中心的需求是该应用程序可以在客户的手机上运行。客户并不关心企业在相关平台上启动应用程序所需经历的流程，但企业必须满足 Apple、Android、Windows 或其他移动操作系统的标准。这些要求成为移动应用程序开发的一些 CTQ，尽管平台的某些要求可能看起来与客户关于愿望或需求的陈述完全无关。
为什么要识别 CTQ？
在流程改进环境中，CTQ 对于缩小工作范围和了解如何实施变革至关重要。考虑第 5 章中讨论的 80/20 规则。通常，CTQ 是推动 80% 客户满意度的因素、特征或输出。通过改善这几个关键因素，团队可以极大地影响客户满意度和整个流程的绩效。确定 CTQ 可以让团队利用可用的时间、金钱和人力资源实现最大程度的改进。

rows: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
zh.text: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
在项目环境之外，了解 CTQ 可以让组织保持最佳质量。通过管理一些关键指标，团队可以持续确保出色的产出，并在潜在的改进领域成为客户面临的问题之前识别出来。

使用 CTQ 树将客户需求转换为质量指标 在第 5 章中，我们介绍了客户之声（VOC）或 VOC 的概念。 六西格玛团队在定义问题和实现项目目标时通常会从某种类型的 VOC 数据开始。团队要么在项目的前几个阶段进行调查，听取统计上相关的客户群体的意见，要么团队从内部客户那里接收有关流程的反馈。有时，团队开始时使用的 VOC 信息很简单，例如冠军或高管人员对内部流程或项目的期望发表声明。 当 VOC 数据如此有限时，团队可能必须更加努力地用数据验证假设，然后再进行 CTQ 分析。
为了更好地了解如何衡量流程质量，团队必须将 VOC 声明转换为 CTQ。实现此目的的最佳方法之一是通过称为 CTQ 树的图表过程。
CTQ 树从特定且关键的客户需求开始，将需求分解为驱动因素，并使用驱动因素创建需求。特定要求更容易转换为可衡量的质量组件。虽然每棵 CTQ 树都是独一无二的，但它们都以通用的形式开始。 CTQ树的常见结构如下所示。
创建 CTQ 树时，您不必遵循相同的驱动因素和需求模式。有些客户需求会比其他需求有更多的驱动因素；有些司机会有更多要求。您可能还拥有多个 CTQ 树 - 您需要为您确定的对客户至关重要的每一项需求创建一棵。
确定客户的关键需求
通过创建对客户至关重要的需求列表来开始 CTQ 树流程。例如，从事在线支票访问流程处理的银行可能会将可访问性、用户友好界面和信息安全性视为对客户至关重要的主要需求。从广义上定义需求，以帮助在稍后的图表过程中捕获所有驱动因素和需求。

定义需求的最佳方法是直接询问客户反馈，但时间和资源并不总是允许进行调查。 六西格玛团队也许能够利用通过最近的调查或反馈表收集的数据，这是退而求其次的事情。在没有客户反馈的情况下，与一组了解客户并具有客户经验的员工一起集思广益，讨论关键需求。当客户是最终用户时，来自销售、客户服务和投诉部门的主题专家通常可以提供可行的信息。您还可以使用 SIPOC 图的输出开始构建 CTQ 树；根据您在 SIPOC 上构造输出的方式，您可能需要定义输出的关键质量因数作为 CTQ 树图的起点。

rows: 术语说明 SIPOC：供应商、输入、流程、输出、客户；用于快速界定流程边界。
zh.text: 术语说明 SIPOC：供应商、输入、流程、输出、客户；用于快速界定流程边界。
识别质量驱动因素
一旦您获得了关键需求列表，请一次处理一个需求，以创建类似于上图的树。 确定满足客户需求必须存在或满足的质量驱动因素。例如，暖通空调服务公司的客户可能需要优质的服务。满足这种需求的驱动因素可能包括友好的服务技术人员、乐于助人且知识渊博的员工以及对服务呼叫的及时响应。
驱动因素是客户需求和要求之间的过渡点；您不一定必须能够衡量驱动因素，但您希望它们比您已经确定的广泛客户需求更详细一些，并且您希望尽可能朝着可衡量因素的方向发展。
列出每个驱动程序的要求
需求是关于关键质量特性（CTQ）特征的最详细的细分。您可以通过这些指标来了解司机的表现是否适当，从而满足客户的需求。
例如，让我们看一下 CTQ 树格式的 HVAC 示例。
您可以在上面的 CTQ 树中看到驱动程序已转换为需求 - 并且每个需求都可以用数字来衡量。在某些情况下，驱动程序到需求的转换相当于一个硬数字。本章开头的巧克力棒示例描述了这样一个场景：如果公司认为含有四分之一杯糖的配方是正确的配方，那么质量的过程指标恰好是四分之一杯糖。
在其他示例中，公司可能会为例外情况提供余地，或者理解流程不会每次都达到确切的数字。例如，暖通空调团队不可能在接到电话后恰好 24 小时内到达客户家中 - 如果服务技术人员能够早于 24 小时到达，大多数人都会希望他们这样做。这意味着公司必须为需求创建一个定义：多少个小时后客户才会认为技术人员不合时宜？以我们的示例公司为例，该时间为 48 小时。另一种情况下的要求可能是 24 小时。
由于团队将使用 CTQ 树中的需求来开发流程测量和成功指标，因此在团队将每个需求纳入项目或流程之前对其进行审查非常重要。 应将要求与 VOC 数据、现有测量以及主题专家和领导者的经验和知识进行比较。团队应该问自己和其他人“如果满足这些要求，客户会满意吗？”如果答案是否定的，那么需求就需要改进。团队还可以考虑询问“这些要求在现实世界中是否可能”。如果答案是否定的，那么流程或需求都需要工作。

en.text: Six Sigma teams must always be aware that quality comes at a cost. When talking about quality costs, many organizations consider what is known as the cost of poor quality, or CoPQ. The cost of poor quality is defined as the costs or expenses associated with defects created by a process. Quality actually has a broader cost – avoiding poor quality comes at an expense as well. The cost of quality, or CoQ, covers the expenses associated with maintaining good quality throughout an organization or process. Sometimes, this is referred to as the cost of good quality. In this section, we’ll talk about both types of cost measurements, how they relate to Six Sigma in general, and how they relate to Six Sigma teams and projects.
The Cost of Poor Quality

In some ways, the cost of poor quality is easier to measure than the cost associated with overall quality. CoPQ is usually broken into two major categories: costs associated with external failures and costs associated with internal failures. External and internal failures are often referred to as the costs of nonconformity – they are the expenses that occur when outputs do not conform to critical to quality requirements.
External Failures

External failures usually occur after products or services have been delivered, which means they are directly associated with customer dissatisfaction. External failures might include revenue losses associated with a reduction in sales because of the quality of products, services, systems, or information. Other types of external losses include expenses associated with repairs, returns, or rework associated with a customer complaint; expenses associated with warranties; or loss of revenue or sales because of customer ill will or bad word-of-mouth.
Internal Failures

Internal failures occur when products, services, or processes don’t conform to the requirements set by the company, and the product or service is provided to the customer in an unsatisfactory fashion. Internal failures are usually handled by scrapping the work, redoing the work, or repairing the work. Obviously, such rework results in added material and labor costs, but it also results in losses associated with delays, shortages of parts or inventory, and lack of flexibility or the ability to adapt. For example, if a process has such poor quality that 50 percent of the items produced by it require rework, then the process might be producing 40 percent less on a daily basis than it could be. That means the process can serve fewer customers, generate less output, and contribute less overall to the company’s profit.
Calculating the Cost of Poor Quality

Understanding the cost of poor quality is critical to Six Sigma organizations because it lets leaders understand how financial needs are related to the need for quality improvements. The higher the cost of poor quality, the more likely an organization will work toward improvement.

At a project or process level, the cost of poor quality might help determine budgets for improvement. If poor quality within the process is costing an organization $5,000 a month, a project that costs $20,000 but saves $3,000 a month in quality would pay for itself in just seven months. On the other end, a
project that costs $100,000 when the costs of poor quality are only $1,000 a month is less likely to make sense.
The equation for CoPQ is:
CoPQ = External Failure Costs + Internal Failure Costs

While the equation seems simple, identifying all of the costs associated with poor quality can be difficult. Most experts use the metaphor of an iceberg to explain the hidden costs of poor quality. On the surface, you see the very small tip of the iceberg—the obvious costs of poor quality. These might be things such as scrap, reprocessing, warranty claims, customer returns, and extra shipping.
Beneath the surface, however, an iceberg is always much bigger. The same is usually true of the cost of poor quality, and hidden costs might include:
Loss of customer loyalty
Loss of morale
Loss of employees if morale remains low for extended periods
Conflicts associated with scheduling or rescheduling
Higher risks of compliance issues, including fines
Higher administrative costs
Unpredictable revenue, sales, or production

Calculating the cost of poor quality is extremely difficult on an enterprise-wide level and still moderately difficult on a process level. A method for listing all possible costs and formulizing them to dollar amounts doesn’t exist. It’s a good idea for organizations to develop a streamlined method that is used throughout the enterprise when calculating CoPQ. At the very least, Six Sigma experts in the organization might consider defining a specific way of listing costs of poor quality company-wide so that various process teams are using similar measures when they report to leadership.
The Cost of Quality

The cost of quality, or CoQ, includes the cost of poor quality and the cost of good quality. In addition to internal and external failure costs, CoQ includes prevention and appraisal costs. Prevention and appraisal costs are often referred to as the costs of conformity – they are the expenses related to ensuring outputs conform to critical to quality requirements.
Prevention Costs

The costs of prevention are the expenses that are related to any activity meant to stop an error or defect from occurring. Error-proofing, which is covered in detail in later chapters on controlling processes, results in prevention costs. For example, if a company produces baked goods, at some point in the process people or machines must measure ingredients to add to dough batches. One way to error-proof such a process is to provide specialized machinery that will only allow a specific amount of each ingredient to be introduced to a batch. Such a machine would likely be quite expensive; it would also have to be managed by a qualified operator and maintained by appropriate repair and cleaning staff. All of that activity would generate costs which might be considered preventative in nature.

Other types of prevention costs include expenses related to quality planning, reviews, or education and training focused on quality. Quality review and evaluation processes also create prevention costs, whether those reviews are related to suppliers, products, processes, or people. Customer surveys, the creation of technical manuals, work to create and manage requirements and specifications, and the management of job descriptions can all lead to prevention costs. Even housekeeping costs might be considered preventative costs, especially if a clean work environment is required to reduce flaws or errors in product manufacturing.
Appraisal Costs

Appraisal costs are those associated with any activity meant to ensure high levels of quality across a process or organization. If a manufacturing plant hires a quality control specialist, and that person’s job is to review parts that come down the manufacturing line and either return the work for correction or report the level of quality as a metric, then the salary of that person and any expenses related to his or her employment are appraisal costs. In some cases, those expenses might also be considered prevention costs, but they would not be counted twice when calculating CoQ.

Other types of appraisal costs might include expenses related to quality audits on products, services, or processes, the cost of calibration and measurement equipment or software, and the costs of field tests. Prototype inspections, consulting expenses, financial reporting and auditing, security checks, safety checks, supplier certifications, employee surveys, and customer feedback are all further examples of areas where appraisal costs might exist.
Calculating the Cost of Quality
The equation for CoQ is:
CoQ = CoPQ + Prevention Costs + Appraisal Costs

The same challenges inherent in calculating CoPQ also exist when calculating CoQ. The same iceberg analogy is relevant, and prevention and appraisal activities often have hidden costs such as unnecessary overtime, paperwork, or system expenses.
The Cost of Quality and Six Sigma

Traditional wisdom might say that if the cost of poor quality goes down, the cost of good quality is likely to go up. You have to spend money on quality to have good quality, in other words. While historically that might be true for many organizations, it is not the case in a Six Sigma company. Because Six Sigma works to create quality that is inherent in the process – meaning things are done right the first time and defects are reduced – the costs of quality often go down while quality itself goes up.

In Chapter 1, we showed that a process with a higher sigma level (and thus, higher quality) has fewer defects. Defects decrease in an exponential manner as sigma level rises. Because there are fewer defects, the costs of poor quality are exponentially reduced as well. But time and again, Six Sigma has also reduced the cost of overall quality. As the sigma level of processes is increased via the application of Six Sigma tools and methodology, the cost of both prevention and appraisal goes down as well.

One way of relating the cost of quality – and perhaps the most common way of doing so among corporations – is as a percent of sales. The cost of quality as a percent of sales typically aligns so closely with sigma values that you can predict the cost of quality based on a company’s or process’s sigma value. The average ranges for CoQ in relation to sigma values are shown in the table below. As you can see, as companies improve their sigma levels, they experience a substantial savings in the cost of quality.
Managing Cost of Quality

Six Sigma is one of the best methodologies for managing the cost of quality because it works to build quality into every process. When approaching an organization or process that has a high cost of quality, teams and leadership can apply a triage-based method to reduce those costs. While no organization can remove quality costs 100 percent, the goal should be zero costs of failure, either internal or external, and minimal preventative and appraisal costs.

First, teams should concentrate on costs associated with failures. It’s often easier and less expensive to detect costs associated with nonconformance, and improvements that seek to correct causes for a few critical failures can have a big impact on overall quality and total cost. Instead of adding layers of quality programs over processes to ensure quality – which only adds prevention or appraisal activities and increases the cost of quality – Six Sigma improvement projects build preventative measures into processes themselves. In other words, efficient Six Sigma processes are self-regulating. They have built in checks and balances that work to constantly reduce defects and rework.
The benefit of building failure stop-points into a process include:

Earlier detection when errors do occur, which keeps hidden costs down. When the error can’t make it to the next process or to the customer, you avoid many issues and costs associated with low morale, reduced customer loyalty, or product returns.

Employees are able to support and manage higher quality. When quality is something employees have ownership of, they are more likely to work hard to create the best possible output. In contrast, appraisal-style quality programs can spark feelings of paranoia at being closely watched or create a relationship in employee minds between the idea of quality and the idea of reprisal or correction. Poor performance on a continuous basis does need to be addressed, but employees should not default to a negative mindset when they hear the word quality.

In-process quality assurance is actually more effective than post-process or over-process prevention and appraisal methods. Statistical process control and Six Sigma improvements can push a process to six sigma level. To ensure the same level of performance – 3.4 defects per million opportunities – quality assurance employees would need to review millions of parts and ensure only a very tiny few had defects. It’s simply not an economical option for most, if any, organization.

After teams use the Six Sigma and Lean process management methods discussed throughout this book to reduce failure costs, teams can turn to prevention and appraisal costs. Often, in a process that is functioning at a high sigma level, prevention and appraisal activities are a form of muda. They can be expunged from the process without impacting the end product, quality, customer satisfaction, or employee morale. In some cases, removing prevention or appraisal from processes actually creates a positive impact on quality, production, and customer and employee satisfaction.
Identifying Prevention and Appraisal Activities

The first step to removing quality-related muda is identifying it. Process maps, spaghetti diagrams, and value stream maps are valuable tools for uncovering activities that don’t need to be included in a process. All of these tools are covered in depth in Unit 9.

Whether you’re mapping a process or simply discussing various components with process owners or a Six Sigma team, asking questions about value and necessity can also help identify muda of prevention and appraisal. If you think an activity related to a process might be an unnecessary form of prevention or appraisal, ask:
Does the activity itself add any value to the output?
Does the activity substantially reduce the time it takes for the process to produce an output?
Does the activity substantially increase the cost of the process?
If the activity is designed to prevent defects within the process, can the activity be made more efficient?
If the activity is designed to prevent defects, can the activity be made less expensive?
If an activity is designed to capture quality data about the process for reporting purposes, are those reports necessary?

If quality reports are necessary– either because of obligatory requirements such as compliance or because the reports provide value in another process – can the reports be automated to reduce associated expense?
The answers to these questions help teams identify areas where muda can be removed or where quality-related processes can be improved.

zh.text: 六西格玛团队必须时刻意识到，质量是有代价的。在谈论质量成本时，许多组织都会考虑所谓的劣质成本 (CoPQ)。低质量成本被定义为与流程产生的缺陷相关的成本或费用。质量实际上有更广泛的成本——避免低质量也需要付出代价。质量成本 (CoQ) 涵盖与在整个组织或流程中保持良好质量相关的费用。有时，这被称为优质成本。在本节中，我们将讨论这两种类型的成本衡量，它们与六西格玛的总体关系，以及它们与六西格玛团队和项目的关系。
质量差的成本
在某些方面，低质量的成本比与整体质量相关的成本更容易衡量。 CoPQ 通常分为两大类：与外部故障相关的成本和与内部故障相关的成本。外部和内部故障通常被称为不合格成本——它们是当产出不符合关键质量特性（CTQ）要求时发生的费用。
外部故障
外部故障通常发生在产品或服务交付后，这意味着它们与客户不满意直接相关。外部故障可能包括因产品、服务、系统或信息质量而导致销售额下降而导致的收入损失。其他类型的外部损失包括与客户投诉相关的维修、退货或返工相关的费用；与保修相关的费用；由于客户恶意或不良口碑而导致收入或销售损失。
内部故障

当产品、服务或流程不符合公司设定的要求，并且以不满意的方式向客户提供产品或服务时，就会发生内部故障。内部故障通常通过报废、重做或修复工作来处理。显然，这种返工会增加材料和劳动力成本，但也会导致与延误、零件或库存短缺以及缺乏灵活性或适应能力相关的损失。例如，如果某个流程的质量很差，以至于其生产的产品中有 50% 需要返工，那么该流程的日产量可能会比实际产量少 40%。这意味着该流程可以服务更少的客户，产生更少的产出，并且对公司利润的总体贡献更少。
计算低质量的成本
了解低质量的成本对于六西格玛组织至关重要，因为它可以让领导者了解财务需求与质量改进需求之间的关系。质量差的成本越高，组织就越有可能致力于改进。
在项目或流程层面，质量差的成本可能有助于确定改进预算。如果流程中的质量问题导致组织每月损失 5,000 美元，那么成本为 20,000 美元但每月在质量方面节省 3,000 美元的项目将在短短 7 个月内收回成本。在另一端，一个
项目成本为 100,000 美元，而低质量成本每月仅为 1,000 美元，则不太可能有意义。
CoPQ 的方程式为：
CoPQ = 外部故障成本 + 内部故障成本
虽然等式看起来很简单，但确定与低质量相关的所有成本可能很困难。大多数专家使用冰山的比喻来解释低质量的隐性成本。从表面上看，你看到的是冰山很小的一角——明显的劣质成本。这些可能包括报废、再加工、保修索赔、客户退货和额外运费等。
然而，在表面之下，冰山总是要大得多。低质量成本通常也是如此，隐性成本可能包括：
客户忠诚度丧失
士气低落
如果士气长时间低迷，就会导致员工流失
与安排或重新安排相关的冲突
合规问题（包括罚款）的风险较高
行政成本较高
不可预测的收入、销售额或产量
计算低质量的成本在整个企业层面上是极其困难的，但在流程层面上仍然是中等难度的。不存在列出所有可能成本并将其表述为美元金额的方法。对于组织来说，在计算 CoPQ 时开发一种在整个企业中使用的简化方法是一个好主意。至少，组织中的六西格玛专家可以考虑定义一种特定的方式来列出全公司范围内的低质量成本，以便各个流程团队在向领导汇报时使用类似的措施。
质量成本
质量成本（CoQ）包括劣质成本和优质成本。除了内部和外部故障成本之外，CoQ 还包括预防和评估成本。预防和评估成本通常被称为合格成本——它们是与确保产出符合关键质量特性（CTQ）要求相关的费用。
预防成本

预防成本是与旨在阻止错误或缺陷发生的任何活动相关的费用。防错会产生预防成本，稍后有关控制过程的章节将对此进行详细介绍。例如，如果一家公司生产烘焙食品，在该过程中的某个时刻，人员或机器必须测量成分以添加到面团批次中。防止这种过程出错的一种方法是提供专门的机器，只允许将特定数量的每种成分引入批次中。这样的机器可能会非常昂贵；它还必须由合格的操作员管理，并由适当的维修和清洁人员维护。所有这些活动都会产生成本，这些成本本质上可能被认为是预防性的。
其他类型的预防成本包括与质量规划、审查或以质量为重点的教育和培训相关的费用。 质量审查和评估流程也会产生预防成本，无论这些审查是与供应商、产品、流程还是人员相关。客户调查、技术手册的创建、创建和管理需求和规范的工作以及工作描述的管理都可能导致预防成本。甚至家政成本也可能被视为预防性成本，特别是如果需要清洁的工作环境来减少产品制造中的缺陷或错误。
评估费用
评估成本是与旨在确保整个流程或组织的高水平质量的任何活动相关的成本。如果制造工厂雇用了一名质量控制专家，并且该人的工作是检查生产线上的零件，并将工作退回进行更正或报告质量水平作为指标，那么该人的工资以及与其就业相关的任何费用都是评估成本。在某些情况下，这些费用也可能被视为预防成本，但在计算 CoQ 时不会被重复计算。
其他类型的评估成本可能包括与产品、服务或流程的质量审核相关的费用、校准和测量设备或软件的成本以及现场测试的成本。原型检查、咨询费用、财务报告和审计、安全检查、安全检查、供应商认证、员工调查和客户反馈都是可能存在评估成本的领域的进一步示例。
计算质量成本
CoQ 的方程式为：
CoQ = CoPQ + 预防成本 + 评估成本
计算 CoQ 时也存在计算 CoPQ 所固有的相同挑战。同样的冰山类比是相关的，预防和评估活动通常具有隐性成本，例如不必要的加班、文书工作或系统费用。
质量成本与六西格玛
传统观点可能会说，如果低质量的成本下降，高质量的成本可能会上升。换句话说，你必须在质量上花钱才能获得好的质量。虽然从历史上看，许多组织可能都是如此，但六西格玛公司的情况并非如此。 因为六西格玛致力于创造流程中固有的质量——这意味着事情第一次就做对了，缺陷也减少了——质量成本往往会下降，而质量本身会上升。
在第一章中，我们表明西格玛水平较高（因此质量较高）的流程缺陷较少。随着西格玛水平的提高，缺陷以指数方式减少。由于缺陷较少，质量差的成本也成倍降低。但六西格玛也一次又一次地降低了整体质量的成本。随着六西格玛工具和方法的应用提高了流程的西格玛水平，预防和评估的成本也随之下降。

rows: 术语说明 Sigma level（西格玛水平）：衡量过程缺陷率的尺度；水平越高，单位机会中产生缺陷的概率越低。
zh.text: 术语说明 Sigma level（西格玛水平）：衡量过程缺陷率的尺度；水平越高，单位机会中产生缺陷的概率越低。
将质量成本联系起来的一种方法——也许是企业中最常见的方法——是占销售额的百分比。质量成本占销售额的百分比通常与西格玛值密切相关，您可以根据公司或流程的西格玛值来预测质量成本。下表显示了 CoQ 与 sigma 值相关的平均范围。正如您所看到的，随着公司提高西格玛水平，他们的质量成本大幅节省。
管理质量成本
六西格玛是管理质量成本的最佳方法之一，因为它致力于将质量融入到每个流程中。当处理质量成本较高的组织或流程时，团队和领导层可以应用基于分类的方法来降低这些成本。虽然没有组织可以 100% 消除质量成本，但目标应该是零失败成本（无论是内部还是外部）以及最小的预防和评估成本。
首先，团队应该关注与失败相关的成本。检测与不合格相关的成本通常更容易、更便宜，而寻求纠正一些关键故障原因的改进可能会对整体质量和总成本产生重大影响。六西格玛改进项目不是在流程上增加层层质量计划来确保质量——这只会增加预防或评估活动并增加质量成本——而是将预防措施纳入流程本身。换句话说，高效的六西格玛流程是自我调节的。他们建立了制衡机制，不断减少缺陷和返工。
将故障停止点构建到流程中的好处包括：
及早发现错误确实发生，从而降低隐性成本。当错误无法进入下一个流程或客户时，您可以避免与士气低落、客户忠诚度降低或产品退货相关的许多问题和成本。
员工能够支持和管理更高的质量。当员工拥有质量时，他们更有可能努力工作以创造最佳产出。相比之下，评估式的质量计划可能会引发因受到密切关注而产生的偏执感，或者在员工心中建立质量观念与报复或纠正观念之间的关系。持续表现不佳确实需要解决，但员工在听到“质量”一词时不应默认抱有消极心态。
过程中的质量保证实际上比过程后或过程中的预防和评估方法更有效。统计过程控制和六西格玛改进可以将流程提升到六西格玛水平。为了确保相同水平的性能（每百万个机会中有 3.4 个缺陷），质量保证员工需要检查数百万个零件并确保只有极少数存在缺陷。对于大多数组织（如果有的话）来说，这根本不是一个经济的选择。

rows: 术语说明 SPC（统计过程控制）：用统计方法监控过程表现，区分普通波动和异常信号。
zh.text: 术语说明 SPC（统计过程控制）：用统计方法监控过程表现，区分普通波动和异常信号。
在团队使用本书讨论的六西格玛和精益流程管理方法来降低失败成本后，团队可以转向预防和评估成本。通常，在高西格玛水平运行的过程中，预防和评估活动是 Muda 的一种形式。它们可以从流程中删除，而不会影响最终产品、质量、客户满意度或员工士气。在某些情况下，从流程中取消预防或评估实际上会对质量、生产以及客户和员工满意度产生积极影响。
识别预防和评估活动
消除与质量相关的 Muda 的第一步是识别它。流程图、意大利面条图和价值流图是发现流程中不需要包含的活动的宝贵工具。所有这些工具都将在第 9 单元中进行深入介绍。

rows: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
zh.text: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
无论您是在绘制流程，还是只是与流程负责人或六西格玛团队讨论各个组成部分，提出有关价值和必要性的问题也可以帮助识别预防和评估的误区。如果您认为与流程相关的活动可能是不必要的预防或评估形式，请询问：
活动本身是否能为产出增加任何价值？
该活动是否大幅减少了流程产生输出所需的时间？
该活动是否大幅增加了流程成本？
如果该活动旨在防止流程中的缺陷，是否可以提高该活动的效率？
如果该活动旨在防止缺陷，是否可以降低该活动的成本？
如果一项活动旨在捕获有关流程的质量数据以用于报告目的，那么这些报告是否必要？
如果质量报告是必要的——无论是因为合规性等强制性要求，还是因为报告在另一个流程中提供了价值——报告是否可以自动化以减少相关费用？
这些问题的答案可帮助团队确定可以消除 Muda 的领域或可以改进质量相关流程的领域。

en.text: When Six Sigma teams are expunging quality-related costs and unnecessary activities from processes, it is critical that they don’t actually remove quality. While it’s true that traditional quality programs and costs don’t have to be present to ensure a reduction in defects and an improvement in customer satisfaction, it’s equally true that you have to replace those programs with some other form of control. By the end of this book, you will have learned about a number of tools, from statistical process control to poka yokes, which you can use to create quality within a process.

It’s also worth noting that a single Six Sigma team – or even an entire department devoted to Six Sigma – can’t reduce the costs of quality in an organization on their own. Corporate leadership must buy into the belief that quality is better when controls are incorporated within the process, and they have to be willing to communicate this fact via training and example. Some companies choose instead to use Six Sigma to improve processes while maintaining the expense of traditional quality, compliance, and audit departments. For some industries, such as healthcare or finance, audits and other appraisal and prevention costs might be mandated by laws and regulations. Outside of that mandate, it’s almost always best to remove any quality activity that doesn’t provide additional value.

zh.text: 当六西格玛团队从流程中消除与质量相关的成本和不必要的活动时，至关重要的是他们不会真正消除质量。虽然确实不必存在传统的质量计划和成本来确保减少缺陷和提高客户满意度，但同样正确的是，您必须用其他形式的控制来取代这些计划。读完本书后，您将了解从统计过程控制到防错的许多工具，您可以使用它们在流程中创建质量。

还值得注意的是，单个六西格玛团队，甚至整个部门致力于六西格玛，无法仅凭一己之力降低组织的质量成本。企业领导层必须相信，当将控制纳入流程中时，质量会更好，并且他们必须愿意通过培训和示例来传达这一事实。 一些公司选择使用六西格玛来改进流程，同时维持传统质量、合规和审计部门的费用。对于某些行业，例如医疗保健或金融，法律法规可能会强制规定审计和其他评估和预防成本。除了该任务之外，最好总是删除任何不提供额外价值的质量活动。

title.zh: 第 9 章：选择正确的项目
