en.text: Value stream mapping is similar, but in some ways different, to process mapping. Value stream mapping is a tool perfected by lean manufacturing and works best in processes that are manufacturing, delivery, shipping, or factory oriented. However, value stream mapping can be useful in a variety of other industries if the Six Sigma expert understands the purpose of the exercise and how to translate the method into his or her process.
What is Value Stream Mapping?

Value stream mapping is a pictorial representation, including the addition of numerical data, of the value stream of product or ideas. When used properly, value stream mapping provides Six Sigma teams with the big picture of a process, lets teams understand what the process looks like today, helps teams create a vision for improving a process, and links the flow of materials, people, and information in one image. A value stream map also helps break down communication barriers because the symbology used tends to be similar or at least intuitive; as such, it makes it easier for teams and support staff to understand where waste – or muda – is occurring in a process.
Evaluating the Seven Flows

A value stream map is one of the few tools that truly captures all of the flow that occurs in a process. It’s possible to capture some information about all of the major seven flows on a value stream map, though most value stream maps concentrate most on raw material, parts, and products than on the other four types of flow. The seven types of flow are:
People
Raw material
Parts
Products
Equipment
Information
Engineering

zh.text: 价值流图与流程图相似，但在某些方面有所不同。价值流图是一种通过精益制造完善的工具，在制造、交付、运输或工厂导向的流程中效果最佳。然而，如果六西格玛专家了解练习的目的以及如何将该方法转化为他或她的流程，那么价值流图可以在其他各种行业中发挥作用。
什么是价值流图？
价值流图是产品或创意价值流的图形表示，包括添加数字数据。如果使用得当，价值流图可以为六西格玛团队提供流程的全局图景，让团队了解当前的流程是什么样子，帮助团队制定改进流程的愿景，并将物料流、人员流和信息流链接到一个图像中。价值流图还有助于打破沟通障碍，因为所使用的符号系统往往是相似的或至少是直观的；因此，它使团队和支持人员更容易了解流程中何处出现浪费（或 Muda）。
评估七种流程
价值流图是真正捕获流程中发生的所有流程的少数工具之一。尽管大多数价值流图主要集中在原材料、零件和产品上，而不是其他四种类型的流，但可以在价值流图上捕获有关所有主要七种流的一些信息。七种流类型是：
人
原料
零件
产品展示
设备
信息
工程
价值流图符号系统

en.text: Value stream maps use different symbols than most process maps do, and the symbols tend to be more specific. For example, if the value stream involves the delivery of goods via truck, the map includes an actual picture of a truck – usually with a text indication of how many times the shipments occur in a given period.

The image above indicates one truck shipment per week. A number of other common value stream map symbols are included below. You can download common symbols for Excel from www.lean.org/ common/display/?o=866 to create value stream maps in Excel. You can also use a value stream map software to create a map.

Note that value stream mapping doesn’t require the use of these exact symbols, especially if you are using the concept of value stream mapping in an industry where such symbols are less useful. You could use the value stream concept to map the workflow in an emergency room department, for example, where different symbols would make more sense. Consider these symbols as a starting point.

The manufacturing process box indicates a specific action in the production process. The name of the action goes in the top part of the box – in this case, “press.” In the bottom, you can put text notes or illustrations as desired. One common use of the bottom section of the process box is indicating how much time occurs during that particular step.
Outside sources are either suppliers or customers. Use this shape to indicate when inputs come from outside the organization or process or when outputs go to the end customer of the process.
Data boxes are important because they house the analytical meat of the value stream map. Common information recorded in data boxes include:
Cycle Time, or C/T. Cycle time is the time it takes for the process as a whole – or a step within the process – to complete one iteration.
Changeover Time, C/T. Changeover time is the time it takes for a change in shift, tools, or other resources in the process or a single step within the process.
Number of operators
Number of shifts
Time worked in a shift
First-pass yield quality
Batch sizes

Takt time, which is the rate at which products must be finished to meet the demand of the customer. Takt time for an individual step in the process might be seen as the time in which the step needs to be finished to keep from slowing down the process.

The inventory box indicates that inventory usually stacks up at a certain point in the process. It is usually coupled with text that says how much inventory is available in amount, time, or both. You might note that there are 100 pieces of inventory regularly at that point in the process. You might note that there are two-day’s worth of inventory at that point in the process; you could note both.

A push arrow indicates that something – either product or information – is pushed from one part of the process to another part of the process. The push arrow means the product or information is generated by that part of the process regardless of the need for it in the downstream parts of the process.
The opposite of a push arrow would be a pull indicator, which means that downstream processes pull inventory, parts, or information as needed from upstream locations.
The finished goods arrow indicates that the output of the process is being pushed or delivered to the customer – whether that customer is internal, external, or another process.

The FIFO arrow indicates that this part of the process features a first-in, first-out sequence, which is important in some processes. Consider processes that deal with food ingredients; if a recipe in a manufacturing plant calls for milk, then the operators should pull the oldest (still good) milk from storage first to keep from wasting product that goes bad while in inventory.

The supermarket is an area in the process where small amounts of inventory are stored. Downstream processes can stock as needed from the supermarket instead of stocking from the larger inventory supply, which might be more difficult to access. An upstream process feeds the supermarket, ensuring enough inventory is stocked. An example of a supermarket might be seen in a large office. One team might have a drawer where supplies, such as paper, pens, paperclips, and staples, are kept. The team can pull from that drawer instead of requisitioning from the larger stock room or from the actual office supply store every time supplies are needed.
The physical pull symbol indicates that product or materials have to be physically pulled from the previous step, station, or supermarket to the next step.

The move-by-forklift symbol is self-explanatory, though not always necessary in every process. You might, however, have a symbol for other types of movement, such as move by hand cart or conveyor belt. The only time you need to include specifications about how items are moved is when those details might become important to the process analysis.
This is also a self-explanatory symbol and also not necessary in every process. You might, instead, have train, plane, or even bike shipments listed on your value stream map.

The type of information indicated by the straight manual flow arrow is typically communicated via memos, face-to-face speaking, phone calls, and reports. The manual information arrow might be accompanied by notes regarding the type of information and the frequency with which it is delivered.

The crooked electronic info flow arrow indicates information that is electronic in nature, such as information communication via Internet, portals, EDI, and automated reporting systems. The type of data and the frequency with which it is delivered can also be included with this symbol.

The withdrawal Kanban shape indicates that there is a Kanban card or signal at that process step. The Kanban card instructs the operator at that particular step to withdraw inventory from a supermarket or other stock location.

The production Kanban shape indicates that a production Kanban card or signal is located at that part of the process. This card tells the operator to produce a certain number of parts to feed a process that is downstream.

The safety stock icon indicates that a “just-in-case” storage of inventory exists at this point in the process. Safety stock is not like a supermarket – it is not intended to be a permanent storage of inventory. Instead, it is a temporary storage of inventory that reduces the chance that downtime or other issues upstream will keep all the downstream processes from occurring. For example, in a fast food restaurant, someone stocks the cup and drink dispenser each morning. These stocks are not meant to be the permanent storage for those items, but a smaller number of items are kept at hand so employees can quickly supply drinks to consumers.

The operator shape indicates a human operator or employee within the process. You don’t have to include the operator shape in every diagram where people are – in some cases, the nature of the value stream map allows readers to assume people are part of the process. However, if automated processes are included amid people-powered processes, this symbol can be used for clarity where needed.

The schedule box is simply a text box that lets you note how work, orders, or other parts of the process are scheduled. You can couple the box along with arrows to show that orders are sent weekly, for example, or that a production schedule for staff is created each month.

zh.text: 价值流图使用与大多数流程图不同的符号，并且符号往往更具体。例如，如果价值流涉及通过卡车运送货物，则地图包含卡车的实际图片 - 通常带有文本指示在给定时期内发生了多少次运输。

rows: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
zh.text: 术语说明 Process Map（流程图）：把流程步骤、流向和责任可视化，帮助识别断点和浪费。
上图显示每周一卡车发货。下面包括许多其他常见的价值流图符号。您可以从 www.lean.org/common/display/?o=866 下载 Excel 的常用符号，以在 Excel 中创建价值流图。 您还可以使用价值流图软件来创建地图。
请注意，价值流映射不需要使用这些精确的符号，特别是当您在此类符号不太有用的行业中使用价值流映射的概念时。例如，您可以使用价值流概念来绘制急诊室部门的工作流程，其中不同的符号更有意义。将这些符号视为起点。
制造过程框表示生产过程中的具体动作。操作的名称位于框的顶部 - 在本例中为“按”。在底部，您可以根据需要放置文字注释或插图。流程框底部的一个常见用途是指示在该特定步骤中发生了多少时间。
外部来源是供应商或客户。使用此形状来指示输入何时来自组织或流程外部，或者输出何时到达流程的最终客户。
数据框很重要，因为它们包含价值流图的分析内容。数据框中记录的常见信息包括：
周期时间，或 C/T。周期时间是整个流程（或流程中的一个步骤）完成一次迭代所需的时间。
转换时间，C/T。转换时间是指流程中班次、工具或其他资源或流程中单个步骤发生变化所需的时间。
操作人员数量
班次数量
时间轮班工作
一次合格率质量
批量大小
节拍时间，即为满足客户需求而必须完成产品的速度。流程中单个步骤的节拍时间可能被视为需要完成该步骤以避免减慢流程的时间。
库存框表示库存通常会在流程中的某个时刻堆积起来。它通常与说明可用库存数量、时间或两者兼而有之的文本结合在一起。您可能会注意到，流程中此时经常有 100 件库存。您可能会注意到，在此过程中，此时有两天的库存量；你可以同时注意两者。
推箭头表示某些东西（产品或信息）从流程的一个部分推到流程的另一部分。推箭头表示产品或信息由流程的该部分生成，而不管流程的下游部分是否需要它。
与推箭头相反的是拉指示器，这意味着下游流程根据需要从上游位置拉库存、零件或信息。
成品箭头表示流程的输出正在推送或交付给客户 - 无论该客户是内部、外部还是其他流程。
FIFO 箭头表示这部分流程具有先进先出的顺序，这在某些流程中很重要。考虑处理食品成分的流程；如果制造工厂的配方需要牛奶，那么操作员应该首先从存储中取出最旧的（仍然是好的）牛奶，以防止浪费在库存期间变质的产品。
超市是流程中存放少量库存的区域。下游流程可以根据需要从超市进行库存，而不是从较大的库存供应中进行库存，因为后者可能更难以获取。上游流程为超市提供原料，确保有足够的库存。超市的例子可以在大型办公室中看到。一个团队可能有一个抽屉，用来存放纸张、笔、回形针和订书钉等用品。每次需要用品时，团队可以从抽屉中取出，而不是从更大的储藏室或实际的办公用品商店申请。
物理拉动符号表示产品或材料必须从上一个步骤、站点或超市物理拉动到下一步。
叉车移动符号是不言自明的，但在每个过程中并不总是必需的。但是，您可能有其他类型移动的符号，例如用手推车或传送带移动。您唯一需要包含有关如何移动项目的规范的时候是这些细节可能对流程分析变得很重要的时候。
这也是一个不言自明的符号，也不是每个过程中都必需的。相反，您的价值流地图上可能会列出火车、飞机甚至自行车运输。
直接手动流程箭头指示的信息类型通常通过备忘录、面对面讲话、电话和报告进行传达。手动信息箭头可能附有有关信息类型及其传递频率的注释。
弯曲的电子信息流箭头表示本质上是电子的信息，例如通过互联网、门户、EDI和自动报告系统进行的信息通信。该符号还可以包含数据类型及其传送频率。
提款看板形状表明该流程步骤有看板卡或信号。看板卡指示操作员在该特定步骤从超市或其他库存地点提取库存。

rows: 术语说明 Kanban（看板）：用可视化信号控制工作流、库存或任务状态。
zh.text: 术语说明 Kanban（看板）：用可视化信号控制工作流、库存或任务状态。
生产看板形状表明生产看板卡或信号位于流程的该部分。该卡告诉操作员生产一定数量的零件来供给下游流程。
安全库存图标表示流程中此时存在“以防万一”的库存存储。安全库存不像超市——它的目的不是永久储存库存。相反，它是库存的临时存储，可以减少上游停机或其他问题导致所有下游流程发生的可能性。例如，在一家快餐店，有人每天早上都会储备杯子和饮水机。这些库存并不是为了永久存储这些物品，而是保留少量物品，以便员工可以快速向消费者提供饮料。
操作员形状表示流程中的操作员或员工。您不必在每个人员所在的图表中都包含运算符形状 - 在某些情况下，价值流图的性质允许读者假设人员是流程的一部分。但是，如果自动化流程包含在人员驱动的流程中，则可以在需要时使用此符号以保持清晰。
计划框只是一个文本框，可让您记录如何计划工作、订单或流程的其他部分。例如，您可以将该框与箭头结合起来，以显示每周发送订单，或者每月为员工创建一个生产计划。

en.text: Creating a value stream map is very different from creating a process map. One point of value stream mapping is that it forces you to really experience the process, which means that committee-creation of value stream maps isn’t going to provide the best outcome. The entire team can get involved in value stream mapping, if you as the Six Sigma expert think that is valuable, but the best results often come when everyone starts with their own individual value stream map. This is also a good process for the Six Sigma experts in a team, because it forces each one to view the process individually.

While you can use the icons above and numerous software programs to create a final copy of your value stream map, use paper and pencil for your first drafts. This lets you record information as you walk through the process, changing it quickly as you go.

When creating process maps, you often concentrate on the process, the employees, and the requirements. When creating value stream maps, you should always concentrate most on the customer and the product.

Physically walk the process whenever possible instead of sitting at a computer or working with a brainstorming session. Some experts recommend walking the process backwards; others say start at the beginning – find a method that works best for you. Don’t try to map every single part of the process, especially if you are mapping a large-scale production process. Instead, follow the major raw materials through to the outputs. If you put all the processes on a single map, it becomes too hard to read and you lose the value of the tool.

While you might eventually create a value stream map of a desired future state, start by mapping the way things are. Even if you see they aren’t working, record the actual process. Use real-time data for the value stream map whenever possible. For example, don’t use historical production and changeover times; when you walk the process, use a stopwatch to record your own observations.

zh.text: 创建价值流图与创建流程图有很大不同。价值流图的一点是它迫使你真正体验这个过程，这意味着委员会创建的价值流图不会提供最好的结果。整个团队都可以参与价值流图绘制，如果你作为六西格玛专家认为这是有价值的，但最好的结果往往是当每个人都从自己的个人价值流图开始时。对于团队中的六西格玛专家来说，这也是一个很好的流程，因为它迫使每个人都单独查看流程。
虽然您可以使用上面的图标和许多软件程序来创建价值流图的最终副本，但请使用纸和铅笔来绘制初稿。这使您可以在整个过程中记录信息，并在过程中快速更改它。
创建流程图时，您通常会关注流程、员工和需求。创建价值流图时，您应该始终最关注客户和产品。
尽可能亲自走动这个过程，而不是坐在电脑前或进行头脑风暴。一些专家建议倒着走这个过程；其他人说从头开始——找到最适合你的方法。不要尝试绘制流程的每个部分，尤其是在绘制大规模生产流程时。相反，要跟踪主要原材料直至产出。如果将所有流程放在一张地图上，就会变得难以阅读，并且会失去该工具的价值。
虽然您最终可能会创建所需未来状态的价值流图，但首先要绘制事物的现状。即使您发现它们不起作用，也要记录实际过程。尽可能使用实时数据来绘制价值流图。例如，不要使用历史生产和转换时间；当你走这个过程时，用秒表记录你自己的观察结果。

en.text: Begin value stream mapping by selecting the product family or process you are concerned with. In a manufacturing environment, you might select product type C and only concern yourself with that product. For example, a toy factory might make dolls, doll houses, and toy cars, but the Six Sigma team

might only be concerned with doll houses. In fact, the Six Sigma team might only be concerned with the doors that are made for the doll houses – you decide what scope of value stream map makes sense for your project.
Next, collect as much relevant data on the current state of the process as possible. Do this by walking the process and taking notes, reviewing actual data, and speaking with subject matter experts.
Create a Value Stream Map Drawing

To create an example of a value stream map while going through the following steps, we’ll consider a simple real-world example. In our example, a factory makes crayons. The Six Sigma team is concerned with the process that makes the 8-pack of primary colored crayons.
The value stream map will need to include information such as:
The suppliers of raw goods (wax, dye, and paper)
Wax melting
Dye addition
Pouring into molds to create crayon shapes
Inspection points
Wrapping crayons with appropriate paper
Packing crayons into boxes of eight
Shipping to final customer -- in this case, retail stores

1. Begin with the major process steps in the value stream. These are indicated by process boxes and are joined in a left-to-right line by the appropriate arrows – often by push arrows. For our example process, let’s assume a few basic process steps:

a. The wax is melted and dye is added b. Wax is poured into molds c. Molds are emptied d. Inspection occurs e. Shaped crayons are wrapped with matching colored paper f. Crayons are packed in boxes g. Shipping

Above, you can see a rough sketch of the process part of the value stream map. Kanban cards or signals tell employees when to pull wax and dye from the supermarket inventory. (The signal might be a light that the previous batch has been processed and the machines have returned to process start

parameters). The employees add the ingredients and start the first piece of the process, which is automated after the initial ingredient measurements. The wax is melted, the dye is mixed in, the colored wax is poured into molds, and the mold sets for 10 minutes before crayons are emptied to the inspection station.

You’ll note that the arrows connecting the first processes are different, because we want to show that they are automated and the process simply runs together unless someone intervenes in that batch. The rest of the processes have push arrows, because inspection, paper addition, and packing don’t operate on a batch process and work as long as inventory is flowing through.
2. Add the important aspects from outside of the process, including process controls, supplies, customers, and shipments.
3. Add data boxes for each part of the process.

4. Add inventory signals and any other information you think would be pertinent for the value stream map. For example, in reviewing the crayon process used in the example, the Six Sigma expert might note that inventory builds up before the packing process because it is slower than the inspection and paper-wrapping process. That could be indicated with an inventory signal and text.

You can also add controls for the process. In this case, the retailer places orders one month ahead for how many boxes it will need each week in the next month. The crayon-making company creates a monthly forecast, but orders once a week from suppliers. Suppliers deliver in multiple batches a week. Production control manages every part of the process with scheduling to keep up with the demands of the retailers.
Finally, add a timeline at the bottom that notes the time it takes for a single item to process through the enter process, breaking the time into value added and non-value added.

In the above example, the yellow portions are value added. They represent time that the product is actually being made or changed. The white portions are the setup, lead times, and inventory wait times – and this particular process is for a single color of crayons and doesn’t take into account any time spent preparing machines for changing colors.
You can add up the times to see that the total process time is 194 minutes or 3.23 hours.
The value added time is 19 minutes, so the team can assume there is definitely waste that can be removed from this process.

Remember, value stream maps aren’t supposed to be formal documents – they are working pictures of the process to help you and the rest of a Six Sigma team better understand the process and related challenges. So, you can add as much or as little information as you think is necessary. You can also come back and add information later if needed. The first draft of a value stream map, whether using pen and paper or a computer program, is probably going to be messy, and that’s okay. In fact, that’s a sign that you are doing it right. You can always make a clean, final copy for inclusion in presentations and training documents if desired.
What Do You Do with Value Stream Maps?

Value stream mapping is a helpful tool for all of the DMAIC phases. During Define, value stream mapping as an activity forces you to become involved with the process at a physical and daily level, which can boost your understanding of the process you are working to improve. It also provides the entire team with another visual that helps when discussing the process and the problem. A good value stream map lets the team visualize exactly where the process and problem might occur with respect to overall production.

Creating a value stream map means you’ve already conducted some measurement, creating a foundation for the Measure phase. The value stream map also points to measurement and data collection points that can be further used in Measure, though teams should never limit themselves to just the first types of information gathered in value stream mapping.

During Analyze, value stream maps are a tool that helps teams brainstorm and identify root causes or problem points in a process, and you can use the initial value stream map to identify activity or resources that don’t provide value – those that create muda in the process. Finally, during Improve, teams can begin creating a future state value stream map, building off the old map and using the information and solutions they have come up with through the DMAIC process. By putting those solutions on paper in the form of a value stream map, teams can better understand where issues might arise and alter solutions appropriately to reduce the number of issues experienced during implementation and beyond.

zh.text: 通过选择您关心的产品系列或流程来开始价值流图绘制。在制造环境中，您可以选择产品类型 C 并且只关心该产品。例如，玩具厂可能生产娃娃、娃娃屋、玩具车，但六西格玛团队
可能只关心玩具屋。 事实上，六西格玛团队可能只关心为娃娃屋制作的门——您可以决定价值流图的哪个范围对您的项目有意义。

rows: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
zh.text: 术语说明 Scope（项目范围）：说明改进项目包括什么、不包括什么，避免目标扩张。
接下来，收集尽可能多的有关流程当前状态的相关数据。通过走遍整个过程并做笔记、审查实际数据以及与主题专家交谈来做到这一点。
创建价值流图
为了在执行以下步骤时创建价值流图示例，我们将考虑一个简单的现实示例。在我们的示例中，一家工厂生产蜡笔。六西格玛团队负责8支装原色蜡笔的制作过程。
价值流图需要包括以下信息：
原材料供应商（蜡、染料和纸张）
蜡熔
染料添加
倒入模具中以形成蜡笔形状
检查点
用合适的纸包裹蜡笔
将蜡笔装入八盒中
运送给最终客户——在本例中为零售店
1. 从价值流中的主要流程步骤开始。这些由流程框指示，并通过适当的箭头（通常是推动箭头）连接在从左到右的线上。对于我们的示例流程，我们假设几个基本流程步骤：
a.蜡熔化并添加染料 b．将蜡倒入模具中 C.模具被清空 d．检查发生 e. f. 形状蜡笔用相配的彩色纸包裹。蜡笔装在盒子 g 中。运输
在上面，您可以看到价值流图的流程部分的粗略草图。看板卡或信号告诉员工何时从超市库存中取出蜡和染料。 （该信号可能是一个指示灯，表明前一批已处理完毕，并且机器已返回到处理开始状态
参数）。员工添加成分并开始流程的第一部分，该流程在初始成分测量后自动完成。蜡熔化，混合染料，将彩色蜡倒入模具中，模具固定 10 分钟，然后将蜡笔清空到检查站。
您会注意到，连接第一个流程的箭头是不同的，因为我们想表明它们是自动化的，并且流程只是一起运行，除非有人干预该批次。其余流程都有推动箭头，因为检查、纸张添加和包装不会在批处理流程中运行，并且只要库存在流动就可以工作。
2. 添加流程外部的重要方面，包括流程控制、供应、客户和发货。
3. 为流程的每个部分添加数据框。
4. 添加库存信号以及您认为与价值流图相关的任何其他信息。例如，在审查示例中使用的蜡笔流程时，六西格玛专家可能会注意到库存在包装流程之前就已积累，因为它比检查和包装流程慢。这可以通过库存信号和文本来指示。
您还可以为流程添加控件。在这种情况下，零售商提前一个月下订单，确定下个月每周需要多少个盒子。这家蜡笔制造公司每月都会进行预测，但每周都会向供应商订购一次。供应商每周分多批交货。生产控制通过调度来管理流程的每个部分，以满足零售商的需求。
最后，在底部添加一个时间线，记录单个项目通过输入过程进行处理所需的时间，将时间分为增值时间和非增值时间。
在上面的例子中，黄色部分是增值的。它们代表产品实际制造或更改的时间。白色部分是设置、交货时间和库存等待时间——这个特定的过程是针对单色蜡笔的，没有考虑到准备机器改变颜色所花费的任何时间。
您可以将时间相加，发现总处理时间为 194 分钟或 3.23 小时。
增值时间为 19 分钟，因此团队可以假设这个过程中肯定存在可以消除的浪费。
请记住，价值流图不应该是正式文件——它们是流程的工作图片，可以帮助您和六西格玛团队的其他成员更好地理解流程和相关挑战。 因此，您可以根据需要添加尽可能多或尽可能少的信息。如果需要，您也可以稍后返回并添加信息。价值流图的初稿，无论是使用笔和纸还是计算机程序，可能会很混乱，但这没关系。事实上，这表明你做得对。如果需要，您始终可以制作一份干净的最终副本，以便包含在演示文稿和培训文档中。
您如何使用价值流图？
价值流图是适用于所有 DMAIC 阶段的有用工具。在定义过程中，价值流图作为一项活动迫使您在实际和日常层面上参与该流程，这可以增进您对正在努力改进的流程的理解。它还为整个团队提供了另一种视觉效果，有助于讨论流程和问题。良好的价值流图可以让团队准确地直观地看到整个生产中可能发生流程和问题的位置。

rows: 术语说明 DMAIC：定义、测量、分析、改进、控制；适用于改进已有流程。
zh.text: 术语说明 DMAIC：定义、测量、分析、改进、控制；适用于改进已有流程。
创建价值流图意味着您已经进行了一些测量，为测量阶段奠定了基础。价值流图还指出了可以在测量中进一步使用的测量和数据收集点，尽管团队永远不应该将自己局限于价值流图中收集的第一类信息。

在分析过程中，价值流图是一种工具，可以帮助团队集思广益并识别流程中的根本原因或问题点，您可以使用初始价值流图来识别不提供价值的活动或资源 - 那些在流程中创造 Muda 的活动或资源。最后，在改进期间，团队可以开始创建未来状态价值流图，构建旧地图并使用他们通过 DMAIC 流程提出的信息和解决方案。通过将这些解决方案以价值流图的形式写在纸上，团队可以更好地了解可能出现问题的位置，并适当地更改解决方案，以减少实施期间及之后遇到的问题数量。

title.en: Tips for Creating a Future-State Value Stream Map
title.zh: 创建未来状态价值流图的技巧

en.text: 1. Use the current-state value stream map and all other information gathered and analyzed to identify as many sources of waste in the process as possible. 2. Categorize waste into two types: those that are the result of remote locations, machinery, and product designs which are all necessary elements to the end product and those that are not the result of these things. 3. Concentration on the second type of waste and create a future state value stream map that removes them all. 4. Review the future state map to ensure processes can flow appropriately. Ask yourself questions such as:

a. What is the Takt time required at each station to meet overall demands, and is each step in the process capable of meeting that Takt time? If not, the team might need to address steps that are not capable. b. How will production be scheduled? Usually, there is a specific part of the process that controls the production schedule. Ultimately, the best and most optimal control is by the customer (The customer needs 100 per day, so the process should make 100 per day). However, there are times when a specific part of the process is only capable of X units per time period, and the team is unable to change that capability because of resource or other restraints. If the process is not controlled by this “pacemaker step,” then inventory is going to build up before it. c. Is batch processing needed, or can it be removed? d. What process changes and improvements are required to implement the future state value stream? Sometimes, machinery changes, staffing changes, or capital investments are required, and these aren’t always possible. Before moving forward with future-state plans, Six Sigma teams have to make sure resources will be approved and available.

As with anything in Lean and Six Sigma processes, the value stream map isn’t a requirement. In fact, one of the cardinal rules of value stream mapping is not to map just to map. Yes, a finished and polished map looks nice – and can be especially impressive in presentations or documents when other people in the organization are not fully familiar with the tool. However, if creating a value stream map isn’t going to help a Six Sigma team through any of the DMAIC phases or if the process involved simply doesn’t lend itself to mapping in this fashion, then skip this tool. A Six Sigma expert should always be aware that muda can creep into any process – and that includes the process of evaluating and improving something. If you’re creating a value stream map without reason, then you are creating muda of overproduction.

zh.text: 1. 使用当前状态价值流图以及收集和分析的所有其他信息来识别流程中尽可能多的浪费源。 2. 将废物分为两类： 那些是远程位置、机械和产品设计的结果，这些都是最终产品的必要元素，而那些则不是这些因素的结果。 3. 专注于第二种浪费，并创建未来状态价值流图，将其全部消除。 4. 检查未来状态图以确保流程能够正常进行。问自己一些问题，例如：

a.满足总体需求所需的每个工位的节拍时间是多少？流程中的每个步骤是否能够满足该节拍时间？如果没有，团队可能需要解决不具备能力的步骤。 b.生产将如何安排？通常，流程中有一个特定部分来控制生产计划。最终，最好、最优化的控制是由客户进行的（客户每天需要 100 个，因此流程应该每天生产 100 个）。然而，有时流程的特定部分每个时间段只能处理 X 个单位，并且由于资源或其他限制，团队无法更改该功能。如果这个过程不受这个“起搏器步骤”的控制，那么库存就会在它之前积累起来。 c.是否需要批处理，或者可以删除它吗？ d.实施未来状态价值流需要哪些流程改变和改进？有时，需要更换机器、更换人员或进行资本投资，但这些并不总是可行。在推进未来状态计划之前，六西格玛团队必须确保资源获得批准并可用。

与精益和六西格玛流程中的任何内容一样，价值流图不是必需的。事实上，价值流映射的基本规则之一不是仅仅为了映射而映射。是的，经过精心设计的地图看起来不错，并且当组织中的其他人不完全熟悉该工具时，在演示文稿或文档中尤其令人印象深刻。但是，如果创建价值流图无法帮助六西格玛团队完成任何 DMAIC 阶段，或者所涉及的流程根本不适合以这种方式进行映射，那么请跳过此工具。六西格玛专家应该始终意识到，muda 可以渗透到任何过程中，包括评估和改进某些事物的过程。如果你毫无理由地创建价值流图，那么你就是在制造生产过剩的泥潭。

title.en: Six Sigma Black Belt Training Manual

source: The Council for Six Sigma Certification training-materials page lists the Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification Training Manual as a free PDF download: https://www.sixsigmacouncil.org/six-sigma-training-material/

licenseNotice.en: The source manual is listed as a free PDF on the CSSC training-materials page. This app is for personal study, Chinese translation, and bilingual reference only. Commercial use is prohibited. This project is not an official CSSC product; all original rights remain with their respective owner.

ch01-overview-en-001.translation: 六西格玛（Six Sigma，或 6σ）既是一套流程改进方法，也是一种用于描述流程固有变异的统计概念。六西格玛的基本前提是：流程中的变异会带来出错机会；出错机会会进一步带来产品或服务缺陷的风险；缺陷最终会损害客户满意度。通过减少变异和出错机会，六西格玛方法最终能够降低流程成本并提升客户满意度。

sentences.source: Six Sigma, or 6σ, is both a methodology for process improvement and a statistical concept that seeks to define the variation inherent in any process.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛（Six Sigma，或 6σ）既是一套流程改进方法，也是一种用于描述流程固有变异的统计概念。

sentences.source: The overarching premise of Six Sigma is that variation in a process leads to opportunities for error;
sentences.translation: 六西格玛的基本前提是：流程中的变异会带来出错机会；

sentences.source: opportunities for error then lead to risks for product defects.
sentences.translation: 出错机会会进一步带来产品或服务缺陷的风险；

sentences.source: Product defects—whether in a tangible process or a service—lead to poor customer satisfaction.
sentences.translation: 缺陷最终会损害客户满意度。

sentences.source: By working to reduce variation and opportunities for error, the Six Sigma method ultimately reduces process costs and increases customer satisfaction.
sentences.translation: 通过减少变异和出错机会，六西格玛方法最终能够降低流程成本并提升客户满意度。

data-driven-processes-en-001.translation: 在应用六西格玛时，组织、团队和项目经理会努力采用基于测量和指标的策略。过去，许多企业领导者依靠直觉或经验做决策。六西格玛并不是要否定经验型领导，也不是要排斥流程中的直觉判断；相反，它让技能、经验和知识获得数学与统计基础。经验可能告诉我们某个流程运转不佳，统计数据则能证明这一点；直觉可能让项目经理认为某项改变能提升产出，六西格玛工具则帮助组织验证这些假设。

sentences.source: In applying Six Sigma, organizations, teams, and project managers seek to implement strategies that are based on measurement and metrics.
sentences.translation: 在应用六西格玛时，组织、团队和项目经理会努力采用基于测量和指标的策略。

sentences.source: Historically, many business leaders made decisions based on intuition or experience.
sentences.translation: 过去，许多企业领导者依靠直觉或经验做决策。

sentences.source: Despite some common beliefs in various industries, Six Sigma doesn’t remove the need for experienced leadership, and it doesn’t negate the importance of intuition in any process.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛并不是要否定经验型领导，也不是要排斥流程中的直觉判断；

sentences.source: Instead, Six Sigma works alongside other skills, experience, and knowledge to provide a mathematical and statistical foundation for decision making.
sentences.translation: 相反，它让技能、经验和知识获得数学与统计基础。

sentences.source: Experience might say a process isn’t working;
sentences.translation: 经验可能告诉我们某个流程运转不佳，统计数据则能证明这一点；

sentences.source: statistics prove that to be true.
sentences.translation: 经验可能告诉我们某个流程运转不佳，统计数据则能证明这一点；

sentences.source: Intuition might guide a project manager to believe a certain change could improve output;
sentences.translation: 直觉可能让项目经理认为某项改变能提升产出，六西格玛工具则帮助组织验证这些假设。

sentences.source: Six Sigma tools help organizations validate those assumptions.
sentences.translation: 直觉可能让项目经理认为某项改变能提升产出，六西格玛工具则帮助组织验证这些假设。

decision-without-six-sigma-en-001.translation: 如果缺少适当的测量和分析，组织内的决策过程可能会变成下面这样：

sentences.source: Without proper measurement and analysis, decision making processes in an organization might proceed as follows:
sentences.translation: 如果缺少适当的测量和分析，组织内的决策过程可能会变成下面这样：

decision-without-six-sigma-en-003.translation: 组织中有影响力的人提出一个好点子，或对别人的点子产生兴趣。

sentences.source: Someone with clout in the organization has a good idea or takes interest in someone else’s idea.
sentences.translation: 组织中有影响力的人提出一个好点子，或对别人的点子产生兴趣。

decision-without-six-sigma-en-004.translation: 决策者基于过往经验或知识，相信这个点子会成功。

sentences.source: Based on past experience or knowledge, decision makers within an organization believe the idea will be successful.
sentences.translation: 决策者基于过往经验或知识，相信这个点子会成功。

decision-without-six-sigma-en-005.translation: 点子被付诸实施；有时会以 Beta 测试形式上线，以尽量降低费用和风险。

sentences.source: The idea is implemented;
sentences.translation: 点子被付诸实施；

sentences.source: sometimes it is implemented in beta mode so expenses and risks are minimized.
sentences.translation: 有时会以 Beta 测试形式上线，以尽量降低费用和风险。

decision-without-six-sigma-en-006.translation: 实施后才评估成败；问题通常要等到已经影响当前或未来的产品、服务或流程后才被处理。

sentences.source: The success of the idea is weighed after implementation;
sentences.translation: 实施后才评估成败；

sentences.source: problems are addressed after they impact products or processes in some way in the present or the future.
sentences.translation: 问题通常要等到已经影响当前或未来的产品、服务或流程后才被处理。

decision-without-six-sigma-en-007.translation: Beta 测试有时也会被纳入六西格玛方法，但相关想法或变更必须先经过严谨的分析和数据检验。如果不经过六西格玛方法，就直接把想法推入 Beta 测试甚至全面推广，组织可能会遭遇意料之外的后果：把资金花在最终无法按计划奏效的方案上，或在充满出错机会的试错期中损害客户感知。许多不依赖数据的组织会在尚未理解真实收益或损失之前就开始改进。有些改进表面看似有效，却未必真正提升客户满意度或利润。

sentences.source: Beta testing is sometimes used in a Six Sigma approach, but the idea or change in question goes through rigorous analysis and data testing first.
sentences.translation: Beta 测试有时也会被纳入六西格玛方法，但相关想法或变更必须先经过严谨的分析和数据检验。

sentences.source: The disadvantage of launching ideas into beta—or to an entire population--without going through a Six Sigma methodology is that organizations can experience unintended consequences from changes, spend money on ideas that don’t end up working out as planned, and impact customer perceptions through trial-and-error periods rife with opportunities for error.
sentences.translation: 如果不经过六西格玛方法，就直接把想法推入 Beta 测试甚至全面推广，组织可能会遭遇意料之外的后果：把资金花在最终无法按计划奏效的方案上，或在充满出错机会的试错期中损害客户感知。

sentences.source: In many cases, organizations that don’t rely on data make improvements without first understanding the true gain or loss associated with the change.
sentences.translation: 许多不依赖数据的组织会在尚未理解真实收益或损失之前就开始改进。

sentences.source: Some improvements may appear to work on the surface without actually impacting customer satisfaction or profit in a positive way.
sentences.translation: 有些改进表面看似有效，却未必真正提升客户满意度或利润。

decision-with-six-sigma-en-001.translation: 六西格玛方法使组织能够识别问题、验证假设、头脑风暴解决方案，并规划实施路径，从而避免意外后果。通过将统计分析、流程图等工具应用于问题与方案，团队可以更准确地可视化并预测结果，让管理层在较低财务风险下做出决策。

sentences.source: The Six Sigma method lets organizations identify problems, validate assumptions, brainstorm solutions, and plan for implementation to avoid unintended consequences.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛方法使组织能够识别问题、验证假设、头脑风暴解决方案，并规划实施路径，从而避免意外后果。

sentences.source: By applying tools such as statistical analysis and process mapping to problems and solutions, teams can visualize and predict outcomes with a high-level of accuracy, letting leadership make decisions with less financial risk.
sentences.translation: 通过将统计分析、流程图等工具应用于问题与方案，团队可以更准确地可视化并预测结果，让管理层在较低财务风险下做出决策。

decision-with-six-sigma-en-002.translation: 当然，六西格玛并不能给组织一颗“水晶球”。即使熟练使用本书介绍的工具，团队在实施和维持解决方案时仍可能遇到问题。因此，六西格玛还强调控制方法：一旦团队实施了变更，就要持续使用六西格玛工具和统计方法，以远低于传统质量方法的成本控制流程。

sentences.source: Six Sigma methods don’t offer a crystal ball for organizations, though.
sentences.translation: 当然，六西格玛并不能给组织一颗“水晶球”。

sentences.source: Even with expert use of the tools described in this book, problems can arise for teams as they implement and maintain solutions.
sentences.translation: 即使熟练使用本书介绍的工具，团队在实施和维持解决方案时仍可能遇到问题。

sentences.source: That’s why Six Sigma also provides for control methods: once teams implement changes, they can control processes for a fraction of the cost of traditional quality methods by continuing the use of Six Sigma tools and statistics.
sentences.translation: 因此，六西格玛还强调控制方法：一旦团队实施了变更，就要持续使用六西格玛工具和统计方法，以远低于传统质量方法的成本控制流程。

defining-6-sigma-en-001.translation: 作为流程改进方法，六西格玛包含大量工具和知识，本书后续会逐步展开。本节先从统计概念角度说明 6σ 的含义。

sentences.source: Six Sigma as a methodology for process improvement involves a vast library of tools and knowledge, which will be covered throughout this book.
sentences.translation: 作为流程改进方法，六西格玛包含大量工具和知识，本书后续会逐步展开。

sentences.source: In this section, we’ll begin to define the statistical concept represented by 6σ.
sentences.translation: 本节先从统计概念角度说明 6σ 的含义。

defining-6-sigma-en-002.translation: 从最基本的定义看，6σ 是许多专家所说“近乎完美”流程的统计表示。严格来说，一个六西格玛流程每百万次机会中只有 3.4 个缺陷。换成百分比，即六西格玛流程产出的产品中有 99.99966% 没有缺陷。若低一个西格玛水平，即五西格玛，准确率约为 99.97%，流程每百万次机会会出现 233 个错误。简单说，这意味着会有多得多的不满意客户。

sentences.source: At the most basic definition, 6σ is a statistical representation for what many experts call a “perfect” process.
sentences.translation: 从最基本的定义看，6σ 是许多专家所说“近乎完美”流程的统计表示。

sentences.source: Technically, in a Six Sigma process, there are only 3.4 defects per million opportunities.
sentences.translation: 严格来说，一个六西格玛流程每百万次机会中只有 3.4 个缺陷。

sentences.source: In percentages, that means 99.99966 percent of the products from a Six Sigma process are without defect.
sentences.translation: 换成百分比，即六西格玛流程产出的产品中有 99.99966% 没有缺陷。

sentences.source: At just one sigma level below—5σ, or 99.97 percent accuracy--processes experience 233 errors per million opportunities.
sentences.translation: 若低一个西格玛水平，即五西格玛，准确率约为 99.97%，流程每百万次机会会出现 233 个错误。

sentences.source: In simpler terms, there are going to be many more unsatisfied customers.
sentences.translation: 简单说，这意味着会有多得多的不满意客户。

real-world-examples-en-001.translation: 根据美国国家海洋和大气管理局的数据，美国空中交通管制员每天处理 28,537 架次商业航班，一年约 1,041.6 万架次。若空管流程处在五西格玛水平，处理流程中每年约有 2,426 架次航班会出现某类错误；如果达到六西格玛水平，这一风险会降至约 35.41 次。

sentences.source: According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, air traffic controllers in the United States handle 28,537 commercial flights daily.1 In a year, that is approximately 10.416 million flights.
sentences.translation: 根据美国国家海洋和大气管理局的数据，美国空中交通管制员每天处理 28,537 架次商业航班，一年约 1,041.6 万架次。

sentences.source: Based on a Five Sigma air traffic control process, errors of some type occur in the process for handling approximately 2,426 flights every year.
sentences.translation: 若空管流程处在五西格玛水平，处理流程中每年约有 2,426 架次航班会出现某类错误；

sentences.source: With a Six Sigma process, that risk drops to 35.41 errors.
sentences.translation: 如果达到六西格玛水平，这一风险会降至约 35.41 次。

real-world-examples-en-002.translation: 美国疾病控制与预防中心报告显示，美国一年约进行 5,140 万台手术。若准确率为 99.97%，医生每年会在 11,976 台手术中出错，即每周约 230 台；达到六西格玛水平后，全国全年错误数会降至约 174 次，也就是每周略高于 3 次。在五西格玛水平下，患者遭遇医疗服务提供者错误的可能性是六西格玛水平的 68 倍。

sentences.source: The CDC reports that approximately 51.4 million surgeries are performed in the United States in a given year.2 Based on a 99.97 accuracy rate, doctors would make errors in 11,976 surgeries each year, or 230 surgeries a week.
sentences.translation: 美国疾病控制与预防中心报告显示，美国一年约进行 5,140 万台手术。

sentences.source: At Six Sigma, that drops to approximately 174 errors a year for the entire country, or just over 3 errors each week.
sentences.translation: 达到六西格玛水平后，全国全年错误数会降至约 174 次，也就是每周略高于 3 次。

real-world-examples-en-003.translation: 美国疾病控制与预防中心报告显示，美国一年约进行 5,140 万台手术。若准确率为 99.97%，医生每年会在 11,976 台手术中出错，即每周约 230 台；达到六西格玛水平后，全国全年错误数会降至约 174 次，也就是每周略高于 3 次。在五西格玛水平下，患者遭遇医疗服务提供者错误的可能性是六西格玛水平的 68 倍。

sentences.source: At Six Sigma, that drops to approximately 174 errors a year for the entire country, or just over 3 errors each week.
sentences.translation: 达到六西格玛水平后，全国全年错误数会降至约 174 次，也就是每周略高于 3 次。

sentences.source: At Five Sigma, patients are 68 times more likely to experience an error at the hands of medical providers.
sentences.translation: 在五西格玛水平下，患者遭遇医疗服务提供者错误的可能性是六西格玛水平的 68 倍。

real-world-examples-en-004.translation: 多数人在日常关键服务中能够接受 99.9% 的准确率，但这些例子说明，六西格玛和五西格玛之间的差距非常大。对组织而言，这不仅是错误率问题，还关系到每一次错误背后的成本。

sentences.source: While most people accept a 99.9 percent accuracy rate in even the most critical services on a daily basis, the above examples highlight how wide the gap between Six Sigma and Five Sigma really is.
sentences.translation: 多数人在日常关键服务中能够接受 99.9% 的准确率，但这些例子说明，六西格玛和五西格玛之间的差距非常大。

sentences.source: For organizations, it’s not just about the error rate—it’s also about the costs associated with each error.
sentences.translation: 对组织而言，这不仅是错误率问题，还关系到每一次错误背后的成本。

real-world-examples-en-005.translation: 以亚马逊发货为例。2013 年网络星期一，亚马逊处理了高达 3,680 万份订单。假设每个订单错误给公司造成 35 美元的平均成本（这是非常保守的估计，因为成本可能包括退货运费、客服接听电话或邮件的人力，以及纠正错误订单所需的人力和运输费用）。

sentences.source: Consider an example based on Amazon shipments.
sentences.translation: 以亚马逊发货为例。

sentences.source: On Cyber Monday in 2013, Amazon processed a whopping 36.8 million orders.3 Let’s assume that each order error costs the company an average of $35 (a very conservative number, considering that costs might include return shipping, labor to answer customer phone calls or emails, and labor and shipping to right a wrong order).
sentences.translation: 2013 年网络星期一，亚马逊处理了高达 3,680 万份订单。

real-world-examples-en-014.translation: 在这个例子中，仅网络星期一业务，不同西格玛水平造成的成本差异就超过 295,000 美元。

sentences.source: For this example, the cost difference in sigma levels is still over $295,000 for the Cyber Monday business.
sentences.translation: 在这个例子中，仅网络星期一业务，不同西格玛水平造成的成本差异就超过 295,000 美元。

real-world-examples-en-015.translation: 对多数组织来说，六西格玛流程是一个持续追求的目标。达到并维持六西格玛“完美”很困难，需要持续流程改进。但即使只是把较低西格玛水平提升到四西格玛或五西格玛，也会显著影响成本和客户满意度。下表继续沿用亚马逊网络星期一示例，比较不同西格玛水平下的结果。

sentences.source: For most organizations, Six Sigma processes are a constant target.
sentences.translation: 对多数组织来说，六西格玛流程是一个持续追求的目标。

sentences.source: Achieving and maintaining Six Sigma “perfection” is difficult and requires continuous process improvement.
sentences.translation: 达到并维持六西格玛“完美”很困难，需要持续流程改进。

sentences.source: But even advancing from lower levels of sigma to a Four or Five Sigma process has a drastic impact on costs and customer satisfaction.
sentences.translation: 但即使只是把较低西格玛水平提升到四西格玛或五西格玛，也会显著影响成本和客户满意度。

sentences.source: Let’s look at the Amazon Cyber Monday example at other levels of sigma.
sentences.translation: 下表继续沿用亚马逊网络星期一示例，比较不同西格玛水平下的结果。

sentences.source: Sigma Level Defects per Million Opportunities Estimated Cyber Monday Defects Total Cost (at $35 estimate per error) One Sigma 690,000 25,392,000 $888,720,000 Two Sigma 308,000 11,334,400 $396,704,000 Three Sigma 66,800 2,458,240 $86,038,400 Four Sigma 6,200 228,160 $7,985,600 Five Sigma 233 8,574.4 $300,104 Six Sigma 3.4 125.12 $4,379
At very low levels of sigma, any process is unlikely to be profitable.
The higher the sigma level, the better the bottom line is likely to be.

calculating-sigma-level-en-001.translation: 在西格玛水平非常低时，任何流程都不太可能盈利。西格玛水平越高，财务结果通常越好。组织和团队可以使用下面的公式计算产品或流程的西格玛水平：

sentences.source: Organizations and teams can calculate the sigma level of a product or process using the equation below:
sentences.translation: 组织和团队可以使用下面的公式计算产品或流程的西格玛水平：

calculating-sigma-level-en-003.translation: 设想一个营销部门负责向客户或潜在客户寄送信件。为便于说明，假设该流程每天将 30,000 封信装入预先写好地址的信封；一个工作周内，流程共输出 150,000 封信。

sentences.source: Consider a process in a marketing department that distributes letters to customers or prospects.
sentences.translation: 设想一个营销部门负责向客户或潜在客户寄送信件。

sentences.source: For the purposes of the example, imagine that the process inserts 30,000 letters in preaddressed envelopes each day.
sentences.translation: 为便于说明，假设该流程每天将 30,000 封信装入预先写好地址的信封；

sentences.source: In a given business week, the process outputs 150,000 letters.
sentences.translation: 一个工作周内，流程共输出 150,000 封信。

calculating-sigma-level-en-004.translation: 随后，营销部门收到投诉：有人收到写着自己地址的信封，但里面的信件却是写给别人或与别人相关的。营销部门从下一周批次中随机抽取 1,000 封信，发现其中 5 封有错误。将这个比例推算到总量上，他们估计可能多达 750 封信存在错误。（抽样与外推会在后续统计章节中详细介绍。）

sentences.source: The marketing department begins receiving complaints that people are receiving letters in envelopes that are addressed to them, but the letters inside are addressed to or relevant to someone else.
sentences.translation: 随后，营销部门收到投诉：有人收到写着自己地址的信封，但里面的信件却是写给别人或与别人相关的。

sentences.source: The marketing department randomly selects 1,000 letters from the next week’s batch and finds that 5 of them have errors.
sentences.translation: 营销部门从下一周批次中随机抽取 1,000 封信，发现其中 5 封有错误。

sentences.source: Applying that to the total amount, they estimate that as many as 750 letters could have errors.
sentences.translation: 将这个比例推算到总量上，他们估计可能多达 750 封信存在错误。

sentences.source: (Sampling and extrapolation are covered in depth in the advanced chapters on statistics.)
sentences.translation: （抽样与外推会在后续统计章节中详细介绍。

calculating-sigma-level-en-005.translation: 该信件流程每周有 150,000 次出错机会，估计有 750 个缺陷。计算为：

sentences.source: The letter process has 150,000 opportunities for error each week and an estimated 750 defects.
sentences.translation: 该信件流程每周有 150,000 次出错机会，估计有 750 个缺陷。

calculating-sigma-level-en-007.translation: 在下方简化西格玛表中查找 99.5 的良率，可以看到上述流程当前介于 4.0 和 4.1 西格玛之间。

sentences.source: Look up a yield of 99.5 in the abridged Sigma table below and you’ll see the process described above is currently between 4 and 4.1 sigma.
sentences.translation: 在下方简化西格玛表中查找 99.5 的良率，可以看到上述流程当前介于 4.0 和 4.1 西格玛之间。

sigma-level-not-final-en-001.translation: 西格玛水平能让组织从高层次了解流程表现，但不同流程之间仅比较西格玛水平，并不总能指出最应该优先改进的流程。领导层还应考虑成本、资源以及改进的预期影响。

sentences.source: Sigma levels provide organization with a high-level look at how a process is performing, but comparing sigma levels between multiple processes doesn’t always point to the particular process an organization should improve first.
sentences.translation: 西格玛水平能让组织从高层次了解流程表现，但不同流程之间仅比较西格玛水平，并不总能指出最应该优先改进的流程。

sigma-level-not-final-en-002.translation: 西格玛水平能让组织从高层次了解流程表现，但不同流程之间仅比较西格玛水平，并不总能指出最应该优先改进的流程。领导层还应考虑成本、资源以及改进的预期影响。

sentences.source: Sigma levels provide organization with a high-level look at how a process is performing, but comparing sigma levels between multiple processes doesn’t always point to the particular process an organization should improve first.
sentences.translation: 西格玛水平能让组织从高层次了解流程表现，但不同流程之间仅比较西格玛水平，并不总能指出最应该优先改进的流程。

sentences.source: Leadership should also consider costs, resources, and the estimated impact of improvements.
sentences.translation: 领导层还应考虑成本、资源以及改进的预期影响。

sigma-level-not-final-en-003.translation: 例如，在一家食品加工厂中，可能存在以下流程：

sentences.source: For example, consider these processes that might be found in a food processing plant:
sentences.translation: 例如，在一家食品加工厂中，可能存在以下流程：

sigma-level-not-final-en-004.translation: 流程 绩效指标 当前西格玛水平 给食品添加装饰元素 装饰位于食品中央且稳定，运输过程中不会脱落 2.2 产品包装 产品密封以保持新鲜 3.1 产品运输 产品及时送达正确客户 4.3

sentences.source: Process Performance Metric(s) Current Sigma Level Attaching a decorative element to food item Decorative touch is centered on food product and stable so it won't fall off in transit 2.2 Packing product Product is sealed for freshness 3.1 Shipping of product Product reaches the right customer in a timely manner 4.3
sentences.translation: 流程 绩效指标 当前西格玛水平 给食品添加装饰元素 装饰位于食品中央且稳定，运输过程中不会脱落 2.2 产品包装 产品密封以保持新鲜 3.1 产品运输 产品及时送达正确客户 4.3

sigma-level-not-final-en-012.translation: 只看西格玛水平，添加装饰元素的流程最需要改进，因为它缺陷率最高。但工厂领导还要问：这对客户有多重要？它对利润底线的影响有多大？

sentences.source: A glance at sigma levels indicates that the process that attaches the decorative element is in most need of improvement.
sentences.translation: 只看西格玛水平，添加装饰元素的流程最需要改进，因为它缺陷率最高。

sentences.source: While that process has the highest rate of defects, leadership within the plant would have to ask themselves: How much does that matter to the customer, and what is the hit to the bottom line?
sentences.translation: 但工厂领导还要问：这对客户有多重要？

sigma-level-not-final-en-013.translation: 多数客户可能更在意产品是否密封保鲜、是否送达正确地点。由于变质产品必须丢弃，最昂贵的错误很可能来自包装密封不当。因此，工厂可能先把资源投入包装流程，而不是装饰元素流程。

sentences.source: It’s likely that most customers will notice most that the product is sealed for freshness and reaches the right location.
sentences.translation: 多数客户可能更在意产品是否密封保鲜、是否送达正确地点。

sentences.source: Since bad product has to be thrown away, the most expensive errors might be associated with improper sealing during packing.
sentences.translation: 由于变质产品必须丢弃，最昂贵的错误很可能来自包装密封不当。

sentences.source: The plant is likely to use resources to improve the packing process before addressing the decorative element issue.
sentences.translation: 因此，工厂可能先把资源投入包装流程，而不是装饰元素流程。

sigma-level-not-final-en-014.translation: 包装流程改进后，工厂再考虑是否改进装饰流程或运输流程。若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。此时是否一定先处理成本更高的问题？如果运输流程只需员工培训即可改善，而装饰问题需要昂贵设备升级呢？有时组织必须把改进成本纳入考虑。六西格玛文化强调持续改进，团队应在启动最有价值的改进措施前综合评估所有选择。

sentences.source: After the packing process is improved, the plant might then consider whether to improve the decorating process or the shipping process.
sentences.translation: 包装流程改进后，工厂再考虑是否改进装饰流程或运输流程。

sentences.source: As part of that consideration, the company might conduct customer surveys to reveal that some customers have stopped buying the product because of the decorative element issue.
sentences.translation: 若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。

sentences.source: An analyst estimates that the loss of sales related to that issue are costing the company $1,000 a week.
sentences.translation: 若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。

sentences.source: Shipping issues are costing the company $500 a week.
sentences.translation: 若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。

sigma-level-not-final-en-015.translation: 包装流程改进后，工厂再考虑是否改进装饰流程或运输流程。若客户调查显示，一些客户因装饰问题停止购买产品，分析师估计该问题每周造成 1,000 美元销售损失，而运输问题每周造成 500 美元损失。此时是否一定先处理成本更高的问题？如果运输流程只需员工培训即可改善，而装饰问题需要昂贵设备升级呢？有时组织必须把改进成本纳入考虑。六西格玛文化强调持续改进，团队应在启动最有价值的改进措施前综合评估所有选择。

sentences.source: Should the company address the costlier issue first?
sentences.translation: 此时是否一定先处理成本更高的问题？

sentences.source: What if you were told that the shipping process could be improved with staff training sessions, while the decorative element issue required an expensive machinery update?
sentences.translation: 如果运输流程只需员工培训即可改善，而装饰问题需要昂贵设备升级呢？

sentences.source: Sometimes, organizations have to consider the expense of an improvement.
sentences.translation: 有时组织必须把改进成本纳入考虑。

sentences.source: Applying a Six Sigma project to all situations isn’t financially lucrative since those improvements take time and money.
sentences.translation: 有时组织必须把改进成本纳入考虑。

sentences.source: A Six Sigma culture is about continuous improvement, which means teams consider all options before embarking on the most lucrative improvement measures.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛文化强调持续改进，团队应在启动最有价值的改进措施前综合评估所有选择。

common-six-sigma-principles-en-001.translation: 组织可以通过把六西格玛核心原则融入领导方式、流程管理和改进行动，影响自身的西格玛水平。六西格玛原则及相关工具将在本书各部分详细展开，下面先介绍几个常见思想。

sentences.source: Organizations can impact their sigma level by integrating core principles from the Six Sigma methodology into leadership styles, process management, and improvement endeavors.
sentences.translation: 组织可以通过把六西格玛核心原则融入领导方式、流程管理和改进行动，影响自身的西格玛水平。

sentences.source: The principles of Six Sigma, and the tools used to achieve them, are covered in detail in various sections of this book, but some common ideas are introduced below.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛原则及相关工具将在本书各部分详细展开，下面先介绍几个常见思想。

customer-focused-improvement-en-001.translation: 从食品工厂的例子可以看到，六西格玛流程并不是为了提高西格玛水平而盲目改进。该方法的首要原则之一是关注客户。第 5 章会介绍客户之声（Voice of the Customer，VoC），以及如何确定客户真正希望从产品或流程中获得什么。将客户理解与测量、统计和流程改进方法结合起来，组织可以提升客户满意度，并最终增强利润、客户留存和忠诚度。

sentences.source: In the illustration about the food plant, we saw that the Six Sigma process doesn’t just make improvements for the sake of driving up sigma levels.
sentences.translation: 从食品工厂的例子可以看到，六西格玛流程并不是为了提高西格玛水平而盲目改进。

sentences.source: A primary principle of the methodology is a focus on the customer.
sentences.translation: 该方法的首要原则之一是关注客户。

sentences.source: In Chapter 5, we’ll look at the Voice of the Customer (VoC) and ways for establishing what the customer really wants from a product or process.
sentences.translation: 第 5 章会介绍客户之声（Voice of the Customer，VoC），以及如何确定客户真正希望从产品或流程中获得什么。

sentences.source: By combining that knowledge with measurements, statistics, and process improvement methods, organizations increase customer satisfaction, ultimately bolstering profits, customer retention, and loyalty.
sentences.translation: 将客户理解与测量、统计和流程改进方法结合起来，组织可以提升客户满意度，并最终增强利润、客户留存和忠诚度。

customer-focused-improvement-en-002.translation: 深入理解客户及其需求，不仅能帮助企业定制产品和服务，还能帮助组织：

sentences.source: A detailed understanding of the customer and customer desires not only lets businesses customize product offerings and services, but it also lets organizations:
sentences.translation: 深入理解客户及其需求，不仅能帮助企业定制产品和服务，还能帮助组织：

customer-focused-improvement-en-003.translation: 提供客户想要且愿意付费的附加功能。

sentences.source: Offer additional features customers want and are willing to pay for
sentences.translation: 提供客户想要且愿意付费的附加功能。

customer-focused-improvement-en-004.translation: 根据当前需求确定产品开发优先级。

sentences.source: Prioritize product development to meet current needs
sentences.translation: 根据当前需求确定产品开发优先级。

customer-focused-improvement-en-005.translation: 基于客户反馈发展新想法。

sentences.source: Develop new ideas based on customer feedback
sentences.translation: 基于客户反馈发展新想法。

sentences.source: Understand changing trends in the market
sentences.translation: 理解市场趋势变化。

sentences.source: Identify areas of concern
sentences.translation: 识别需要关注的领域。

customer-focused-improvement-en-008.translation: 根据客户对不同问题的感知，确定挑战处理优先级。

sentences.source: Prioritize work on challenges based on how customers perceive various problems or issues
sentences.translation: 根据客户对不同问题的感知，确定挑战处理优先级。

customer-focused-improvement-en-009.translation: 在投入时间和资金前测试解决方案与想法。

sentences.source: Test solutions and ideas before investing time and money in them
sentences.translation: 在投入时间和资金前测试解决方案与想法。

value-streams-en-001.translation: 价值流是为了产生最终结果而需要的所有事项、事件和人员的序列。例如，为某人提供一个加番茄酱的热狗，其价值流可能包括：

sentences.source: The value stream is the sequence of all items, events, and people required to produce an end result.

value-streams-en-017.translation: 如果把上述所有过程用图形准确表示出来，说明这些要素如何变成最终端出的热狗，就形成了价值流图。确定流程价值流的目的，是识别关注点、浪费和改进机会。在上述流程中，是否有四个人分别完成夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘和端送？若是，产品在四个人之间转手是否增加了时间？是否由一个人完成会更快？供应商是否是一家杂货店，还是从多家商店采购，原因是什么？多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？这些都是价值流图能帮助揭示并回答的问题。

sentences.source: If you combine all of the above processes into a pictorial representation of exactly how these elements become the served hotdog, then you have a value stream map.
sentences.translation: 如果把上述所有过程用图形准确表示出来，说明这些要素如何变成最终端出的热狗，就形成了价值流图。

value-streams-en-018.translation: 如果把上述所有过程用图形准确表示出来，说明这些要素如何变成最终端出的热狗，就形成了价值流图。确定流程价值流的目的，是识别关注点、浪费和改进机会。在上述流程中，是否有四个人分别完成夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘和端送？若是，产品在四个人之间转手是否增加了时间？是否由一个人完成会更快？供应商是否是一家杂货店，还是从多家商店采购，原因是什么？多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？这些都是价值流图能帮助揭示并回答的问题。

sentences.source: The purpose for determining a value stream for a process is that you can identify areas of concern, waste, and improvement.
sentences.translation: 确定流程价值流的目的，是识别关注点、浪费和改进机会。

sentences.source: In the above process, are there four different people putting the hotdog together and serving it, or is one person doing all four of those tasks?
sentences.translation: 在上述流程中，是否有四个人分别完成夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘和端送？

sentences.source: Is the supplier a single grocery store, or are you shopping for items at various stores and why?
sentences.translation: 供应商是否是一家杂货店，还是从多家商店采购，原因是什么？

sentences.source: Do you get savings benefits to offset the added time spent working with multiple suppliers?
sentences.translation: 多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？

value-streams-en-019.translation: 如果把上述所有过程用图形准确表示出来，说明这些要素如何变成最终端出的热狗，就形成了价值流图。确定流程价值流的目的，是识别关注点、浪费和改进机会。在上述流程中，是否有四个人分别完成夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘和端送？若是，产品在四个人之间转手是否增加了时间？是否由一个人完成会更快？供应商是否是一家杂货店，还是从多家商店采购，原因是什么？多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？这些都是价值流图能帮助揭示并回答的问题。

sentences.source: Do you get savings benefits to offset the added time spent working with multiple suppliers?
sentences.translation: 多供应商带来的节省是否足以抵消额外协作时间？

sentences.source: These are some examples of the questions you can reveal and answer during value stream mapping.
sentences.translation: 这些都是价值流图能帮助揭示并回答的问题。

continuous-process-improvement-en-001.translation: 持续流程改进是六西格玛方法的内在要求。真正采用六西格玛方法的组织不会停止改进，而会持续识别并优先处理机会领域。一个领域改进后，组织会继续改进另一个领域。如果某流程从 4 西格玛提升到 4.4 西格玛，组织还会继续寻找进一步提升的方法。目标是在尽快满足财务稳定等其他要求的同时，使组织内所有流程逐步接近 99.99966% 准确率的“近乎完美”水平。

sentences.source: Inherent in the Six Sigma method is continuous process improvement.
sentences.translation: 持续流程改进是六西格玛方法的内在要求。

sentences.source: An organization that completely adopts a Six Sigma methodology never stops improving.
sentences.translation: 真正采用六西格玛方法的组织不会停止改进，而会持续识别并优先处理机会领域。

sentences.source: It identifies and prioritizes areas of opportunity on a continuous basis.
sentences.translation: 真正采用六西格玛方法的组织不会停止改进，而会持续识别并优先处理机会领域。

sentences.source: Once one area is improved upon, the organization moves on to improving another area.
sentences.translation: 一个领域改进后，组织会继续改进另一个领域。

sentences.source: If a process is improved from 4 Sigma to 4.4 Sigma, the organization considers ways to move the sigma level up further.
sentences.translation: 如果某流程从 4 西格玛提升到 4.4 西格玛，组织还会继续寻找进一步提升的方法。

sentences.source: The goal is to move ever closer to the “perfect” level of 99.99966 accuracy for all processes within an organization while maintaining other goals and requirements, such as financial stability, as quickly as possible.
sentences.translation: 目标是在尽快满足财务稳定等其他要求的同时，使组织内所有流程逐步接近 99.99966% 准确率的“近乎完美”水平。

variation-en-001.translation: 持续改进流程的一种方式是减少流程变异。每个流程都有固有变异：例如一个有 20 名员工的呼叫中心，即便所有电话都有脚本，不同电话之间仍会因为语调、口音、环境和来电者情绪而产生差异。通过为员工提供脚本或常见场景建议话术，呼叫中心可以在一定程度上减少变异。

sentences.source: One of the ways to continuously improve a process is to reduce the variation in the process.
sentences.translation: 持续改进流程的一种方式是减少流程变异。

sentences.source: Every process contains inherent variation: in a call center with 20 employees, variation will exist in each phone call even if the calls are scripted.
sentences.translation: 每个流程都有固有变异：例如一个有 20 名员工的呼叫中心，即便所有电话都有脚本，不同电话之间仍会因为语调、口音、环境和来电者情绪而产生差异。

sentences.source: Inflection, accents, environmental concerns, and caller moods are just some things that lead to variation in this circumstance.
sentences.translation: 每个流程都有固有变异：例如一个有 20 名员工的呼叫中心，即便所有电话都有脚本，不同电话之间仍会因为语调、口音、环境和来电者情绪而产生差异。

sentences.source: By providing employees with a script or suggested comments for common scenarios, the call center reduces variation to some degree.
sentences.translation: 通过为员工提供脚本或常见场景建议话术，呼叫中心可以在一定程度上减少变异。

variation-en-002.translation: 再看一家披萨店。员工被要求按披萨尺寸使用固定配料量：小披萨一杯奶酪，大披萨两杯奶酪。店主发现每个披萨上的奶酪量差异很大，担心客户体验不一致。为减少变异，他给员工提供两个量杯：小披萨用一杯量杯，大披萨用两杯量杯。

sentences.source: Consider another example: A pizzeria.
sentences.translation: 再看一家披萨店。

sentences.source: The employees are instructed to use certain amounts of ingredients for each size of pizza.
sentences.translation: 员工被要求按披萨尺寸使用固定配料量：小披萨一杯奶酪，大披萨两杯奶酪。

sentences.source: A small gets one cup of cheese;
sentences.translation: 员工被要求按披萨尺寸使用固定配料量：小披萨一杯奶酪，大披萨两杯奶酪。

sentences.source: a large gets two cups.
sentences.translation: 员工被要求按披萨尺寸使用固定配料量：小披萨一杯奶酪，大披萨两杯奶酪。

sentences.source: The pizzeria owner notes a great deal of variation in how much cheese is on each pizza, and he fears it will lead to inconsistent customer experiences.
sentences.translation: 店主发现每个披萨上的奶酪量差异很大，担心客户体验不一致。

sentences.source: To reduce variation, he provides employees with two measuring cups: a 1-cup container for small pizzas and a 2-cup container for large pizzas.
sentences.translation: 为减少变异，他给员工提供两个量杯：小披萨用一杯量杯，大披萨用两杯量杯。

variation-en-003.translation: 变异降低了，但并未消失。有的员工把奶酪倒入量杯，有的用勺舀；有人只装到杯口，有人让奶酪高出杯口形成小堆。店主再次减少变异：培训所有员工把奶酪装到超过杯口，然后用平刮刀刮去多余奶酪。虽然空气间隙或奶酪沉降方式仍会造成变异，但整体变异大幅减少，客户得到的披萨也更一致。

sentences.source: The variation is reduced, but it is still present.
sentences.translation: 变异降低了，但并未消失。

sentences.source: Some employees pour cheese into the cups and some scoop it.
sentences.translation: 有的员工把奶酪倒入量杯，有的用勺舀；

sentences.source: Some fill the cups just to the rim;
sentences.translation: 有人只装到杯口，有人让奶酪高出杯口形成小堆。

sentences.source: others let the cheese create a mound above the rim.
sentences.translation: 有人只装到杯口，有人让奶酪高出杯口形成小堆。

sentences.source: The owner acts to reduce variation again: he trains all employees to fill the cup over the rim and use a flat spatula to scrape excess cheese off.
sentences.translation: 店主再次减少变异：培训所有员工把奶酪装到超过杯口，然后用平刮刀刮去多余奶酪。

sentences.source: While variation will still exist due to factors such as air pockets or how cheese settles in the cup, it is greatly reduced, and customers experience more consistent pizzas.
sentences.translation: 虽然空气间隙或奶酪沉降方式仍会造成变异，但整体变异大幅减少，客户得到的披萨也更一致。

removing-waste-en-001.translation: 还记得热狗价值流的例子吗？如果夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘、端送分别由四个人完成，流程是否因为产品要在四个人之间传递而耗时更长？如果一个人能完成所有动作，是否会更快？若答案是肯定的，我们就识别出流程中的一种浪费，在这个例子里是搬运浪费。

sentences.source: Remember the hotdog example for value streams?
sentences.translation: 还记得热狗价值流的例子吗？

sentences.source: We asked the question: do four different people act to place the hotdog in the bun, put the ketchup on the hotdog, plate the hotdog, and serve it?
sentences.translation: 如果夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘、端送分别由四个人完成，流程是否因为产品要在四个人之间传递而耗时更长？

sentences.source: If so, does the process take more time because the product has to be transferred between four people?
sentences.translation: 如果夹热狗、加番茄酱、装盘、端送分别由四个人完成，流程是否因为产品要在四个人之间传递而耗时更长？

sentences.source: Would it be faster to have one person perform all those actions?
sentences.translation: 如果一个人能完成所有动作，是否会更快？

sentences.source: If so, then we’ve identified some waste in the process—in this case, waste of conveyance.
sentences.translation: 若答案是肯定的，我们就识别出流程中的一种浪费，在这个例子里是搬运浪费。

removing-waste-en-002.translation: 消除浪费，即去除对流程结果并非必要的事项、动作或人员，可以减少处理时间、出错机会和总体成本。虽然浪费是六西格玛方法中的重要关注点，但“浪费”这一概念来自精益流程管理。

sentences.source: Removing waste—items, actions, or people that are unnecessary to the outcome of a process—reduces processing time, opportunities for errors, and overall costs.
sentences.translation: 消除浪费，即去除对流程结果并非必要的事项、动作或人员，可以减少处理时间、出错机会和总体成本。

sentences.source: While waste is a major concern in the Six Sigma methodology, the concept of waste comes from a methodology known as Lean Process Management..
sentences.translation: 虽然浪费是六西格玛方法中的重要关注点，但“浪费”这一概念来自精益流程管理。

equipping-people-en-001.translation: 如果组织没有让直接参与流程的员工掌握监控和维持改进的方法，改进流程只能是暂时措施。多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；随后，该团队赋能每天直接处理流程的员工，使他们能够在改进后的状态下控制和管理流程。

sentences.source: Implementing improved processes is a temporary measure unless organizations equip their employees working with processes to monitor and maintain improvements.
sentences.translation: 如果组织没有让直接参与流程的员工掌握监控和维持改进的方法，改进流程只能是暂时措施。

sentences.source: In most organizations, process improvement includes a two-pronged approach.
sentences.translation: 多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；

sentences.source: First, a process improvement team comprised of project management, methodology experts, and subject-matter experts define, plan, and implement an improvement.
sentences.translation: 多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；

equipping-people-en-002.translation: 如果组织没有让直接参与流程的员工掌握监控和维持改进的方法，改进流程只能是暂时措施。多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；随后，该团队赋能每天直接处理流程的员工，使他们能够在改进后的状态下控制和管理流程。

sentences.source: First, a process improvement team comprised of project management, methodology experts, and subject-matter experts define, plan, and implement an improvement.
sentences.translation: 多数组织中的流程改进通常采用双重路径：首先，由项目管理人员、方法专家和主题专家组成的流程改进团队定义、规划并实施改进；

sentences.source: That team then equips the employees who work directly with the process daily to control and manage the process in its improved state.
sentences.translation: 随后，该团队赋能每天直接处理流程的员工，使他们能够在改进后的状态下控制和管理流程。

controlling-the-process-en-001.translation: 六西格玛改进通常针对失控流程。所谓失控流程，是指满足特定统计条件、表现出不受控状态的流程。改进目标是让流程回到统计受控状态。改进实施后，组织继续使用测量、统计和其他六西格玛工具，确保流程保持受控。任何持续改进流程的一部分，都是建立这些控制，并确保经常接触流程的一线员工知道如何使用这些控制。

sentences.source: Often, Six Sigma improvements address processes that are out of control.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛改进通常针对失控流程。

sentences.source: Out of control processes meet specific statistical requirements.
sentences.translation: 所谓失控流程，是指满足特定统计条件、表现出不受控状态的流程。

sentences.source: The goal of improvement is to bring a process back within a state of statistical control.
sentences.translation: 改进目标是让流程回到统计受控状态。

sentences.source: Then, after improvements are implemented, measurements, statistics, and other Six Sigma tools are used to ensure the process remains in control.
sentences.translation: 改进实施后，组织继续使用测量、统计和其他六西格玛工具，确保流程保持受控。

sentences.source: Part of any continuous improvement process is ensuring such controls are put in place and that the employees who are hands-on with the process on a regular basis know how to use the controls.
sentences.translation: 任何持续改进流程的一部分，都是建立这些控制，并确保经常接触流程的一线员工知道如何使用这些控制。

challenges-of-six-sigma-en-001.translation: 六西格玛也有自身挑战。作为一种范围广、需要持续改进承诺的方法，六西格玛常被视为昂贵或不必要的流程，尤其对中小型组织而言更是如此。位于明尼苏达州的制造和工程公司 Ideal Aerosmith 的领导层曾对六西格玛理念及实施成本持怀疑态度。尽管有所保留，该公司仍开始实施六西格玛，并在 18 个月后看到有价值的成果，包括产量提升 25%、第一年利润提升 5%、按时交付提升 30%。

sentences.source: Six Sigma is not without its own challenges.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛也有自身挑战。

sentences.source: As an expansive method that requires commitment to continuous improvement, Six Sigma is often viewed as an expensive or unnecessary process, especially for small or mid-sized organizations.
sentences.translation: 作为一种范围广、需要持续改进承诺的方法，六西格玛常被视为昂贵或不必要的流程，尤其对中小型组织而言更是如此。

sentences.source: Leadership at Ideal Aerosmith, a manufacturing and engineering company in Minnesota, was skeptical of Six Sigma ideas and the costs associated with implementing them.
sentences.translation: 位于明尼苏达州的制造和工程公司 Ideal Aerosmith 的领导层曾对六西格玛理念及实施成本持怀疑态度。

sentences.source: Despite reservations, the company waded into Six Sigma implementations, eventually seeing worthwhile results after only 18 months.
sentences.translation: 尽管有所保留，该公司仍开始实施六西格玛，并在 18 个月后看到有价值的成果，包括产量提升 25%、第一年利润提升 5%、按时交付提升 30%。

sentences.source: Those results included a production improvement of 25 percent, a 5 percent improvement in profits within the first year, and a 30 percent improvement in timely deliverables.4
sentences.translation: 尽管有所保留，该公司仍开始实施六西格玛，并在 18 个月后看到有价值的成果，包括产量提升 25%、第一年利润提升 5%、按时交付提升 30%。

challenges-of-six-sigma-en-002.translation: 阻碍六西格玛取得积极成果的常见障碍包括：缺乏支持、资源或知识；项目执行不佳；无法持续获得有效统计数据；以及对在新行业中使用该方法的顾虑。

sentences.source: Some obstacles and challenges that often stand in the way of positive results from Six Sigma include lack of support, resources, or knowledge, poor execution of projects, inconsistent access to valid statistical data, and concerns about using the methodology in new industries.
sentences.translation: 阻碍六西格玛取得积极成果的常见障碍包括：缺乏支持、资源或知识；

lack-of-support-en-001.translation: 六西格玛需要组织各层级的支持和认同。领导者和高管必须愿意以资金和人力资源支持改进行动；主题专家应愿意向项目团队分享流程信息；各层级员工也需要接受变化和改进理念，并参与培训。常见支持障碍包括：

sentences.source: Six Sigma requires support and buy-in at all levels of an organization.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛需要组织各层级的支持和认同。

sentences.source: Leaders and executives must be willing to back initiatives with resources—financial and labor related.
sentences.translation: 领导者和高管必须愿意以资金和人力资源支持改进行动；

sentences.source: Subject-matter experts must be open to sharing information about their processes with project teams, and employees at all levels must embrace the idea of change and improvement and participate in training.
sentences.translation: 主题专家应愿意向项目团队分享流程信息；

sentences.source: Common barriers to support include:
sentences.translation: 常见支持障碍包括：

lack-of-support-en-002.translation: 领导者不熟悉或不了解六西格玛流程。

sentences.source: Leaders that are unfamiliar with or don’t understand the Six Sigma process
sentences.translation: 领导者不熟悉或不了解六西格玛流程。

lack-of-support-en-003.translation: 领导者起初愿意推动改进，但在项目完成前失去监督和倡导兴趣。

sentences.source: Leaders willing to pursue improvements initially but who lose interest in overseeing and championing projects before they are completed
sentences.translation: 领导者起初愿意推动改进，但在项目完成前失去监督和倡导兴趣。

lack-of-support-en-004.translation: 员工害怕改变，尤其是在历史上改变曾给员工带来负面后果的环境中。

sentences.source: Staff that is fearful of change, especially in an environment when change has historically caused negative consequences for employees
sentences.translation: 员工害怕改变，尤其是在历史上改变曾给员工带来负面后果的环境中。

lack-of-support-en-005.translation: 员工抵触改变，因为担心改进会让自己被替代、显著改变工作，或让工作更难。

sentences.source: Employees who are resistant to change because they believe improvements might make them obsolete, drastically change their jobs, or make their jobs harder
sentences.translation: 员工抵触改变，因为担心改进会让自己被替代、显著改变工作，或让工作更难。

lack-of-support-en-006.translation: 部门负责人或员工持续维护本部门流程和需求，不愿从整体视角思考。

sentences.source: Department heads or employees who constantly champion their own processes and needs and are unwilling to enter into big-picture thinking
sentences.translation: 部门负责人或员工持续维护本部门流程和需求，不愿从整体视角思考。

lack-of-resources-en-001.translation: 缺乏资源可能是六西格玛项目的挑战，但并不一定构成障碍。中小企业首先面临的问题之一，是缺乏使用和实施六西格玛的知识。小企业并不总能聘请专职人员处理持续流程改进，但随着培训资源和六西格玛课程更容易获得，组织越来越可以在没有专家的情况下使用部分工具，或派内部员工取得六西格玛认证。

sentences.source: Lack of resources can be a challenge to Six Sigma initiatives, but they don’t have to be a barrier.
sentences.translation: 缺乏资源可能是六西格玛项目的挑战，但并不一定构成障碍。

sentences.source: Lack of knowledge about how to use and implement Six Sigma is one of the first issues small- and mid-sized companies face.
sentences.translation: 中小企业首先面临的问题之一，是缺乏使用和实施六西格玛的知识。

sentences.source: Smaller businesses can’t always afford to hire dedicated resources to handle continuous process improvement, but the availability of resources and Six Sigma training makes it increasingly possible for organizations to use some of the tools without an expert or to send in-house staff to be certified in Six Sigma.
sentences.translation: 小企业并不总能聘请专职人员处理持续流程改进，但随着培训资源和六西格玛课程更容易获得，组织越来越可以在没有专家的情况下使用部分工具，或派内部员工取得六西格玛认证。

poor-project-execution-en-001.translation: 首次实施六西格玛的公司，尤其是在项目制环境中，如果第一个项目或改进效果不佳，往往会转而放弃整个方法。若领导层和其他相关人员仍在观望，组织内的六西格玛推动者必须让第一个项目取得足够有说服力的成果。团队可以通过谨慎、正确地执行项目每个阶段来避免绩效不佳；也可以选择低风险、高回报的改进，为首个项目创造有利条件。这种策略的不足在于，后续改进未必总能复制第一次的惊艳效果，因此长期实施和持续承诺对六西格玛至关重要。

sentences.source: Companies implementing Six Sigma for the first time, especially in a project environment, often turn away from the entire methodology if the first project or improvement falls flat.
sentences.translation: 首次实施六西格玛的公司，尤其是在项目制环境中，如果第一个项目或改进效果不佳，往往会转而放弃整个方法。

sentences.source: Proponents of Six Sigma within any organization really have to hit it out of the ballpark with the first project if leadership and others are on the fence about the methodology.
sentences.translation: 首次实施六西格玛的公司，尤其是在项目制环境中，如果第一个项目或改进效果不佳，往往会转而放弃整个方法。

sentences.source: Teams can help avoid poor project performance by taking extreme care to execute every phase of the project correctly.
sentences.translation: 团队可以通过谨慎、正确地执行项目每个阶段来避免绩效不佳；

sentences.source: By choosing low-risk, high-reward improvements, teams can also stack the deck in their favor with first-time projects.
sentences.translation: 也可以选择低风险、高回报的改进，为首个项目创造有利条件。

sentences.source: The only disadvantage with such a tactic is that it can be hard to duplicate the wow factor with subsequent improvements, making it important to remember that long-term implementation and commitment is vital in Six Sigma.
sentences.translation: 这种策略的不足在于，后续改进未必总能复制第一次的惊艳效果，因此长期实施和持续承诺对六西格玛至关重要。

data-access-issues-en-001.translation: 数据和分析问题是各种规模组织共同面对的挑战。获得一致、准确的数据流，并以适当方式对数据进行统计分析并不容易。常见数据挑战包括：

sentences.source: Data and analytics issues are a common challenge for organizations of all sizes.
sentences.translation: 数据和分析问题是各种规模组织共同面对的挑战。

sentences.source: Gaining access to consistent and accurate data streams—and applying statistical analysis to that data in an appropriate manner—is difficult.
sentences.translation: 获得一致、准确的数据流，并以适当方式对数据进行统计分析并不容易。

sentences.source: Some data-related challenges include:
sentences.translation: 常见数据挑战包括：

data-access-issues-en-002.translation: 发现重要流程指标没有被采集。

sentences.source: Discovering that an important process metric is not being captured
sentences.translation: 发现重要流程指标没有被采集。

data-access-issues-en-003.translation: 许多流程仍依赖手工数据处理。

sentences.source: The use of manual data processes in many processes
sentences.translation: 许多流程仍依赖手工数据处理。

data-access-issues-en-004.translation: 自动化数据流程捕获了海量数据，反而带来范围界定挑战。

sentences.source: Automated data processes that capture enormous amounts and create scope challenges
sentences.translation: 自动化数据流程捕获了海量数据，反而带来范围界定挑战。

data-access-issues-en-005.translation: 数据因假设、人为交互或采集错误而产生偏差。

sentences.source: Data that is skewed due to assumptions, human interaction in the process, or incorrect capture
sentences.translation: 数据因假设、人为交互或采集错误而产生偏差。

data-access-issues-en-006.translation: 从原始数据采集到可访问之间耗时过长。

sentences.source: Lengthy times between raw data capture and access
sentences.translation: 从原始数据采集到可访问之间耗时过长。

data-access-issues-en-007.translation: 行业或公司合规规则使获取必要数据变得困难。

sentences.source: Industry or company compliance rules that make it difficult to gain access to necessary data
sentences.translation: 行业或公司合规规则使获取必要数据变得困难。

industry-concerns-en-001.translation: 六西格玛起源于制造业，许多概念和工具至今仍在工厂或工业环境语境下教授。因此，组织常常低估这些方法，或认为它们很难在其他行业实施。事实上，六西格玛可以针对任何行业进行定制。

sentences.source: Six Sigma originated in the manufacturing industry and many of the concepts and tools of the methodology are still taught in the context of a factory or industrial environment.
sentences.translation: 六西格玛起源于制造业，许多概念和工具至今仍在工厂或工业环境语境下教授。

sentences.source: Because of this, organizations often discount the methods or believe they will be too difficult to implement in other industries.
sentences.translation: 因此，组织常常低估这些方法，或认为它们很难在其他行业实施。

sentences.source: In reality, Six Sigma can be customized to any industry.
sentences.translation: 事实上，六西格玛可以针对任何行业进行定制。
